renders_to: Rendered by docs/board/render-board.mjs into docs/board/rc-board-phase2.rendered.html, a gitignored build product that is generated and never hand-edited. That HTML is published as a claude.ai artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/92e2da75-961c-4ce3-a765-9e00686c6bb2, and the same URL is re-rendered and updated after every board change so the owner link stays live. This JSON remains the single source of truth: the render is strictly downstream of it and never writes back. The phase 1 board and its artifact are untouched and stay live at their own URL.
doctrine: A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof, and the acceptance field carries the check that produced it. The executor terminal updates this JSON at every checkpoint, in the same PR as the code, and bumps as_of. docs/board/validate-board.mjs must exit 0 before every commit; a commit made while the validator is red is reverted, not patched forward. GATE VOCABULARY, amended 2026-08-25 by owner ruling R-002. OWNER_MERGE IS RETIRED ON THIS BOARD. Cards ship on green_self_merge discipline: the green quality check PLUS the card's named acceptance spec passing. Visual and behavioural defect review belongs to the CRITIC at wave boundaries and to an optional owner batch review before the client demo; NEITHER IS A MERGE GATE. green_self_merge means the executor self-decides and merges its own PR once quality is green and the named acceptance has passed, no approval needed. stakeholder means Mihai (the client) accepts on production, and P2-14 is the only card that carries it. cyan_clear, owner_authorizo and owner_merge are unused on this board; owner_merge remains a legal value only because the closed phase 1 board carries it on nine shipped cards. A blocked_on entry naming Ivan is an OWNER ACTION (apply a DNS record, rotate a credential, tick a checklist), never a review, and retiring owner_merge does not touch it. LAUNCH GATE CONDITIONS still flip to pass only on their named proof: for screen conditions that proof is now the named spec green in CI plus EXECUTOR's own deployed-screen verification, both recorded as evidence. EVIDENCE VOCABULARY: kind pr is a merged pull request number, kind journal is a commit sha or command output pasted so a stranger can re-verify, kind e2e is a named Playwright test plus the run that passed it, kind screenshot is Ivan or Mihai on-screen confirmation. SKIP-NOT-HALT: the run never stops for a question. A card that cannot proceed gets its question field filled with the structured decision-needed text (DECISION NEEDED, CONTEXT, OPTIONS, RECOMMENDATION, IMPACT IF UNANSWERED), blocked_on set to the person who owes the answer, status set to blocked, and the executor moves to the next eligible card in the same session. A recommendation is mandatory: a question without one is unfinished. DEFAULTS: every card carries a defaults field holding the pre-authorized answers to that card's expected ambiguities. When defaults covers an ambiguity the executor applies it and logs the application in notes, and does not ask. Defaults fill silence, they never override an explicit instruction in the card. ACCEPTANCE: every card names a machine-checkable acceptance line, a command with an expected exit code, a URL with expected content, or a named test. No acceptance, no ship. A card whose acceptance cannot be run yet is blocked, never shipped. MIGRATIONS: authored as supabase/migrations/NNNN_name.sql files, listed in the PR description by path, and applied by Ivan alone in the Supabase SQL editor. No terminal in this repo ever connects to a database. A card whose acceptance needs an APPLIED migration is set blocked_on ivan with the apply request written into question. A migration file is never edited after it has been applied; a correction is a new numbered file. SECRETS: environment variable names only. Values never appear in chat, in this board, in a commit, in a log or in tool output. /Users/ivan/rc-secrets is out of bounds for reads. ELIGIBILITY: a card is eligible when status is todo, every id in depends_on belongs to a shipped card, and blocked_on is null. The executor takes the lowest-id eligible card. The full standing rules are in CLAUDE.md at the repo root.

THE DECIDING CLAUSE CHANGES. It is no longer "one real document has travelled the whole path on production". It is: THE INGEST ENDPOINT ASSERTED AGAINST A FIXTURE DOCUMENT, PLUS ITS FOUR NAMED FAILURE CASES, redirect, malformed payload, oversize and auth rejection.

THE RATIONALE IS A PROPERTY OF MACHINE ENDPOINTS AND NOT AN ACCOMMODATION. An endpoint sitting behind a redirect RETURNS 200 WHILE DOING NOTHING. The caller sees success, the payload goes to the redirect target or nowhere, and every happy-path test passes. So the happy path was never the thing worth gating on: it is the case least able to tell a working endpoint from a broken one. The four failure cases are what prove the endpoint exists, is reachable without a redirect, validates what it receives, bounds what it accepts, and refuses what is not authenticated.

THIS IS A STRICTLY STRONGER GATE. One real document through a live scenario proves one document worked once, on a day, through a third party's configuration. It is not re-runnable, it is not a check, and it cannot fail in CI. A fixture plus four failure assertions runs on every push, for ever.

WHAT IT REMOVES IS A DEPENDENCY ON A PERSON, NOT A STANDARD. This gate has been fail since the board opened and every audit recorded the same cause: it waits on Andre. R-046 said plainly that no terminal could close it and no card existed that moved it. ANDRE'S LIVE SCENARIO IS DEGATED, NOT CANCELLED. It becomes a non-gating card landing whenever his result arrives. The round trip is still the thing that proves the integration with the real counterparty; it simply stops holding a launch condition hostage.

IT DOES NOT FLIP HERE. Gates flip on committed evidence only, under R-023, and the assertions do not exist yet. What changed today is that a terminal can now author them.

R-074's conclusion, that this gate stays fail, is correct and is confirmed here on better evidence. Its premise is not, and a ruling is never edited, so the correction is R-080.
THE CLAUSES ARE MEASURED AGAINST THE TREE THIS TIME, NOT AGAINST THE CARDS. AUTH REJECTION: GREEN. Case 4, `secret gresit sau lipsa este 401 si nu scrie nimic`.

conditions.title: G7: Reminders fire a Resend email when stock crosses a product threshold
conditions.plain: A warning email actually arrives when a product falls below the level set for it.
conditions.notes:
Closes when P2-10 has landed and one real email has been delivered from a real threshold crossing on production. The mocked test proves the logic; this gate needs the live send, which needs RESEND_API_KEY in the production environment. BLOCKED ON IVAN AS OF 2026-08-26, WITH A SECOND PRECONDITION THE ORIGINAL TEXT DID NOT KNOW ABOUT. P2-10 shipped on 2026-08-26 and its logic is proven by tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts, four cases green in the quality run for PR #21. Two things stand between that and one real delivered email. FIRST, RESEND_API_KEY must exist in the production environment, which is what this condition already said. SECOND, migration 0006 (supabase/migrations/0006_reminder_recipients.sql) must be applied to the RC project. It adds owner_reminder_recipients(), SECURITY DEFINER, which is how the reminder learns who to write to: profiles_select is (id = auth.uid()) OR is_owner(), so an account_manager cannot read the owner profile row, and an account_manager issuing material is the main way a threshold gets crossed. The migration contains no DROP, no TRUNCATE and no DELETE, and CI proves the file on every run because supabase db reset replays it before the suite. THE APPLY COULD NOT BE PERFORMED BY THE EXECUTOR: the harness classifier denied the permitted secrets read from /Users/ivan/rc-secrets/phase2.env, so no connection was attempted, no hostname was guessed, and nothing was tried on a credential that was not derived as CLAUDE.md 8.4 requires. Until it is applied, a threshold crossing on production writes the reason onto the reminder row and shows it on /memento as Netrimis; the stock movement itself is unaffected, which is the designed degradation and not a new defect. CORRECTED 2026-08-26, SAME DAY, BEFORE THIS PR MERGED. MIGRATION 0006 IS APPLIED. The paragraph above says it was not, and that was true when it was written and false a few hours later. It is corrected here rather than rewritten, so the record shows what was believed and when. Under ruling R-007 the executor was granted the secrets read, connected on the eu-west-1 session pooler, proved connectivity with SELECT 1, and found in the PRE-CHECK that the work was already done: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations already carried version 0006, name reminder_recipients, 8 statements. The migration was NOT re-applied. It was verified read-only instead, with default_transaction_read_only on: the function exists with prosecdef true and search_path pinned to public, pg_temp, it returns SETOF text, its ACL is postgres, authenticated and service_role only with no PUBLIC and no anon entry, and it returns exactly one recipient. Corroboration that 0006 added exactly one object and nothing else: the public function count is 9 against the CRITIC wave 1 baseline of 8, and the new name is owner_reminder_recipients. No drift anywhere else: 11 tables all with RLS enabled and non-zero policy counts, 41 policies in public plus 3 on storage.objects for the rc-docs bucket, which reproduces the CRITIC baseline of 44 exactly, and 6 enums with identical labels in identical order. Journal ordering is forward: 0006 is the maximum version and exactly one row sorts after 0005. WHO APPLIED IT IS NOT RECORDED: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations carries version, name and statements, and no timestamp and no actor column, so the table cannot say when or by whom. It was not this terminal. WHAT G7 STILL NEEDS, AND IT IS NOT THIS: RESEND_API_KEY present in the PRODUCTION Vercel environment, and one real delivered email from a real crossing. There is a third thing, found while verifying and not previously written anywhere: owner_reminder_recipients() returns exactly one address and it is on the domain rc-inventory.local, which is the seeded DEV owner account and a domain that does not exist. A crossing on production today would address the email to nobody. The real client accounts are created at P2-13, which is where that closes.

cards.title: Schema migration 0001 authored: every phase 2 table, the owner|account_manager role enum, and RLS on every table.
cards.plain: The stock, orders and suppliers now have a real permanent home instead of a demo one, with separate permissions for the owner and for the person doing daily entry. Nobody can reach data they are not meant to see.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `test -f supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql && npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. The file must exist at that exact path and the repository must still typecheck clean.
cards.defaults: UNITS: the unit enum is the phase 1 mock set, m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3, and nothing else. The stored enum values are those English tokens; the Romanian display labels the phase 1 UI already uses (m2, lm, buc, sac, kg, rola, m3) stay in the presentation layer as a lookup, because UI copy is Romanian and stored enum values are not UI copy. CURRENCY: the currency enum is EUR, RON, MDL. No FX rates and no runtime conversion; a stored total in a stored currency, exactly as phase 1 did it. NAMING: snake_case for every table, column, enum, index and constraint. Tables plural, columns singular, foreign keys named <referenced_table_singular>_id, timestamps created_at and updated_at, primary keys uuid with gen_random_uuid(). SHAPES: when a column is ambiguous, mirror the phase 1 mock data shapes in lib/mock/types.ts field for field rather than inventing a better model. The phase 1 screens are the specification and they already read those shapes. MONEY: numeric(14,2), never float. QUANTITIES: numeric(14,3), because m2 and m3 are fractional. SOFT DELETE: every catalog-like table carries active boolean not null default true. RLS: deny by default, then grant. Read policies are to authenticated only; write policies are role-checked against profiles.role. If a table's write rule is not obvious, owner writes and account_manager reads, and log that choice in notes.

evidence.ref: commit fae808823d8725ecdfd807e1d9a1fde8f0d2bde4, PR #3. MIGRATION 0001 APPLY JOURNAL, three phases per CLAUDE.md 8.5, run 2026-08-25 under ruling R-001. CONNECTION (8.4): project ref derived from NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, length 20, never printed. Session pooler eu-west-1, port 5432, user postgres.<ref>, password via PGPASSWORD so it never enters a connection string. Host aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com resolved and accepted TCP but rejected the tenant: 'psql: error: connection to server at aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com (108.128.216.176), port 5432 failed: FATAL: (ENOTFOUND) tenant/user postgres.<ref> not found'. Retried on aws-1-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com: SELECT 1 returned 1, psql exit 0. Connectivity proven before any migration work. DESTRUCTIVE GATE (8.6): 0 DROP TABLE, 0 TRUNCATE, 0 DELETE FROM, 0 DROP SCHEMA, 0 DROP DATABASE. Near-misses correctly excluded: 14 'on delete <action>' foreign key clauses and 9 'for delete' policy targets, neither of which deletes a row. GATE PASS. PHASE 1 PRE-CHECK: 1 pending file, 0001_phase2_schema.sql, 652 lines. File claims 11 create table, 6 create type as enum, 3 create function, 11 enable row level security, 41 create policy, 13 create index, 7 create trigger. DATABASE STATE BEFORE APPLY: 11 tables, 6 enums, 41 policies. THE PRE-CHECK CAUGHT THAT THE MIGRATION WAS ALREADY APPLIED, by Ivan, between the wave 1 report and this run. PHASE 2 APPLY: attempted anyway rather than assumed away. psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f, the file's own BEGIN/COMMIT. Result: 'BEGIN' then 'psql:supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql:46: ERROR: type "app_role" already exists', psql exit 3. The transaction rolled back whole and nothing was left behind, which is exactly the behaviour the single-transaction wrapper exists to produce. THIS TERMINAL DID NOT APPLY 0001. IVAN DID. PHASE 3 POST-CHECK, run against the live schema: TABLES 11, every one rls=true, every one with a non-zero policy count, 41 policies total, 0 tables with RLS disabled, 0 tables with zero policies. Per table: batches 4, categories 4, inbound_orders 4, order_lines 4, outbound_issues 4, outbound_lines 4, products 3, profiles 4, reminders 4, status_history 2, units 4. Products has 3 because it carries no delete policy by design, and status_history has 2 because it is append only. ENUMS 6: app_role [owner, account_manager]; currency_code [EUR, RON, MDL]; inbound_status [pending_arrival, arrived]; outbound_status [awaiting_shipment, shipped]; status_entity [inbound_order, outbound_issue]; unit_code [m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3]. FUNCTIONS 3: current_app_role security_definer=true, is_owner security_definer=true, set_updated_at security_definer=false. The two definer functions are what keep the profiles policies from recursing. SEEDED REFERENCE DATA: units 7 rows in sort order m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3. ZERO REAL CLIENT DATA, which is the standing condition of the R-001 grant: products 0, categories 0, profiles 0 at post-check time. INDEXES 30 (13 explicit plus primary key and unique constraint indexes), ROW TRIGGERS 7. FILE VS DATABASE TABLE DIFF: IDENTICAL, every table named in the file exists in the database and nothing else does. CONCLUSION: 0001 is applied and the live schema matches the committed file exactly. Acceptance for this card (file exists, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0) was already green at ship time; this journal adds the applied-state proof the card was blocked for.

cards.notes:
The foundation card. Authors ONE SQL file and nothing else: no client, no queries, no screens. Tables: products, categories, units, inbound_orders, order_lines, batches, outbound_issues, outbound_lines, status_history, reminders, profiles. profiles carries the role enum with exactly two values, owner and account_manager, and is keyed on the Supabase auth.users id. RLS is ENABLED on every one of those tables, with authenticated-only read policies and role-checked write policies. A table without RLS enabled is the defect this card exists to prevent, so the file ends with an explicit ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY line per table, grouped and commented, so a reader can count them against the table list. Stock is NOT a column. Stock is the sum of a product's batches, per the P2-04 default, so no products.stock column is created here. NO TERMINAL CONNECTS TO A DATABASE. This card produces a file. EXIT STATE, DISCHARGED 2026-08-25: this card originally ended blocked_on ivan with a SQL editor apply request in question. Ruling R-001 delegated the apply to EXECUTOR, Ivan applied 0001 himself before the ruling landed, and the applied state is now proven in evidence by a full three-phase journal. blocked_on and question are cleared. THE CARD IS FULLY CLOSED.

--- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-25 (card shipped) ---
Delivered: supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql, one transaction, 108 statements. Eleven tables exactly as listed above, six enum types, three functions, 41 policies, 13 indexes, seven updated_at triggers, and eleven ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY lines, one per table. Acceptance ran green: file present, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0.

DEFAULTS APPLIED (CLAUDE.md section 5, logged rather than asked):
1. UNITS. The unit enum stores the English tokens m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3. Phase 1's lib/mock/types.ts stores the Romanian tokens (buc, sac, rola) directly; the card default says stored enum values are not UI copy, so the English tokens win and the Romanian labels become a presentation-layer lookup. Extended by the same reasoning to inbound_status (pending_arrival, arrived) and outbound_status (awaiting_shipment, shipped), whose phase 1 values are the Romanian display strings.
2. CURRENCY. EUR, RON, MDL per the default. Phase 1's Currency type carried only EUR and RON with a separately stored totalMdl; the card's three-value enum wins and total_mdl stays as a stored column, with no FX and no runtime conversion.
3. SEEDING. units is seeded with all seven rows, because the set is fixed by the enum and an empty units table would leave the product form with nothing to pick. categories is NOT seeded: phase 2 starts with an empty database and no migration from any old system, and phase 1's seven categories were mock data invented for a demo.
4. WRITE RULES. The card default says to fall back to owner-writes when a table's rule is not obvious. Applied to the catalog half: profiles, categories, units and products are owner-write, which is also P2-03's stated rule. NOT applied to the operational half, because that case is not doubtful: inbound_orders, order_lines, batches, outbound_issues, outbound_lines, status_history and reminders are writable by both roles, since P2-04, P2-05 and P2-14 all describe an operator running the daily cycle and P2-02 names exactly one thing the account_manager is refused, which is settings. DELETE on the operational tables stays owner-only. This is the one place the default was deliberately not applied, and it is the first thing to overturn if Ivan disagrees.

JUDGMENT CALLS, all reversible by a later numbered migration:
5. NO SUPPLIERS TABLE. The card's table list is explicit and carries no suppliers table, and adding an unlisted table is scope. Supplier is stored as supplier_name text on products and on inbound_orders, which is what every phase 1 screen that touches a supplier actually reads: a name to display and to filter by. Promoting it to a table is a straightforward migration if the client needs supplier records of their own.
6. THREE COLUMNS ADDED FOR DOWNSTREAM CARDS, all nullable or defaulted, all inside tables the card lists: inbound_orders.document_path and inbound_orders.document_uploaded_at for P2-04's upload, and products.needs_review for P2-09's unmatched-name flag. Each would otherwise force a second migration and a second apply round trip through Ivan.
7. batches.order_line_id CARRIES A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT, which is what makes P2-04's idempotent arrival enforceable by the database rather than by whichever code path happens to run.
8. status_history HAS NO UPDATE AND NO DELETE POLICY, for any role including owner. RLS denies what no policy allows, so append-only is enforced rather than remembered.
9. products HAS NO DELETE POLICY AT ALL, matching P2-03's soft-delete-only default, and the on delete restrict foreign keys back it up.
10. NO STOCK VIEW. Stock is the sum of batches, but the computing view belongs to P2-04, which owns the stock rules. This card creates tables, per its own notes.
11. NO CREATE EXTENSION LINE. gen_random_uuid() has been core since PostgreSQL 13 and every Supabase project runs 15 or later, so a pgcrypto line would add a failure mode for nothing.

VERIFICATION LIMIT, stated plainly: the SQL was never executed. CLAUDE.md section 8 forbids any terminal in this repo from connecting to a database, and there is no local PostgreSQL on this machine. The file was checked by a structural linter that parses the text and executes nothing (scratchpad/lint-migration.mjs, uncommitted): 0 problems, and it confirms eleven tables against eleven RLS lines with every policy, index, trigger and foreign key resolving to a table created in the same file. It cannot catch a syntax error. That is why the file is wrapped in one transaction: a failed apply rolls back whole and costs a round trip, never a partial schema.

--- APPLY VERIFICATION 2026-08-25 (ruling R-001) ---
The apply was verified, not performed, and the difference is recorded rather than smoothed over. The phase 1 pre-check found 11 tables, 6 enums and 41 policies already present. The apply was attempted anyway and failed on 'type app_role already exists', rolling back whole. The phase 3 post-check then confirmed the live schema matches the committed file exactly: 11 tables all with RLS enabled and non-zero policy counts, 6 enums with the exact labels the file declares, both role helpers security_definer, units seeded with 7 rows, and an IDENTICAL table-name diff between file and database. Full journal in evidence.ref.

cards.title: Supabase Auth wired: Romanian email and password login, middleware protecting every route, profiles.role read into the session, account_manager refused at settings.
cards.plain: Staff sign in with an email and a password, in Romanian, and the system knows who each person is. The daily operator can do their work but cannot open the owner settings.
cards.acceptance: COMMANDS: `npm run build` exits 0, and `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits 0 locally. auth.spec covers: login with the owner account succeeds; login with a wrong password shows the Romanian error; an unauthenticated request to a protected route redirects to login; the account_manager account is refused at the settings route.
cards.defaults: NO SIGNUP PAGE. Accounts are created by Ivan in the Supabase dashboard and the corresponding profiles row is inserted by hand. A public signup route on an internal warehouse tool is a way in for strangers, not a feature. There is no password reset screen either in this card; Ivan resets from the dashboard. SESSION: use the supabase-js ssr package defaults for cookie handling and refresh. Do not hand-roll refresh timing, do not store tokens in localStorage, do not lengthen the default session lifetime. ROUTE PROTECTION: middleware denies by default and allows an explicit list (the login route, static assets, the auth callback). A new route is protected because it is new, not because someone remembered to add it. ROLE READ: profiles.role is read once per request in middleware and passed down; do not re-query it in every component. UNAUTHENTICATED: redirect to the login route, never render a shell with empty data. AUTHENTICATED BUT WRONG ROLE: a Romanian 403 screen, not a redirect loop and not a silent blank. COPY: all login copy Romanian with diacritics, including the Supabase error strings, which are English by default and must be mapped.

evidence.ref: auth.spec, 10 of 10 passed on chromium in 17.7s, run locally 2026-08-25. Tests: unauthenticated request to a protected route redirects to login; every protected route redirects (/inventar, /comenzi, /iesiri, /setari, /memento), not just the root; a wrong password shows the Romanian error 'Email sau parola incorecta.' and leaks no English; an unknown email returns the IDENTICAL message so the screen cannot be used to enumerate accounts; the owner account signs in and the topbar reads 'Administrator'; the owner can open /setari; the account_manager signs in and the topbar reads 'Operator'; the account_manager is refused at /setari with the Romanian 403 screen while the URL stays /setari, proving a rewrite and not a redirect loop; signing out restores the default deny; an authenticated user cannot sit on the login screen. Also green: npm run build exit 0, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0. Commit 8a80e5e92d9212157454dbe6c8a1badfe20f00d2.

cards.notes:
Everything after this card assumes a signed-in user with a known role, so it comes before any real screen. Two accounts exist for the whole phase: one owner, one account_manager, both created by Ivan. This card needs migration 0001 APPLIED, because profiles and the role enum must exist before auth can read a role. If the migration is not applied when this card is picked up, the executor sets status blocked, blocked_on ivan, fills question with the apply request per the doctrine, and moves on. That is the migration rule working, not a stall. Closes gate G1 once two accounts exist on production and the account_manager is visibly refused at settings. Deliberately not done: password reset UI, magic links, OAuth, MFA, invite flows.

--- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-25 (card blocked, no code written) ---
Picked up as the lowest-id eligible card the moment P2-01 shipped, and blocked before any code was written, which is what this card's own notes prescribe for an unapplied migration.

WHAT WAS CHECKED, so the block is a finding and not an assumption:
- Migration 0001: merged in PR #3 and definitionally unapplied. The apply request was raised on P2-01 in the same hour and no terminal here may connect to a database to confirm it, so this one is asserted from the audit trail rather than from the database.
- .env.local: does not exist. Checked by listing .env* in the repository root, which matched nothing. No Supabase URL or anon key is reachable from this machine without reading /Users/ivan/rc-secrets/phase2.env, which CLAUDE.md section 7 puts out of bounds.
- @supabase/supabase-js, @supabase/ssr: not in package.json.
- @playwright/test: not in package.json and not in node_modules/.bin. The tests/ directory does not exist, so no acceptance line on this board can run yet.

WHY NO CODE WAS WRITTEN ANYWAY. Half the acceptance (npm run build) could have been reached by building the login screen and the middleware blind, leaving only the Playwright half outstanding. That was rejected. Route protection that nobody has executed is the worst possible thing to merge onto main, because every screen delivered after this card sits behind it, and a wrong middleware would be inherited silently by P2-03 through P2-14. CLAUDE.md section 6 is explicit that a card whose acceptance cannot run is blocked rather than shipped, and section 5 says a card's own instruction outranks a default: these notes said to block and move on.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RUN: with P2-02 blocked, nothing on this board is eligible. P2-03, P2-04, P2-05, P2-06 and P2-07 all depend transitively on P2-02 being shipped, and P2-08 onward is outside the wave 1 ceiling. The session ends here with one card shipped and one card blocked, which is the migration rule working rather than a stall.

--- UNBLOCKED 2026-08-25 BY RULING R-001 ---
All three blockers are cleared, and each was cleared by an action recorded elsewhere rather than by assertion:
1. MIGRATION 0001 IS APPLIED. Ivan applied it; EXECUTOR verified it with the three-phase journal now carried in P2-01 evidence. 11 tables, all RLS enabled, all with non-zero policy counts, 6 enums, table diff against the committed file IDENTICAL.
2. THE TWO ACCOUNTS EXIST. Created by EXECUTOR through the Supabase auth admin API with email confirmation bypassed, and their profiles rows inserted with roles set explicitly. Verified by selecting id and role only: 326a7899-5f84-4c75-858d-48385f963edf owner, 5d95288b-4b83-4d1d-8620-a6f70730efed account_manager. profiles row count 2. These are DEV accounts on a database holding zero real client data; real client accounts are created at P2-13, which also retires these.
3. .env.local EXISTS. Written by EXECUTOR, mode 600, confirmed gitignored by git check-ignore before it was written. Carries NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, TEST_OWNER_EMAIL, TEST_OWNER_PASSWORD, TEST_MANAGER_EMAIL and TEST_MANAGER_PASSWORD. No value was printed at any point.

DEFECT FOUND AND CORRECTED WHILE UNBLOCKING, worth knowing before anyone copies from the secrets file again: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL in phase2.env is NOT the bare project origin. It carries a '/rest/v1/' suffix, 49 characters total against the 40 a bare origin would be. Copied verbatim it produces '<origin>/rest/v1/auth/v1/admin/users', which the auth API rejects with 'Invalid path specified in request URL', and it would break supabase-js in every card after this one. .env.local was written with the normalised origin 'https://<ref>.supabase.co' derived from the same variable, not with the raw value. The Vercel environment should be checked for the same defect before P2-12.

--- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-25 (card shipped) ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged rather than asked:
1. NO SIGNUP PAGE and no password reset screen. The only way in is a login form. Accounts come from the Supabase dashboard, and under R-001 EXECUTOR created the two dev accounts through the admin API.
2. SESSION via @supabase/ssr defaults. No hand-rolled refresh timing, no token in localStorage, no lengthened lifetime. getUser() is used rather than getSession() everywhere a decision depends on identity, because getSession only reads the cookie, which is client-supplied data.
3. ROUTE PROTECTION IS DENY BY DEFAULT. proxy.ts holds an ALLOW list of one path plus the auth callback prefix; everything else needs a session. A route added tomorrow is protected because it is new. The matcher excludes only static assets and optimised images.
4. ROLE READ ONCE PER REQUEST in the proxy and passed down as the x-rc-role header. No component re-queries profiles.
5. UNAUTHENTICATED REDIRECTS to the login route and never renders a shell with empty data. This is why the app shell moved into the (app) route group: the root layout is now html, body and styles only, so the login screen cannot inherit a sidebar and topbar full of zeroes.
6. WRONG ROLE gets a Romanian 403 screen delivered by REWRITE, so the URL stays on the requested path and no redirect loop is possible. A redirect to a /403 route would have been easier to assert and worse to use.
7. ALL COPY ROMANIAN, including Supabase's English error strings, which are mapped in lib/supabase/auth-errors.ts. An unknown email and a wrong password return the SAME message on purpose: a login screen that distinguishes them tells a stranger which addresses are registered.

BEYOND THE STATED DEFAULTS, three decisions worth naming:
8. A SIGN-OUT CONTROL was added to the topbar. It is not in the card text, but without it the only way to change accounts is deleting cookies by hand, and the account_manager refusal test would need a second browser profile. It is four lines and it makes the acceptance runnable.
9. THE APP LAYOUT RE-CHECKS THE SESSION even though the proxy already refused unauthenticated requests. Defence in depth: a layout that assumes its user renders empty data the day a matcher is edited wrong.
10. A PROFILE ROW THAT IS MISSING OR INACTIVE MEANS NO ACCESS, not a default role. An authenticated user without an active profile row is redirected to login rather than treated as an account_manager.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, all appended to docs/LEARNINGS.md. The first two each presented as 'login silently does nothing' with no console error and no failed assertion on page content, which is why they are written up in full:
- process.env[name] with a computed key is never inlined into a client bundle by Next, so the browser threw inside createClient before issuing any request. Fixed by reading both variables through fully literal member access at module scope.
- Next 16 blocks cross-origin requests to /_next dev resources. Playwright asked for localhost as 127.0.0.1, every JS chunk returned 403, React never hydrated, and the form had no handlers while looking perfectly correct. Fixed by pointing the harness at localhost rather than adding allowedDevOrigins to the application config.
- the middleware file convention is deprecated in Next 16; renamed to proxy.ts on day one.

GATE: green_self_merge, per ruling R-002. Shipped on green quality plus auth.spec passing, which is the two-part discipline that ruling defines.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, as the card says: password reset UI, magic links, OAuth, MFA, invite flows.

cards.title: Inbound real: manual order entry, document upload to the private rc-docs bucket, Pending arrival and Arrived, arrival creating batches and moving stock, status_history on every change.
cards.plain: Incoming deliveries are real: the office types an order in or uploads the supplier document, and marking it arrived genuinely raises the stock. Every change is recorded, so it is always clear who did what and when.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/inbound.spec.ts` exits 0. inbound.spec covers: a manually entered order persists with its lines; a document uploads and is retrievable only through a signed URL; marking an order Arrived creates one batch per line and raises the computed stock by exactly the arrived quantities; a second Arrived click creates no extra batch; every transition wrote a status_history row.
cards.defaults: STOCK IS A COMPUTED BATCH SUM. There is no denormalised stock counter anywhere, in any table, at any point. Current stock is the sum of that product's batch quantities minus what outbound has issued, computed in a view or a query, never cached in a column. A counter and a sum disagree eventually, and when they do the warehouse trusts the wrong one. If performance ever demands a cache, that is a new card with its own reconciliation check, not a quiet column added here. PARTIAL ARRIVALS ARE OUT OF SCOPE. Whole-order statuses only, as in phase 1. If the client asks for partial arrivals during this card, log the request as a new card in REVIEW BATCH (IVAN) and keep building whole-order. BUCKET: rc-docs, PRIVATE. Never public, never a public URL. Documents are reached through a short-lived signed URL generated server side. Path convention inbound/<order_id>/<original_filename>. ACCEPTED FILES: pdf, png, jpg. Max 10 MB. Anything else is refused in Romanian before upload starts. ARRIVAL IS IDEMPOTENT: marking an already-Arrived order Arrived again creates no second batch. STATUS HISTORY: every transition writes a row carrying the order, the from-status, the to-status, the acting user id and the timestamp. A status that changes without a history row is a defect. STATUS LABELS stay the phase 1 Romanian strings, In asteptare and Receptionata, spelled with their proper diacritics in the code.

evidence.ref: inbound.spec, 7 of 7 passed on chromium; full suite 25 of 25, run TWICE end to end, 2026-08-25. Tests: a manually entered order persists with its lines across a full reload and its reference matches INT-YYYY-NNNN; a pending order does NOT move stock; receiving creates one batch per line and raises computed stock by exactly 40; a second receive click reports 'era deja receptionata', leaves the batch count at 1 and the stock unchanged; creation writes the first status_history row and receipt writes the second; a document uploads to the private bucket and is readable only through a signed URL under /storage/v1/object/sign/rc-docs/ with a token, while the same path without a signature does not return the file; an order with no lines is refused in Romanian; a text file is refused before upload starts. Also green: npm run build exit 0, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0. MIGRATIONS APPLIED under R-001 with the three-phase journal: 0002_rc_docs_bucket.sql (pre-check 11 tables / 6 enums / 41 policies; apply BEGIN, INSERT 0 1, three CREATE POLICY, COMMIT; post-check bucket rc-docs public=f, file_size_limit 10485760, mime types {application/pdf,image/png,image/jpeg}, policies rc_docs_insert/select/update all {authenticated}); 0003_inbound_functions.sql (apply BEGIN, two CREATE FUNCTION, two COMMENT, two GRANT, COMMIT; post-check create_inbound_order and receive_inbound_order both security_definer=false, invoker on purpose). Destructive gate PASS on both files, 0 hits. Commit 2536ead924325dbe521f18bb9ef408df19286ac3.

The inbound half of the real system, and the card the AI pipeline later feeds into, which is why P2-08 depends on it: the extraction has to have something real to create. Two ways in, both real: an order typed by hand, and an order carrying an uploaded document. The upload here stores the file and nothing more; no extraction, no webhook, no Make. That is P2-08. DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged rather than asked:
1. STOCK IS A COMPUTED BATCH SUM. No counter column was added, anywhere. Receiving inserts batches and the inventory screen re-reads the sum. The spec proves the arithmetic: stock 0 before, still 0 while pending, exactly 40 after receiving 40.
2. PARTIAL ARRIVALS OUT OF SCOPE. Whole-order statuses only, and the screen says so.
3. BUCKET rc-docs, PRIVATE, path inbound/<order_id>/<filename>. The filename is sanitised because an operator's filename can carry spaces, diacritics and slashes, and a slash would move the object into a different folder. Never a public URL; reading is a server-generated signed URL, 15 minutes.
4. ACCEPTED FILES pdf, png, jpg, max 10 MB, refused in Romanian BEFORE the upload starts. The check exists in three places on purpose: the browser (so the operator is told immediately), the server action (because a browser check is a courtesy), and the bucket constraint in 0002 (because that is the one nothing can bypass).
5. ARRIVAL IS IDEMPOTENT, with two locks rather than one. SELECT FOR UPDATE serialises two callers; the unique constraint on batches.order_line_id catches anything that gets past it.
6. STATUS HISTORY ON EVERY TRANSITION, creation included. An order whose history starts at its second status cannot be audited back to its creation.
7. STATUS LABELS are the phase 1 Romanian strings with their diacritics, mapped from the English enum tokens.

DECISIONS WORTH NAMING:
8. TWO DATABASE FUNCTIONS INSTEAD OF APPLICATION CODE (migration 0003). Creating an order is three writes and receiving one is three more; over PostgREST each is its own transaction, so a failure between two of them leaves a state the application believes impossible. Both are SECURITY INVOKER: they bundle work into one transaction and grant nobody new rights.
9. NO DELETE POLICY ON THE BUCKET, for any role. A document is the evidence behind an order; an order that says a document arrived, pointing at an object that no longer exists, is worse than either fact alone.
10. DELIBERATE INTERMEDIATE STATE: inbound is real, outbound still reads the mock layer, and the orders screen carries a visible label saying so. The outbound panel was moved to OutboundPanelMock.tsx precisely so its deletion at P2-06 is obvious rather than archaeological.
11. THE ORDER REFERENCE is computed from the highest existing one for the year. Two operators creating an order in the same second can collide, and the unique constraint refuses the second with a Romanian message. A database sequence would be better and is a separate card, not a column slipped in here.

FIVE DEFECTS FOUND, all in docs/LEARNINGS.md. Three of them are Next.js boundary rules that build clean until they do not: a "use server" file may export only async functions (and the knock-on error names a function that is plainly there); server-only breaks on a value import but not a type import; window.open called after an await opens a tab that never navigates, now replaced by a real anchor that is also keyboard and middle-click friendly. Two are test-harness truths: an empty tbody is invisible to Playwright, and a test that passed alone and failed in the suite was a cold-compile crossing the default expect timeout, now an explicit threshold with the reason written beside it rather than a retry. The suite was run twice end to end to confirm.

AVAILABLE STOCK is read at submit time inside the same transaction as the write, so two simultaneous issues cannot both pass a stale check. --- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-26 (card shipped) ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged rather than asked:
1. OVERDRAW IS BLOCKED, NOT WARNED, and the placement is the whole design. The check exists in three layers: the form (so the operator is told immediately), the server action (because a browser check is a courtesy), and create_outbound_issue under an advisory transaction lock (which is the only one that survives two operators issuing the last 40 m2 at the same instant). The lock is taken BEFORE the stock is read, so the value cannot change between the read and the insert, and locks are acquired in sorted product order so two transactions touching the same products queue instead of deadlocking.
2. QUANTITIES ARE SUMMED PER PRODUCT before the check. Splitting 100 into two lines of 50 must not pass a check that 50 would fail; the operator's line layout is not a way around the stock. Proven by its own test.
3. COMBOBOX REUSED, not rebuilt: same component, same portal rendering, same diacritics-insensitive filtering. See the deviation below.
4. UNIT taken from the product, not editable on the line. SALE PRICE optional, blank renders as the phase 1 'fara pret' string. ISSUE-TO-PROJECT with client and project names. PARTIAL SHIPMENTS out of scope. STATUS LABELS are the phase 1 Romanian strings.

DECISIONS WORTH NAMING:
5. ERROR MESSAGES ARE MACHINE READABLE IN SQL AND ROMANIAN IN THE APP. The function raises INSUFFICIENT_STOCK|<product_id>|<available>|<unit>; the action composes the Romanian sentence with the proper unit label. Interface copy does not belong in the schema, for the same reason enum values are English tokens.
6. SHIPPING DOES NOT MOVE STOCK. Stock left the warehouse when the issue was created, which is why the overdraw check lives there and not at shipping. The panel says this on screen so nobody expects a second decrement.
7. product_available_stock IS THE SINGLE DEFINITION of how much is there, used by both the inventory screen and the overdraw check, so the number shown and the number enforced cannot drift.
8. THE MOCK OUTBOUND PANEL IS DELETED and the orders screen now reads both directions from the database. lib/mock survives only for the dashboard and the upload screen, which P2-06 and P2-09 own.

Invisible with fixed mock data because nobody ever typed an existing name; immediate with real repeated data. A field that erases itself after being filled correctly is the worst kind of defect, because the operator concludes they made the mistake. Shipping that to avoid touching a phase 1 file would have been the wrong trade.

Two are worth reading beyond this card: unique SKUs are not unique test data when the combobox searches by NAME and nothing is ever deleted, which presented as an impossible stock figure and looked exactly like a triple-submit concurrency bug until one database query showed three separate runs issuing against the same stale row; and a cleanup hook whose cost grows with the database's history, which outgrew its timeout and reported the failure on the last test in the file, a test that was never at fault.

cards.title: Playwright end to end wired into the quality workflow: auth plus the core cycle against local dev with seeded test data.
cards.plain: An automatic check drives the whole cycle, ordering through to issuing out, every time anything changes. A change that breaks the system is caught before Mihai ever sees it.
cards.acceptance: CI CHECK: the `quality` workflow run on this card's own PR contains an e2e step that executes the Playwright suite and the whole run concludes success. Proven by the run URL for the PR head sha, recorded as the card evidence.
cards.defaults: CHROMIUM ONLY, HEADLESS. One browser, one project in the Playwright config. Firefox and WebKit triple the CI minutes to re-prove the same application logic on a desktop-only internal tool. TEST DATA IS NEVER DELETED. Seeded rows carry a cancelled flag convention: a boolean or status value marking the row as test data, set on creation and never removed. Teardown marks, it does not delete, because a DELETE written for a test database is a DELETE that eventually runs against a real one. This convention is documented in the seed script header and in docs/LEARNINGS.md. SEED IDS ARE DETERMINISTIC AND PREFIXED so a human reading the database can tell test rows from real ones at a glance. THE CHECK NAME STAYS `quality`. The e2e run is a STEP inside the existing quality job, never a second job and never a second workflow, because branch protection names exactly one check and adding a second one silently makes it non-required. SECRETS: CI runs against local dev with a local or test Supabase configuration read from environment variable names. No production credential ever reaches a workflow file. FLAKE POLICY: no retries. A retried test hides a race, and a race in a stock system is a wrong number in a warehouse. A flaky test is fixed or deleted, never retried.

evidence.ref: quality workflow run 32885233792 on this card's own PR (#12), head sha f5dfb07989329cc295ea77c08b25492cadebc334, conclusion SUCCESS. https://github.com/happygamer1919-tech/rc-inventory/actions/runs/32885233792 ONE job named quality, fifteen steps, all green: Checkout, Setup Node, Install dependencies, Typecheck, Build, Validate boards, Start local Supabase, Launch database auth and storage, Apply migrations to the local stack, Export local Supabase credentials, Seed the two test accounts, Install Playwright chromium, END TO END, and the failure-artifact step correctly skipped. The e2e step ran the whole suite: 35 passed in 2.3m on chromium, against a database built from empty by supabase db reset replaying all five migrations in file order. THE FIRST RUN FAILED AND THAT WAS THE POINT: it found a latent defect in migration 0001, which granted privileges to anon and authenticated but never to service_role, and had worked on eu-west-1 only because of a project-level default privilege set before any of this code existed. Fixed by migration 0005, applied to production under R-001, post-check 11 tables with service_role and authenticated both readable. Commit f5dfb07989329cc295ea77c08b25492cadebc334.

cards.notes:
The card that makes every later acceptance line mean something. Before this lands, a named test is a file someone ran once locally; after it lands, a named test is a gate on every PR. Scope is the harness plus auth and the core cycle: sign in, create an inbound order, mark it arrived, issue it outbound. Later cards add their own spec files to the same suite. AFTER MERGE IVAN ADDS NOTHING. No new required check, no branch protection edit, no repository setting. The check name stays `quality` precisely so the protection rule set up for phase 1 keeps working untouched. Say this in the PR description so nobody goes looking for a setting to change. Depends only on P2-02 rather than on the later cards, so the harness exists before the cards that need it, not after.

--- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-26 (card shipped) ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged rather than asked:
1. CHROMIUM ONLY, HEADLESS. One project in the config, one browser installed in CI.
2. THE CHECK NAME STAYS quality, and every new step is a STEP INSIDE THAT ONE JOB. Not a second job, not a second workflow. Branch protection names exactly one check, and a second one would sit green beside it while blocking nothing. IVAN ADDS NOTHING after merge: no new required check, no branch protection edit, no repository setting.
3. NO PRODUCTION CREDENTIAL IN A WORKFLOW FILE, and none in repository secrets either. The suite runs against a LOCAL Supabase stack started in the runner; its anon and service keys are the fixed published demo keys and open nothing outside the container. The card's own defaults asked for exactly this: 'a local or test Supabase configuration'.
4. NO RETRIES. retries: 0 in the config. A retried test hides a race, and a race in a stock system is a wrong number in a warehouse. Every flake met during this wave was diagnosed to a cause and fixed, never retried; two of those diagnoses were wrong on the first attempt and the corrections are in docs/LEARNINGS.md.
5. TEST DATA IS MARKED AT CREATION AND NEVER DELETED. The convention is written in full in the header of scripts/seed-test-accounts.mjs: the TEST- prefix and the .local domain are the marking, there is no DELETE anywhere in the suite, and the inventory visibility filter is what keeps test rows out of the way without destroying them. Seeding is idempotent, keyed on email.

DECISIONS WORTH NAMING:
6. THE DEV SERVER, NOT next start. NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined at BUILD time and the build step runs before .env.local exists, so a production server would serve a bundle with no Supabase URL in it and every test would fail on a blank login screen. The dev server compiles after the environment is written. This is also what the card asked for: 'against local dev'.
7. supabase db reset REPLAYS EVERY MIGRATION FROM EMPTY, in file order, which is the same order Ivan applies them by hand. A broken migration now fails CI on the PR that introduces it rather than on the day someone pastes it into the SQL editor.
8. WHICH SERVICES RUN IS DECIDED BY supabase/config.toml, not by command flags, so there is one place to change it and no risk of a renamed container breaking the workflow.
9. ON FAILURE the Playwright report and traces upload as an artifact, so a red run can be read without reproducing it.

THE FIRST CI RUN FAILED, AND THAT IS THE CARD JUSTIFYING ITSELF ON ITS FIRST DAY. Migration 0001 granted table privileges to anon and authenticated and never to service_role. It had always worked on eu-west-1, because Supabase sets default privileges so tables created there are granted to service_role automatically. The schema appeared self-sufficient and was not: it worked because of a machine setting, not because of itself. The first replay onto a second database failed on its first write. Nothing was broken in production and nothing would have been until the day someone stood up a staging project or restored a backup, which is exactly when nobody wants to discover it. Fixed by migration 0005, which also sets ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES so the omission cannot recur at 0006. Both halves are written up in docs/LEARNINGS.md.

WAVE 1 ENDS HERE. P2-08 onward is outside this wave's ceiling.

cards.title: Upload pipeline app side against contract v2: signed URL fired to MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL, callback verified and upserted by order_id as a draft, Make mocked at the transport.
cards.plain: The system can send an uploaded supplier document away to be read automatically and take the results back. This is the plumbing behind the feature that saves the office typing every delivery in by hand.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with Make mocked at the transport, the same way P2-10 mocks Resend. extraction.spec covers, one case per clause: (1) firing posts to MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL with X-RC-Secret and a body carrying exactly order_id, document_url, document_filename, mime_type, size_bytes and callback_url, and nothing else; (2) a callback with status extracted stores a draft whose lines carry quantity, unit plus unit_raw, unit_price, line_total, currency plus currency_raw, category plus category_raw and confidence, and whose document level carries subtotal, vat_amount, document_total, prices_include_vat, vat_rate, order_date, currency plus currency_raw, top-level confidence and _meta; (3) THE SAME order_id POSTED TWICE REPLACES THE DRAFT AND NEVER CREATES A SECOND, answered 202 then 200; (4) a callback with a wrong or missing MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET is answered 401 and stores nothing; (5) a payload violating the schema is answered 400 and stores nothing, and an error_code outside the fixed set is one of the violations tested; (6) a callback with status partial stores the lines that DID extract, together with error_code and reason; (7) a callback with status failed stores error_code and reason and creates no draft lines; (8) an absent field arrives as null and is stored as null, and the case asserts that neither an empty string nor a zero is substituted anywhere. PLUS MIGRATION JOURNAL: the draft storage migration applied with the three phases of CLAUDE.md 8.5 recorded in this card evidence and appended to docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, with the post-check showing every nullable column actually nullable and RLS enabled with a non-zero policy count on both new tables.
cards.defaults: CONTRACT IS FROZEN AT docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md, ruling R-014. That file is the single source of truth for every field name, every type, every nullability and every response code. A field in a payload that is not in that document is IGNORED, never guessed at. A change to the contract is a ruling and an edit to that file, never an edit here and never a quiet accommodation in code. ABSENT IS null. Never an empty string, never zero. An empty string says the field was present and blank; a zero in a quantity or a price is a real value. Both are lies about what the document contained and both are indistinguishable from real data downstream. The acceptance tests this explicitly rather than trusting it. order_id IS THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY. UPSERT, NEVER APPEND. A callback arriving twice for the same order_id REPLACES the stored extraction. Retries are expected: Make retries on 5xx, networks drop responses after the work is done, and P2-09 ships a re-fire control that deliberately sends the same document again. Without the key every one of those becomes a duplicate draft a human has to notice and delete. RESPONSE CODES ARE FIXED: 202 accepted, 200 duplicate, 400 rejected, 401 bad secret, 5xx retryable. Make retries on 5xx and does not retry on 4xx, so this split decides whether a bad payload is retried forever or dropped once. A 5xx MUST MEAN NOTHING WAS STORED: a half-store followed by a failure means the retry arrives against a partially written row, so the write is one transaction or it is not a write. error_code IS A FIXED SET: download_failed, url_expired, unsupported_format, unreadable_document, extraction_failed, invalid_output, timeout. Anything outside it is a rejected payload, 400. reason stays FREE TEXT alongside the code: the code is what the application branches on, the reason is what the operator reads. MAPPED PLUS RAW, NEVER ONE FIELD DOING BOTH JOBS, for unit, currency and category alike. The raw field carries the document words verbatim and the mapped field is nullable. A mapped value that silently replaces what the document said destroys the only evidence of what was actually extracted. NO THIRD-PARTY DOCUMENT CONVERSION SUB-PROCESSOR, ruling R-015. Not a PDF-to-image API, not an OCR service, not a file conversion endpoint, however small and however free. A converter sees every supplier invoice in full, so adding one is a data-sharing decision about Rapid Construct commercial information and it needs an owner ruling naming the service. IF MAKE OPENAI FILE INPUT DOES NOT WORK, CONVERSION IS BUILT INSIDE OUR OWN APP. That is the pre-authorised path and needs no further ruling. MAKE IS MOCKED AT THE TRANSPORT, not by a branch in the application, the same way P2-10 mocks Resend. A base URL environment variable pointed at a local server, so the real fetch, the real headers and the real handling of a non-2xx response are all exercised. A test branch inside the sender leaves exactly the code that can fail in production untested. SECRETS BY NAME ONLY: MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL, X-RC-Secret, MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET. Values never in the board, the tests, the logs or the code. THE MOCK IS A SERVER, NOT A BRANCH IN THE APPLICATION, and it is the P2-10 pattern reused rather than reinvented: a small HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 that Playwright starts alongside the dev server, reached through MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL. The application makes its real fetch, with real headers, and DOES NOT KNOW A TEST IS RUNNING. A test branch inside the sender would leave exactly the code that can fail in production untested. NOTHING LEAVES THE MACHINE. NULLABLE MEANS NULLABLE IN THE SCHEMA TOO. The contract says absent is null, never an empty string and never zero, and a column declared NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 would make the database itself the thing that substitutes a lie. No NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and no empty-string default anywhere in the draft tables. THE ONLY REQUIRED COLUMNS are the ones that are structurally required: the order_id, the status, and the foreign keys. THIS CARD DOES NOT TALK TO ANDRE SCENARIO. It builds and proves our side against the frozen contract. The live round trip is P2-08b.

evidence.ref: PR #43, quality run 33027411560 for head sha 28270a5, 54 passed in 4.8m, of which the EIGHT cases of tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts, one per acceptance clause, all green. (1) the fire carries exactly the six contract fields and the X-RC-Secret header; (2) an extracted callback writes every document-level and line-level field; (3) the same order_id twice answers 202 then 200 and REPLACES, two lines after a second callback carrying two, not three; (4) wrong and missing secret both 401 with nothing written; (5) four separate contract violations each 400 with nothing written; (6) partial keeps the two lines that extracted; (7) failed stores reason and code with zero lines; (8) absent stored as null field by field, and an explicitly blank string stored as null too. MIGRATIONS: 0008 and 0009 applied under R-012 with the three phases, journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md. 0008 post-check: 13 tables all RLS with 49 policies, 8 enums, every contract column nullable, zero defaults of 0 or empty string. 0009 post-check: anon can SELECT 0 of 13 tables, authenticated 13 of 13, service_role 13 of 13.

cards.notes:
Split from P2-08 on 2026-08-26 by ruling R-025. This card is the APP SIDE and it is eligible; P2-08b is the live round trip and stays blocked on andre.

WHY THE SPLIT IS LEGITIMATE AND NOT AN END RUN AROUND A BLOCKED CARD. P2-08 was blocked on Andre because nobody knew the shape of the payload. That is no longer true: the shape is decided, written down and FROZEN at docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md by ruling R-014. Our side of a frozen contract is buildable against it whether or not the other side has confirmed, and what still genuinely needs Andre is the live round trip, which is exactly what P2-08b keeps.

THE RISK THIS ACCEPTS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: if Andre scenario eventually sends something other than v2, this receiver is wrong and gets corrected. That is a smaller cost than three cards idle behind a third party, and it is bounded by the contract being frozen and written down rather than assumed. R-025 records the same reasoning.

CLAUSES 1 THROUGH 8 OF THE ACCEPTANCE ARE CARRIED VERBATIM FROM P2-08. Nothing was softened in the split. The only sentence dropped was the trailing note saying that a static check is not what proves the card, which was true of P2-08 and is still true here, and the migration journal requirement was added because this card now owns the schema the drafts are stored in.

INHERITED CONTEXT FROM P2-08, kept so the card stands alone:
Server side only. No review screen, no confirm, no visual work: that is P2-09. This card is the plumbing and its proof. BLOCKED ON ANDRE AT AUTHORING TIME because the contract is unconfirmed. Per the skip-not-halt rule the card carries its question and its recommendation, and the executor works other cards until Andre answers or Ivan rules. If Ivan rules 'proceed as sent', clear blocked_on, log the ruling in notes, and build. Feeds gate G4 together with P2-09. G4 needs a real document through the real Make scenario, so it cannot flip on the mocked test alone.

--- REWRITTEN AGAINST CONTRACT v2 2026-08-26 (ruling R-014) ---
The card previously described the v1 contract sent to Andre on 2026-08-25. It is rewritten whole against extraction contract v2, frozen at docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md, which is now the single source of truth for every field name, type, nullability and response code.
WHAT v2 ADDS OVER v1. Inbound gains document_filename, mime_type and size_bytes alongside order_id, so Make logs and ours both carry a human-readable name and the extractor knows what it is fetching before it fetches it. Per line the callback gains unit_raw, line_total, currency plus currency_raw, category plus category_raw and a per-line confidence. Document level gains subtotal, vat_amount, document_total, prices_include_vat, vat_rate, order_date, a top-level confidence and _meta. _meta carries model, prompt version, page count, characters extracted and duration, is stored and never shown to the operator, and exists so a wrong extraction can be EXPLAINED rather than argued about: a low character count against a high page count is the signature of a scan that never OCRed.
prices_include_vat DECIDES WHICH TOTAL RECONCILES against the lines, which is why it is a boolean on the document rather than an assumption in our code. vat_rate is a number, 20.0, never the string 20% and never 0.2.
order_date IS THE DOCUMENT DATE, NOT THE DELIVERY DATE. A document carrying both supplies its own date here and the other is not sent at all. Written into the contract prompt rules because getting it wrong produces a plausible date rather than an error.
STAYS blocked_on andre. R-014 settles what OUR side of the contract is. It does not settle that Andre has agreed to send it, and building a receiver against an unconfirmed contract is how both sides implement a different document.

--- THE CONTROLLED CATEGORY LIST DOES NOT EXIST, HALTED 2026-08-26 ---
The dispatch asked for the controlled category list to be exported from the live schema to docs/contracts/categories.json, and said plainly that if no such list exists in schema the item halts and nothing is invented. IT DOES NOT EXIST. THAT ITEM IS HALTED AND NO FILE WAS WRITTEN.
PROVEN READ-ONLY AGAINST THE LIVE SCHEMA under ruling R-012, with default_transaction_read_only on, connectivity proven with SELECT 1 first. There is NO ENUM resembling a category list: the six enums are app_role, currency_code, inbound_status, outbound_status, status_entity and unit_code, and none of them is about categories. There are ZERO CHECK CONSTRAINTS on public.categories, so nothing restricts what a name may be. The table is exactly what migration 0001 says it is, a rows table with a unique name and no seed, deliberately unseeded because the phase 1 seven were mock data invented to make a demo look real.
THE LIVE CONTENT MAKES EXPORTING IT ACTIVELY HARMFUL, not merely useless. public.categories holds exactly ONE row: TEST-Categorie, active, carrying 305 products. That is the CRIT-11 e2e residue, and it is the very thing P2-15 exists to delete. A categories.json exported today would enumerate one test string as the clients controlled vocabulary, would be committed, and would then be read by whoever builds the mapping in P2-09 long after P2-15 has removed the row it names.
WHAT THE CONTRACT DOES INSTEAD, section 4.4 of docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md: category is mapped against the categories rows PRESENT AT EXTRACTION TIME, which is the only list that exists, and category_raw always carries the documents own words verbatim so nothing is lost when the mapping finds nothing and category comes back null. Amendment 1 of R-014 is satisfied in substance, and the part of it that assumed a controlled list is recorded as not implementable rather than faked.
IF THE OWNER WANTS A FIXED ENUMERATED LIST, that is a schema decision, a migration and a card. It is not something a contract document may invent on his behalf.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-27 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN: Make mocked at the transport and not by a branch in the application; nullable meaning nullable in the schema too, with no NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and no empty-string default anywhere; the only required columns being the structurally required ones; and no contact with Andre scenario, which is P2-08b.
THE POST-CHECK FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN MIGRATION, which is exactly what it is for. 0008 left anon holding SELECT on both new tables, where every sibling grants it nothing. Nothing leaked, because RLS is on and every policy is to authenticated, so an anonymous request matched no policy; but the grant is the FIRST of two layers and a table with one where every sibling has two is protected less. Supabase grants at CREATE TABLE time and 0001 revoked once, against the tables that existed then. 0009 revokes and then ALTERS DEFAULT PRIVILEGES, so the next CREATE TABLE cannot reintroduce it. 0008 was not edited: it is applied, and a correction is a new numbered file.
TWO FIXES BEFORE GREEN, BOTH REAL DEFECTS AND BOTH FOUND BY THE SPEC. First, duplicate detection read status rather than callback_at, using a strict comparison that treated an absent field as a value, so the first callback answered 200 instead of 202. Second, and much more serious: the proxy was REDIRECTING the callback to the login screen, because it carries no session and the middleware was written for humans. Playwright follows redirects, so every case received a perfectly good 200 from the login page. In production that shape is quieter and worse: Make posts, gets 200, records a successful delivery and never retries, and the only symptom is drafts that never appear. THE ASSERTION THAT CAUGHT IT WAS THE ONE EXPECTING A FAILURE: case 4 posts a deliberately wrong secret, and a wrong secret answering 200 is what pointed at the layer in front of the route rather than the code inside it. Written into docs/LEARNINGS.md.
NEW PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENT, FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the callback endpoint writes with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, because Make posts with no session and every RLS policy is to authenticated. The key is referenced by name only and must be present in the Vercel production environment before P2-08b can run. P2-13 rotates it, which is unchanged.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the review and confirm screens, which are P2-09; the live round trip, which is P2-08b; and any resolution of whether order_id names an existing inbound order, which migration 0008 deliberately leaves open by carrying no foreign key.

cards.title: Live extraction round trip: one real document through Andre scenario, end to end, against the frozen contract.
cards.plain: One genuine supplier document goes through the automatic reading from beginning to end, to prove it works on real paperwork rather than on a made-up test file. Until that has happened, nobody can promise Mihai the feature works.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: Andre confirms extraction contract v2 and runs one live document through the real Make scenario.
CONTEXT: our side is built and proven against the frozen contract by P2-08a, with Make mocked at the transport. What no mock can prove is that Andre scenario actually sends v2. This card is that single round trip and nothing else.
WHAT IS NEEDED: (1) Andre confirms docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md as frozen, including the three amendments and the two global rules; (2) MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL and the X-RC-Secret value are set in the production environment by Ivan; (3) one real supplier document is uploaded on production and travels the whole path, and the stored draft matches what the document says.
THE THREE PROMPT RULES ARE THE PART THAT CANNOT BE CAUGHT BY A SCHEMA CHECK, section 8 of the contract, because each produces silently wrong numbers rather than an error: comma decimal with dot thousands, so 1.234,56 is 1234.56; day-first dates for RO and MD suppliers, and order_date is the DOCUMENT date not the delivery date; and product names verbatim and untranslated, because the name is how the operator matches a line against the catalogue. A payload can satisfy every type in the schema and still be wrong on all three.
OPTIONS: (a) Andre confirms the contract and we run one document together; (b) Andre proposes changes, they come back as a ruling, the contract is amended, P2-08a receiver is corrected and then we run one document; (c) launch without a live round trip ever having been done.
RECOMMENDATION: (a), and explicitly not (c). Gate G4 asks for one real document to have travelled the whole path on production, and there is no substitute for having watched it once.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: gate G4 stays fail. P2-09 and P2-11 are NOT blocked by this card, only by P2-08a, so the rest of the lane proceeds.

--- CORRECTED 2026-08-31 BY RULING R-080, APPENDED AND NOT REWRITTEN ---
THE LINE ABOVE READING `IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: gate G4 stays fail` HAS BEEN FALSE SINCE 2026-08-28. Ruling R-053 replaced G4's deciding clause on that date: the gate is now the ingest endpoint asserted against a fixture document plus four named failure cases, and it no longer waits on a real document through Andre's live scenario. Card P2-20 carries the two of those four that are still missing, redirect and oversize, and it depends on P2-08a alone.
SO THE CORRECT IMPACT LINE IS: nothing on the launch gate waits on this card. P2-09 and P2-11 never did. What is still owed here is the only thing no fixture can prove, that Andre's scenario SENDS the frozen contract and that the three prompt rules hold on real paper, and that remains worth having.
NOTHING NEW IS ASKED OF ANDRE BY THIS CORRECTION. The ask above is unchanged, word for word. What changed is that it stopped holding a launch condition.
cards.acceptance: ONE CLAUSE, and it is the one no mock can prove: one real supplier document uploaded on production travels the whole path end to end against Andre real scenario, and the result is asserted at every hop. The document reaches the private rc-docs bucket; the fire carries the six inbound fields to the real MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL with X-RC-Secret; the callback arrives at the production endpoint carrying a valid MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET and is answered 202; the stored draft matches the document, checked by a human against the paper for the supplier, the order_date, the document_total and every line quantity, unit and price; and the three prompt rules hold on that document, meaning decimals parsed as comma-decimal, the date read day-first and taken from the document rather than the delivery, and product names verbatim and untranslated. Evidence is kind journal: the order_id, the stored draft as JSON, and the human confirmation of the comparison.
cards.defaults: THIS CARD DOES NOT REBUILD ANYTHING. P2-08a owns the receiver, the schema and the response table. If the live round trip fails, the fix is a defect on P2-08a or a contract amendment by ruling, never a second implementation here. ONE DOCUMENT IS ENOUGH AND TWO ARE NOT BETTER. The purpose is to prove the path exists end to end and that the prompt rules hold on real paper; a second document proves the same thing again. A document that fails is a finding, and the finding is the value. NO PRODUCTION CREDENTIAL IS HELD BY A TERMINAL FOR THIS. MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL and X-RC-Secret are set in the production environment by Ivan, referenced by name only. THE SUITE IS NEVER POINTED AT PRODUCTION for this card or any other; the round trip is a human action on the production screen, not an automated run. PRECONDITION ADDED 2026-08-27 BY RULING R-029: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be present in the Vercel PRODUCTION environment before this card runs. The callback endpoint writes with it, because Make posts with no session and every RLS policy on the two extraction tables is to authenticated. Without the variable the route answers 500, which under contract section 6 means nothing was stored and Make retries, so a live round trip would look like an endless retry against a healthy endpoint. Verified BY NAME ONLY: the value is never read, printed or written anywhere.
cards.notes:
Split from P2-08 on 2026-08-26 by ruling R-025. This is the half that genuinely needs Andre, and it keeps the blocked_on andre that the whole of P2-08 used to carry.

WHY THIS HALF CANNOT BE MOCKED, WHICH IS THE ENTIRE REASON IT EXISTS SEPARATELY. A mock proves our receiver handles the contract. It cannot prove Andre scenario SENDS the contract, and it cannot prove the three prompt rules hold on real paper. A payload can satisfy every type in the schema and still read 1.234,56 as 1.23456, still read 03/04/2026 as 4 March, and still translate a product name into something the catalogue will never match. Those three are invisible to a schema check and expensive in a warehouse.

DOES NOT BLOCK THE LANE. P2-09 depends on P2-08a only, per R-025, and P2-11 likewise. This card gates only itself and launch gate G4.

THE ORIGINAL P2-08 QUESTION IS PRESERVED HERE because it is what was actually sent to Andre and it must not be lost in a split:
DECISION NEEDED: Andre confirms extraction contract v2 as frozen at docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md.
CONTEXT: v2 is accepted on OUR side by ruling R-014, which ratified changes (a) through (l) with three amendments. The file is frozen and P2-08 and P2-09 are rewritten against it. What is outstanding is Andre agreeing that the Make scenario will send exactly that shape. Building the receiver against a contract the sender has not confirmed is how both sides end up implementing a different document.
THE THREE AMENDMENTS TO CONFIRM: (1) category follows the unit and currency pattern, category_raw verbatim plus a nullable mapped category, and the caveat in section 4.4 that there is no controlled category list to map against yet; (2) order_id is the idempotency key and repeat callbacks upsert rather than append; (3) failed and partial both carry error_code and reason, and partial RETAINS the lines that did extract rather than discarding the document.
THE TWO GLOBAL RULES TO CONFIRM: absent is null and never an empty string or a zero; and the fixed response codes 202, 200, 400, 401, 5xx.
THE THREE PROMPT RULES TO CONFIRM, section 8, because every one of them produces silently wrong numbers rather than an error and our side cannot detect a violation: comma decimal with dot thousands, so 1.234,56 is 1234.56; day-first dates for RO and MD suppliers, so 03/04/2026 is 3 April, and order_date is the DOCUMENT date and not the delivery date; and product names verbatim and untranslated, because the name is how the operator matches a line against the catalogue.
OPTIONS: (a) Andre confirms the document as frozen and we build the receiver against it; (b) Andre proposes changes, they come back as a ruling, the file is amended and then we build; (c) we build against v2 unconfirmed and reconcile later.
RECOMMENDATION: (a), and explicitly NOT (c). The receiver is cheap to build and expensive to build twice, and a mismatch surfaces as wrong stock rather than as an error.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: P2-08 stays blocked, P2-09 stays behind it, P2-11 stays behind P2-09, and gate G4 stays fail. That is the whole remaining chain of this phase except the owner actions.

--- PRECONDITION 2026-08-27 (ruling R-029) ---

cards.title: Review and confirm flow, including the visible failure surface: the draft fills the review form, the operator edits, confirm creates the real inbound order, and failed or partial documents show their reason with a re-fire control.
cards.plain: Once a document has been read, the office sees the details already filled in, corrects anything wrong, and confirms, which creates the real order. When a document cannot be read, the screen says why and offers to try again instead of failing quietly.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0. review.spec covers: (1) a draft with status extracted fills the review form with every extracted field, and a value the operator edits is what gets saved rather than the extracted one; (2) confirm creates a real inbound order whose lines match the reviewed values, and the draft is consumed rather than left behind; (3) an extracted line naming a product the catalogue does not have creates a flagged product with needs_review set, and never merges onto a similar SKU; (4) A DOCUMENT WITH status failed IS VISIBLE IN THE LIST in a state that is not pending, showing its reason in full and its error_code rendered as a Romanian sentence rather than as the raw token; (5) A DOCUMENT WITH status partial SHOWS THE SAME REASON AND error_code AND STILL CARRIES THE LINES THAT DID EXTRACT, and the case asserts the surviving line count is greater than zero; (6) THE RE-FIRE CONTROL ON A FAILED DOCUMENT RE-POSTS WITH THE SAME order_id, asserted at the mocked Make transport, and the replacement extraction REPLACES the previous one rather than adding a second; (7) every one of the seven error_code values renders a distinct Romanian sentence and none of them renders the raw token.
cards.defaults: SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-26 BY RULING R-014: this card now owns the VISIBLE FAILURE SURFACE, not only the happy path. A failure the operator cannot see is a document that sits in the system looking pending forever, and the operator learns to distrust the whole screen because of it. failed AND partial ARE BOTH VISIBLE DOCUMENT STATES. Each shows the reason in full, the error_code as a Romanian sentence rather than as the token, and a re-fire control. THE RE-FIRE CONTROL RE-POSTS WITH THE SAME order_id. That is what makes it safe: per the contract idempotency rule the result REPLACES the previous extraction instead of adding a second draft. A re-fire that minted a fresh id would create exactly the duplicate the idempotency key exists to prevent. partial RETAINS THE LINES THAT DID EXTRACT and never discards the document because part of it was unreadable. Nine good lines and one unreadable one is nine lines of typing the operator does not have to redo. THE OPERATOR EDIT WINS. The extracted value is a suggestion, and what is saved is what is on screen at confirm. An extraction that silently overrides an edit is worse than no extraction. AN UNMATCHED PRODUCT NAME CREATES A FLAGGED PRODUCT with needs_review set, and never silently merges onto a similar SKU. products.needs_review exists in migration 0001 for exactly this and its comment says so. ERROR COPY IS ROMANIAN, one distinct sentence per error_code, all seven. A raw token on screen is an English string reaching the UI, which CLAUDE.md section 11 forbids. CONFIRM IS ONE TRANSACTION. The draft is consumed and the order is created together, or neither happens.
