cards.title: The confirmation message lives inside the draft row that confirming makes disappear, so a successful confirm can leave the screen blank.
cards.plain: Fixed: confirming a document could leave the operator looking at a blank screen with nothing to say it had worked. The natural next step is to confirm again, which would have created the same delivery twice.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0, and case 2 asserts the two facts TOGETHER: after confirm, the draft card for that order_id is gone from the list AND the success panel is still visible. Asserting either alone is what let the defect through: the old case checked only that the message appeared, and whether it appeared depended on whether the assertion arrived before the refresh that unmounted it.
cards.defaults: THE FIX IS WHERE THE MESSAGE LIVES, NOT WHEN THE REFRESH RUNS. Delaying router.refresh() until the operator dismisses the panel would also make the test pass, and it would leave the list showing a draft that no longer exists until somebody clicks. The confirmation belongs to the panel, above the list, because it is about the panel's work and not about one draft row. NO NEW MIGRATION AND NO SERVER CHANGE: the data was always written correctly, and the created order was always created. This is entirely a question of which component owns the message.

evidence.ref: PR #51, quality run 33076204137 for head sha d864d22, 61 passed 0 failed in 5.7m. review.spec case 2 green with the tightened assertion, which now demands BOTH facts at once: after confirm the draft card for that order_id is gone from the list AND the success panel is still visible. The defect was found by run 33075182379 on the P2-11 branch, where case 2 failed with review-created never appearing while cases 1 and 3, which confirm identically, passed; the failure snapshot showed the flagged product already in the catalogue and the list empty, which is what proved the confirm had succeeded and only the message was missing. No migration, no server change: the fix is which component owns the message.

cards.notes:
FOUND BY CI ON THE P2-11 BRANCH, 2026-08-27, run 33075182379: review.spec case 2 failed with review-created never appearing, while cases 1 and 3, which confirm in exactly the same way, passed. The catalogue in the failure snapshot already carried the flagged product that confirm creates, and the screen showed the document list with no drafts pending, so THE CONFIRM HAD SUCCEEDED and only the message was missing.

THE MECHANISM. Confirm consumes the draft. The consumed draft leaves the review list on the next refresh. The review form, and the success message inside it, are rendered INSIDE that draft's row, so router.refresh() unmounts the message it was supposed to show. Whether the test saw it depended on which arrived first, which is why it passed on P2-09's own green run and failed on a busier machine.

WHAT THE OPERATOR WOULD HAVE SEEN: press Confirmă, something flickers, and the screen is a document list with nothing on it. The order was created and there is no way to know that from the screen. On the screen the client judges the whole system by, that is worse than an error message.

WHY IT IS A CRIT AND NOT A PATCH ON P2-09: P2-09 is shipped and its acceptance ran green. A defect found in shipped code after the fact gets its own card, like CRIT-10 through CRIT-15, so the history says what was broken and when it was found rather than quietly rewriting a shipped card.

cards.title: A session whose profile row is missing or inactive bounces between the login page and the home page until the browser gives up.
cards.plain: Fixed: someone whose account had not been given access yet could type the right password and then get an endless loading loop instead of an answer. They now see a Romanian screen saying the account has no access and who to ask.
cards.acceptance: NAMED SPEC: tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts, describe block "Cont fara profil activ", four cases, green in the quality workflow. (1) Signing in as an account with a valid auth user and NO profiles row renders the Romanian no-access screen and observes FEWER THAN 5 redirect responses, where the defect produced them until the browser aborted. (2) Every protected route returns that same screen at the requested URL, proving a rewrite and not a redirect. (3) The sign-out control on that screen returns to the login page, so the session cannot trap the user. (4) An account WITH an active profile is unaffected: owner still lands on the dashboard and the login page still sends it to the dashboard. The account the three first cases need is seeded by scripts/seed-test-accounts.mjs, which creates the auth user and deliberately writes no profiles row.
cards.defaults: REWRITE, NEVER REDIRECT, for any refusal that a refused user can trigger again by following it. That is the rule the defect broke and it is the rule the fix restores: the 403 screen already worked this way and never looped. THE PROFILE IS PART OF THE SESSION, so it is resolved once, before any branch decides where the request goes. A QUERY ERROR IS NOT AN ABSENT ROW: both refuse, because entering with an unknown role is worse than not entering, but the error is logged so a broken policy cannot masquerade as a deleted account. THE SCREEN LIVES OUTSIDE THE (app) GROUP, like the login screen, because the application shell renders the navigation and the role badge and this account has no role to render. NO CREDENTIAL AND NO ROLE IS INFERRED FROM ABSENCE: a missing profile is never treated as the least privileged role, it is treated as no access.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 FROM A PRODUCTION REPORT. The owner could not log in: rc-inventory-iota.vercel.app answered ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS after a successful sign-in.

THE DEFECT, EXACTLY. proxy.ts evaluated two redirect branches in the wrong order. First "authenticated and sitting on the login page, so go to /". Second "no active profiles row, so go to the login page". The two pointed at each other, so any session whose profile lookup came back empty bounced between / and /autentificare until the browser aborted. Nothing in the unauthenticated path was involved, which is why the site looked healthy to anyone not signed in: verified live on the day, / answers 307 to /autentificare and /autentificare answers 200, on both the vercel.app host and the client domain.

WHAT THE FIX CHANGES. The profile is read before any branch decides. A session without an active profile is REWRITTEN to a dedicated Romanian screen, never redirected, so no loop is reachable whatever route was asked for, including the login page itself. The login-page redirect now runs only for a session that has an active profile.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME LINE AND FIXED WITH IT. The query discarded its error: const { data: profile } left error unbound, so a broken RLS policy, a network fault or any PostgREST failure was indistinguishable from "this account has no row", and all of them took the looping branch. The refusal is unchanged, because entering with an unknown role is worse than not entering, but anything that is not PGRST116, the code for "single found no row", is now logged as the defect it is.

WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY READS IT AS MORE THAN IT IS. It does not give any account access. An account with no profiles row still cannot enter; it now learns that in one clear screen instead of a loop. If the owner's own account is the one without a row, the row is still his to create, and that is data rather than code.

cards.title: Reminders real, with a Resend email sent when a product crosses its threshold, checked at every stock mutation.
cards.plain: When a product drops below the level Mihai sets for it, the system sends a warning email on its own. This is what stops him finding out something has run out at the moment somebody needs it.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts` exits 0 with Resend mocked. reminders.spec covers: an outbound issue that takes stock below a threshold triggers exactly one send; a further issue below the threshold triggers none; an arrival above the threshold re-arms and the next crossing sends again; a send failure is recorded and does not roll back the stock mutation.
cards.defaults: ONE EMAIL PER PRODUCT PER CROSSING, RE-ARMED WHEN STOCK RISES BACK ABOVE THE THRESHOLD. The reminder records that it fired; it does not fire again while stock stays below. When an arrival lifts stock above the threshold the reminder re-arms and may fire again on the next crossing. Without this a warehouse that sits under threshold for a week sends one email per outbound line and the operator filters the sender. CHECKED AT EVERY STOCK MUTATION, in the same path that writes the mutation: arrivals, issues, and any future adjustment. No cron, no scheduled job, no Inngest, no Twilio. SENDER is the Resend onboarding domain until the client domain lands, then it moves. That move is a one-line environment change and is noted on P2-12, not a new card. RECIPIENTS: the owner account email. Per-user notification preferences are out of scope. A FAILED SEND NEVER BLOCKS THE STOCK MUTATION. The mutation commits, the send failure is recorded on the reminder with its reason and shown on the reminders screen. Stock truth outranks email delivery. EMAIL BODY IS ROMANIAN, naming the product, its SKU, the current stock with its unit, and the threshold. RESEND_API_KEY is referenced by name only.

evidence.ref: PR #21, quality run https://github.com/happygamer1919-tech/rc-inventory/actions/runs/32973198555 for head sha 10f39e91cce10faaa90c6212362277a2623c8d5a, End to end step: 46 passed in 3.5m, of which the four cases of tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts. Case 43: an outbound issue below the threshold sends exactly one email, and the body carries the product name, the SKU, 8 buc and 10 buc. Case 44: a second issue below the threshold sends none, stock 6. Case 45: an arrival above the threshold re-arms, stock 28, and the next crossing sends a second email. Case 46: a refused send is recorded as Netrimis with the 500 on screen and the stock movement still stands at 8. Resend is mocked at the transport by tests/e2e/support/resend-mock.mjs on 127.0.0.1, so nothing left the runner and no real address received anything.

cards.notes:
The phase 1 screen showed thresholds and a fired-alerts list with toggles that sent nothing and said so. This card makes the sending real. RESEND_API_KEY IS PENDING and this card does not wait for it: the whole card is buildable, testable and shippable with Resend mocked, which is what the acceptance line checks. The card goes blocked_on ivan ONLY at live-send verification, meaning the moment gate G7 needs one real delivered email from a real crossing on production. Everything up to that point proceeds. Feeds gate G7, which needs the live send and therefore stays fail until the key exists. Deliberately not done: SMS, per-user preferences, digest emails, escalation.

--- GATE CHANGE 2026-08-25 (ruling R-002) ---
Gate flipped from owner_merge to green_self_merge. owner_merge is retired on this board. This card now ships on the green quality check plus its own named acceptance spec passing. Defect review moves to the CRITIC at the wave boundary and to an optional owner batch review before the client demo, and neither is a merge gate.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN: one email per product per crossing with re-arm on rising above the threshold, carried in reminders.is_armed; the check on the same path that writes the mutation (create_outbound_issue for the decrement, receive_inbound_order for the increment) with no cron and no scheduled job; the Resend onboarding domain as sender; the owner account email as recipient; a failed send never blocking the stock mutation; the email body Romanian with product, SKU, current stock with unit and threshold; and RESEND_API_KEY referenced by name only.

TWO DECISIONS TAKEN INSIDE THE CARD, neither covered by defaults, both reversible in one line.
(1) A THRESHOLD OF ZERO IS NOT A THRESHOLD. products.threshold defaults to 0, so every product created without one would email the first time it emptied. An operator who filters the sender stops receiving the reminders that were asked for too, which is the exact failure the one-per-crossing rule exists to prevent. Products that need an out-of-stock alert get a threshold set on the product screen. If Ivan wants the opposite, it is the condition threshold <= 0 in lib/reminders/notify.ts.
(2) THE ROW DISARMS ON ATTEMPT, NOT ON DELIVERY. When a send fails, the reminder still disarms and the reason is written to last_send_error and shown on /memento as Netrimis. Re-arming after a failure would retry at every subsequent stock mutation, which is the same email storm triggered by a down service instead of by a low warehouse. The card default says the failure is recorded and shown on the reminders screen, and that is what happens.

MARKING AN ISSUE SHIPPED IS NOT A STOCK MUTATION and is deliberately not wired: stock decrements when the issue is created and the outbound_lines are written. A check at shipping would reread the same numbers and could not find a new crossing. Said in a comment above shipOutboundIssue so the next reader does not add it back.

MIGRATION 0006 ADDED, NOT YET APPLIED TO PRODUCTION. supabase/migrations/0006_reminder_recipients.sql adds owner_reminder_recipients(), SECURITY DEFINER, returning nothing but the email addresses of active owners. It exists because profiles_select is (id = auth.uid()) OR is_owner(), so an account_manager cannot read the owner row, and an account_manager issuing material is the main way a threshold gets crossed. CI proves the file: supabase db reset replays every migration before the suite runs. THE PRODUCTION APPLY COULD NOT BE PERFORMED FROM THIS TERMINAL: the harness classifier denied the permitted secrets read from /Users/ivan/rc-secrets/phase2.env, so no connection was attempted, nothing was guessed, and no hostname was tried. Until it is applied, a crossing on production writes the reason onto the reminder row and shows it on /memento; the stock movement is unaffected. Gate G7 needs the live send regardless, and stays fail.

ONE EXISTING TEST WAS CORRECTED, NOT DELETED. dashboard.spec asserted that the memento screen said the sending would come at P2-10. That was true when P2-06 wrote it and false the moment this card landed. The assertion now checks the property rather than the sentence: the page names no card id, and the alerts card renders exactly one of its two states. Written up in docs/LEARNINGS.md.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: SMS, per-user notification preferences, digest emails, escalation, a re-evaluation when a threshold is EDITED (a threshold edit is not a stock mutation, and the card scopes the check to stock mutations), and any retry of a failed send.

--- RATIFIED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-008) ---
Both decisions taken inside this card are now standing behaviour, not executor judgement awaiting review. A threshold of 0 is not a threshold. A reminder disarms on send ATTEMPT and not on delivery, with no automatic retry. Neither is revisited: a future card that wants different behaviour supersedes R-008 by id, it does not reopen the question by preference.

cards.title: Production hardening: security headers, an environment presence check at boot, Romanian 404 and 500 pages, and no console errors on any screen.
cards.plain: The live site now behaves like a finished product: proper Romanian error pages, standard web security in place, and nothing broken running quietly in the background.
cards.acceptance: COMMANDS: `npm run build` exits 0, and `npx playwright test tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts` exits 0. headers.spec covers: each required security header is present on a production-mode response; the 404 route renders the Romanian page; a forced 500 renders the Romanian page; and a walk of every authenticated screen records zero console errors. PLUS APPLY LOG (added 2026-08-26 by ruling R-013): `test -f docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md` exits 0, and the file carries one entry per applied migration with version, actor, UTC timestamp, and the pre-check and post-check output, proven by `grep -c "^## " docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md` printing at least the number of files in supabase/migrations that have been applied.
cards.defaults: NEXT.JS HARDENING DEFAULTS, NO EXPERIMENTAL FLAGS. Use the framework's documented header and security configuration. Do not enable experimental options, do not hand-roll a CSP nonce pipeline, do not add a security middleware library. An experimental flag on the release build of a client's first production system is a bet with someone else's business. HEADERS: at minimum Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY or an equivalent frame-ancestors directive, and Referrer-Policy. A Content-Security-Policy is included only if it can be proven not to break the app; a CSP that silently blocks a script is worse than none, so if it cannot be verified in this card, log it as a follow-up card rather than shipping it untested. ENV PRESENCE CHECK: the application fails loudly at boot when a required environment variable is missing, naming the MISSING VARIABLE NAME and nothing else. It never prints a value, never prints a partial value, and never prints the length of a value. 404 AND 500 ARE ROMANIAN and carry a link back into the app. NO CONSOLE ERRORS means zero, on every screen, in a production build. A warning is triaged; an error is fixed or the screen does not ship. APPLY LOG, ADDED 2026-08-26 BY RULING R-013. Every migration apply appends an entry to a COMMITTED file, docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, carrying the version, the ACTOR who applied it, a UTC timestamp, and the pre-check and post-check output in full. THE REASON IS A GAP FOUND ON 2026-08-26: migration 0006 was discovered already applied, and the project could not say by whom or when, because supabase_migrations.schema_migrations carries version, statements and name and has NO actor column and NO timestamp column. A migration path nobody can audit is a hardening defect, which is why this is folded into P2-11 rather than raised as its own card. The log is append-only and an entry is never edited after it is written; a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects.

evidence.ref: PR #50, quality run 33077820675 for head sha 80ca249, 66 passed 0 failed in 4.8m, of which the FIVE cases of tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts, all green, and `npm run build` exits 0 twice in that run: once as the workflow's own build step and once inside Playwright's production web server. THE FIVE CASES RUN AGAINST A SERVER IN PRODUCTION MODE, not the development server, in a Playwright project of their own pointed at it: next build followed by next start, in a separate build directory via NEXT_DIST_DIR so the two servers cannot overwrite each other mid-run. (1) every required header is present on THREE different response shapes: the rendered public page /autentificare, the proxy's REDIRECT for / without a session, and the authenticated screen /inventar; the redirect is asserted to really be a redirect so the case cannot pass by checking a page twice. Headers asserted: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy strict-origin, Permissions-Policy camera=(). (2) an unknown address answers 404 and renders the Romanian page, and its way back to the dashboard works. (3) /diagnostic-eroare answers 500 and renders the Romanian 500 page, showing the digest and NOT the error text, asserted by the deliberate error message being absent from the body. (4) a walk of every route in lib/nav.ts, signed in as owner, records ZERO console errors and zero uncaught page errors, in a production build. (5) docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md carries one heading per file in supabase/migrations, eleven of eleven, and every versioned entry names its actor and when it was applied. ENV PRESENCE CHECK: instrumentation.ts register() runs assertRequiredEnv on the Node runtime at boot; the suite exercises it on every run by the simple fact that both servers start, which they cannot do with a required variable missing.

cards.notes:
The last card before the system carries real data, and the reason it depends on all four feature-complete cards: hardening a moving target means re-doing it. Deliberately not done: a WAF, rate limiting, audit logging, penetration testing. Those are worth doing and none of them are this card; if the owner wants them, they are new cards.

--- GATE CHANGE 2026-08-25 (ruling R-002) ---
Gate flipped from owner_merge to green_self_merge. owner_merge is retired on this board. This card now ships on the green quality check plus its own named acceptance spec passing. Defect review moves to the CRITIC at the wave boundary and to an optional owner batch review before the client demo, and neither is a merge gate.

--- APPLY LOG REQUIREMENT ADDED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-013) ---
On 2026-08-26 migration 0006 was found already applied to the production project and NOBODY COULD SAY BY WHOM OR WHEN. supabase_migrations.schema_migrations carries version, statements and name, and no actor column and no timestamp column, so the question is not answerable from the database at all. It was not this terminal, and that is the entire extent of what could be established.
R-013 folds this into P2-11 rather than raising a separate card, on the reasoning that an unauditable apply path is a production hardening defect and this card is production hardening. The requirement is written into defaults and acceptance above: docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, one entry per apply, version and actor and UTC timestamp and both check outputs, committed, append-only.

--- DEPENDENCY RECALCULATED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-025) ---
depends_on is unchanged in substance and is restated against the split: P2-06, P2-07, P2-09 and P2-10. It never named P2-08 directly, so the split does not add an edge here. WHAT LANDED ON THE BRANCH, AND THE ONE DECISION THAT SHAPED THE REST.

THE SUITE NOW RUNS A SECOND SERVER, IN MOD PRODUCTIE, and everything else
follows from it. Two clauses of this card cannot be proven on the development
server: the headers are required on a PRODUCTION-MODE response, and defaults
says zero console errors means zero IN A PRODUCTION BUILD. The development
server carries an error overlay, React development warnings and on-demand
recompilation, so a green there would be about a different program from the one
the client opens. playwright.config.ts starts next build followed by next start
on its own port, the two servers get separate build directories through
NEXT_DIST_DIR because they would otherwise overwrite each other mid-run, and
headers.spec runs in its own project pointed at that origin.

HEADERS: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff,
X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin and a
Permissions-Policy that closes what the app never uses, through the framework's
documented headers() and no experimental flag. THE CSP HAS EXACTLY ONE
DIRECTIVE, frame-ancestors none, and that is deliberate: it is the modern
equivalent of X-Frame-Options that defaults names as acceptable, and it cannot
block a script, so "proven not to break the app" is satisfied by reading it.
script-src and the rest would need a nonce pipeline through the whole render,
which defaults forbids on this card, and they stay a future card rather than an
untested line shipped now.

ENV PRESENCE CHECK at boot, through instrumentation.ts register(), which is
stable API. TWO CLASSES, and the border is "can it serve a page": the two
NEXT_PUBLIC_ Supabase variables are REQUIRED and their absence throws so the
server does not start, while SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL,
MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL are EXPECTED IN
PRODUCTION and their absence writes a warning NAMING the variable. Putting the
second class in the first would be stricter and worse: it turns a warehouse
without email into a warehouse without an application. Names only, never a
value, never a partial value, never a length.

404 AND 500 IN ROMANIAN, both at app/ root rather than inside the (app) group,
because that group's layout renders the shell and reads the session, and a shell
with no data is what P2-02 forbids. Both carry a way back. The 500 screen shows
the DIGEST and never the error text: a database message carries table names,
column names and sometimes query fragments.

A ROUTE THAT THROWS ON PURPOSE, /diagnostic-eroare, because the acceptance asks
for a forced 500 and an error screen nobody has watched fall is the safety net
that turns out to be torn on the day it is needed. It is behind the proxy like
every other screen, is not in NAV, reads nothing and writes nothing. The
alternative was an if-TEST branch, which is the exact mistake LEARNINGS records
at P2-10: a second implementation that only runs in tests and that everybody
trusts in CI.

APPLY-LOG: the pre-log table became one entry per migration, word for word, with
no fact changed. It was the only part of the file without a heading per version,
so "does every migration have an entry" could not be asked by a machine. Case 5
of headers.spec now asks exactly that, per file, and also that every entry names
its actor and when it was applied.

NOT SHIPPED YET: the acceptance has not run. Next step is the green quality run
on the head sha, then merge.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-27 ---
quality run 33077820675 on head sha 80ca249: 66 passed, 0 failed.

ONE DEFECT FOUND BY THIS CARD AND FIXED ON ITS OWN CARD. The first full run of
this branch failed review.spec case 2, which belongs to P2-09 and had been green
on P2-09's own run. It was not this card: the success message of the review
screen was rendered inside the draft row that confirming deletes, so the refresh
that follows a confirm unmounted the message it was meant to show. It became
CRIT-16, was fixed and shipped there, and this branch merged it in. The reason
it surfaced here is worth keeping: this card adds a production build to the
suite's startup, the machine is busier, and a race that resolved one way on a
quiet runner resolved the other way on a loaded one.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR A FUTURE CARD, written down rather than implied:
a full Content-Security-Policy. The one shipped carries a single directive,
frame-ancestors none, which cannot block a script and is the equivalent the
card's defaults name as acceptable. script-src and the rest need a nonce
pipeline through the whole render, which defaults forbids here. A WAF, rate
limiting and audit logging were out of scope by the card's own text and stay
out.

cards.plain: The system knows its own web address, so signing in and following a link always lands on the real site rather than a temporary one.
cards.acceptance: URL CHECK: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -L https://rapidconstructmd.com/` prints 200 over a valid certificate after following the redirect chain, the apex answers 308 to https://www.rapidconstructmd.com/, and a request to the client domain is answered by the client domain rather than by any other host. A root domain with no SPF publishes no policy about who may send as it.
RESEND VERIFICATION STATUS, NOT VERIFIABLE FROM HERE, AND THAT IS WHY THE CARD STAYS BLOCKED. GET https://api.resend.com/domains answered: This API key is restricted to only send emails. The key in the environment is a SENDING-ONLY restricted key, so it cannot read the domains endpoint and cannot report whether Resend itself considers the domain verified. The DNS records being present is necessary and is not sufficient: only Resend can say it has checked them.
THE SECOND HALF OF THE ACCEPTANCE IS ALSO UNMET. The reminder sender must move off the Resend onboarding domain to the client domain, proven by a delivered email. RESEND_FROM is not set in the production environment, so the sender is still the default onboarding address. AND A THIRD THING, FOUND AT TASK 1 AND NOT PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN ANYWHERE: owner_reminder_recipients() returns exactly one address, on the domain rc-inventory.local, which is the seeded dev owner account on a domain that does not exist. A reminder sent today would be addressed to nobody, whatever the sender says. That closes at P2-13, where the real client accounts are created.
DEPENDENCY STILL UNMET INDEPENDENTLY OF ALL THE ABOVE: depends_on names P2-11, which is todo and parked behind P2-09 and P2-08 on andre. Clearing blocked_on would not have made this card eligible.

--- RESEND VERIFIED, OWNER CONFIRMED 2026-08-26 ---
ASK 1 IS ANSWERED. The Resend dashboard shows the domain VERIFIED. Confirmed by the owner in the dashboard on 2026-08-26. This terminal could not read it and still cannot: the key in the environment is a sending-only restricted key and GET https://api.resend.com/domains answers that it is restricted to only send emails. The owner report is the evidence, and it is corroborated by public DNS, which already showed all three records present and correctly placed: SPF TXT and MX both at send.rapidconstructmd.com, DKIM at resend._domainkey.rapidconstructmd.com.
ASKS 2 AND 3 MOVE TO THE P2-13 CHECKLIST rather than staying here. RESEND_FROM is unset in the production environment, so P2-10 still sends from the Resend onboarding address. owner_reminder_recipients() returns exactly one address and it is on rc-inventory.local, the seeded dev account on a domain that does not exist, so a reminder today is addressed to nobody whatever the sender says. Both are credential-and-account work at the handover, which is what P2-13 IS, and both are now tickable items on its checklist.
THE CARD STAYS blocked_on ivan. Not for those two any more, but because depends_on names P2-11, which is todo behind P2-09 and P2-08 on andre, and because the acceptance still needs a reminder email DELIVERED from a sender at the client domain. The domain half of this card is finished and verified; the delivery half cannot be proven until there is somebody to deliver to.

--- DEPENDENCY SEVERED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-019) ---
depends_on named P2-11 and no longer does. Connecting a domain and verifying that it serves over HTTPS has no dependency on security headers, an environment presence check, Romanian error pages or a console sweep. The edge was not wrong when it was authored: it encoded an ORDER, that domain work came last, at a time when that was the plan. The plan changed, Ivan did the DNS early, the verification passed, and the edge then held a finished piece of work behind a card parked three deep behind a third party. An ordering constraint that has outlived its ordering is a stale edge, and a stale edge is indistinguishable from a real one to everything that reads this board.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26, AND ONE CLAUSE OF THE ACCEPTANCE WAS WITHDRAWN IN WRITING ---
THE WITHDRAWN CLAUSE, QUOTED VERBATIM SO THE EDIT ADDS A RECORD RATHER THAN ERASING ONE. The acceptance read, in full: "URL CHECK: after Ivan connects the domain, `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" https://<client-domain>/` prints 200 over a valid certificate, and signing in from that host lands back on that same host. The clause naming the vercel.app host as the alternative is removed under ruling R-004: that host is not an entrypoint and is not what a redirect is measured against. PLUS RESEND DOMAIN VERIFICATION (added 2026-08-25 by ruling R-002): the Resend dashboard shows the client domain VERIFIED, and the reminder sender is switched off the Resend onboarding domain to the client domain. Proven by a reminder email delivered from a sender at the client domain."
WHAT WAS REMOVED AND WHY: the clause requiring that the reminder sender be switched off the Resend onboarding domain to the client domain, PROVEN BY A REMINDER EMAIL DELIVERED FROM A SENDER AT THE CLIENT DOMAIN. That work is no longer this card. It moved to P2-13 on 2026-08-26 as checklist items (e) set RESEND_FROM in the production environment and (f) create the real owner account and confirm owner_reminder_recipients returns it. Both are credential and account work at the handover, which is what P2-13 IS. An acceptance line that still demands proof of work another card now owns is stale in exactly the way ruling R-019 described the depends_on edge: indistinguishable from a real requirement to everything that reads the board.
THE PRECEDENT FOR CORRECTING RATHER THAN QUIETLY SATISFYING IT IS CRIT-14, which is in docs/LEARNINGS.md: when the acceptance and what can actually be checked disagree, the ACCEPTANCE is what gets corrected, in writing, with the old text preserved. The alternative was to ship on the dispatch instruction alone and leave the card carrying a clause nobody could ever run, which is the board lying about a commit that does not exist.
WHY THE EMAIL CANNOT BE PROVEN TODAY, IN ONE LINE: there is nobody to send it to. owner_reminder_recipients() returns exactly one address and it is on rc-inventory.local, a domain that does not exist. That is item (f) on P2-13.
RESEND STATUS IS OWNER CONFIRMATION, NEVER A MACHINE READ, and the card says so in both the acceptance and the evidence. The key in the environment is a sending-only restricted key and GET /domains still answers that it is restricted to only send emails. What corroborates the owner report is public DNS, where all three records Resend asks for are present and correctly placed. A verification flag this terminal cannot read is recorded as what it is.
CANONICAL IS www, which the card default left to Ivan and which he answered by pointing the 308 at www.
GATE G8 IS NOT FLIPPED BY THIS CARD. It is a launch gate condition and flipping it is a separate judgement about launch readiness, recorded on the gate rather than assumed from a card closing.

cards.title: Credential firewall flip before real data: the rotation checklist authored as a committed document and executed by Ivan.
cards.plain: Before any real Rapid Construct data goes in, the passwords used during the build are changed and the builder's direct access to the database is switched off. After this the system belongs to the business rather than to the workshop.
cards.question: DECISION NEEDED: execute the credential rotation checklist and tick every box in the committed document. CONTEXT: during the build, terminals held credentials in order to build. Before Rapid Construct puts real supplier data and real stock into the system, every credential a terminal ever held is rotated and the terminals stop holding any. This is the point where I lose access on purpose. Only Ivan can perform it: it requires the Supabase and Vercel dashboards. OPTIONS: (a) rotate everything on the checklist in one sitting, immediately before the client starts entering real data; (b) rotate progressively as each service finishes, which leaves a window where some old keys are still live and nobody can say which. RECOMMENDATION: (a). One sitting, one checklist, every box ticked in the committed document so the state is recorded rather than remembered. Do it after P2-12 and before P2-14, so Mihai's acceptance cycle is the first real data the system sees. IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: real client data would sit behind credentials that a build terminal once held. That is the one risk in this phase with no technical mitigation, only this checklist.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: the checklist document is committed and every box is ticked, proven by `grep -c "^- \[ \]" docs/RUNBOOK-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION.md` printing 0 while `grep -c "^- \[x\]" docs/RUNBOOK-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION.md` prints the full item count. An unticked box is an unfinished card. PLUS, ADDED 2026-08-31 BY R-072, THE CAPABILITY PRECONDITION AS ITS OWN TICKABLE BOX: docs/RUNBOOK-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION.md carries a box, ticked before any credential is rotated, confirming that every migration file under supabase/migrations/ is recorded as applied in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md. Machine-checkable by the same count the rest of this acceptance uses, because an unticked box is an unfinished card. THIRTEEN FILES ARE PENDING TODAY, 0013 to 0025, and P3-27 is the card that applies them. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 BY R-095: THE SENTENCE ABOVE READING 'THIRTEEN FILES ARE PENDING TODAY, 0013 to 0025, and P3-27 is the card that applies them' WAS TRUE ON 2026-08-31 AND IS FALSE NOW. Zero files are pending, the Pending section of docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md is empty, 0013 to 0027 are all recorded as applied, and P3-27 is shipped. THE BOX IS KEPT AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED INTO A STATEMENT OF FACT: it is a precondition to be re-checked on rotation day against whatever the highest migration number is then, not a note about wave 1. PLUS, ADDED 2026-09-02 BY R-095, A SECOND BOX NAMING THE THIRD GRANT: the runbook carries a box, ticked on rotation day, confirming that the migration-applier grant created by R-082 on 2026-08-31 is revoked along with the two grants section 8.7 already enumerates by id. Section 8.7 covers R-082 only by the blanket phrase 'reverting section 8', and a checklist that enumerates two grants and leaves the third to a blanket is a checklist that will revoke two. PLUS, ADDED 2026-09-02 BY R-095, A THIRD BOX FOR THE VERIFICATION THIS CARD MAKES IMPOSSIBLE: the runbook carries a box, ticked before any credential is rotated, confirming that card P3-35 has shipped or that the four phase 3 launch conditions it serves have been ruled unreachable by a dated ruling. This card removes the database connection those four conditions need, and after it lands no terminal can take the read.
cards.defaults: THE CHECKLIST IS A COMMITTED DOCUMENT WITH REAL CHECKBOXES, not a chat message. Ivan ticks boxes in the file and commits, so the completion state is in the repository rather than in someone's memory. ROTATE AT MINIMUM: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and VERCEL_TOKEN. Also listed for Ivan's decision: the Supabase anon key, the database password, MAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET, X-RC-Secret and RESEND_API_KEY, because each was handled during the build. REMOVE TERMINAL-HELD COPIES: local .env files, shell history entries, scratchpad files and any value pasted into a chat. The checklist names each location explicitly so none is forgotten. IVAN-ONLY FROM THEN ON: after the flip, no terminal holds a production credential, ever, for any reason. A card that needs one is blocked on Ivan instead. TEST DATA ROWS ARE MARKED CANCELLED, NOT DELETED, per the P2-07 convention. The checklist includes verifying that every seeded test row carries the cancelled flag before real data arrives. THE DOCUMENT NEVER CONTAINS A CREDENTIAL VALUE, only variable names, locations and steps. GRANT REVOCATION IS PART OF THIS CHECKLIST, ADDED BY RULING R-001 (2026-08-25). The checklist must carry these four items as tickable boxes, and P2-13 is not complete until all four are ticked: (a) revoke the EXECUTOR migration-apply grant by reverting CLAUDE.md section 8 to Ivan-only applies with no database connection from any terminal, which also revokes the single permitted read of /Users/ivan/rc-secrets/phase2.env; (b) rotate SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD; (c) rotate SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; (d) confirm no terminal-held copies of either remain, including .env.local, shell history and scratchpad files. The grant was given on the basis that the database holds zero real client data, and this card is the moment that stops being true. DEVIATION 5 OF THE CRITIC WAVE 1 REPORT IS A ROTATION LINE ITEM, ADDED BY RULING R-003 (2026-08-26): the dev account password was passed on a URL query string by the pre-CRIT-10 login form and is therefore recorded in the Vercel edge request logs for the production deployment. The checklist must carry it as its own tickable box: rotate the password of both dev accounts (owner@rc-inventory.local, manager@rc-inventory.local) before those accounts are retired, and treat the Vercel log retention window as the exposure period rather than assuming the fix removed the record. CRIT-10 stopped new leaks; it could not unwrite the ones already logged. TWO ITEMS MOVED HERE FROM P2-12 ON 2026-08-26, and the checklist must carry both as tickable boxes. (e) SET RESEND_FROM IN THE PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT to a sender at the verified Resend identity, which is the send. subdomain and not the root, for example a sender at send.rapidconstructmd.com. Until it is set, P2-10 sends from the Resend onboarding address even though the client domain is verified. (f) CREATE THE REAL OWNER ACCOUNT AND CONFIRM owner_reminder_recipients() RETURNS IT. Today that function returns exactly one address, on rc-inventory.local, which is the seeded dev account on a domain that does not exist, so a threshold reminder is addressed to nobody however correct the sender is. This card already retires the dev accounts; the addition is confirming the replacement is what the function returns.
cards.notes:
The card that hands the system over. Two halves: the executor authors the checklist document, Ivan executes it and ticks the boxes. The executor cannot execute it and must not try. Ordered after P2-12 and before P2-14 on purpose: the domain is live, the system is hardened, and the first real data to enter is Mihai's acceptance cycle, behind rotated credentials. BLOCKED ON IVAN AT AUTHORING TIME. The document half can be written and merged while blocked; the card ships only when the boxes are ticked.

--- RULING R-001 AMENDMENT 2026-08-25 ---
This card now also revokes the EXECUTOR migration-apply grant. The four revocation items are written into defaults above. The dev accounts created during the build (owner@rc-inventory.local, manager@rc-inventory.local) are retired here as well: real client accounts are created at this card, not before. A grant that outlives the condition it was granted under is how a temporary permission becomes a permanent one, so reverting CLAUDE.md section 8 is a checklist item and not a follow-up.

--- GATE CHANGE 2026-08-25 (ruling R-002) ---
Gate flipped from owner_merge to green_self_merge. owner_merge is retired on this board. This card now ships on the green quality check plus its own named acceptance spec passing. Defect review moves to the CRITIC at the wave boundary and to an optional owner batch review before the client demo, and neither is a merge gate.

--- RULING R-003 AMENDMENT 2026-08-26 ---
Deviation 5 of the CRITIC wave 1 report, the dev password recorded in the Vercel edge logs by the pre-CRIT-10 login form, is now a line item on this card's rotation checklist. Written into defaults above. It is a rotation item and not an incident card because the accounts it affects are dev accounts that this same card retires, and because there is no way to unwrite a log line: the only available action is to make the recorded value worthless, which is what rotation does.

--- DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-08-26 ---
depends_on gains P2-15. Deciding what the database should contain has to happen before every credential is rotated and the migration grant is revoked, because after this card nobody but Ivan can run anything against the database.

--- TWO ITEMS INHERITED FROM P2-12 2026-08-26 ---
The Resend domain is verified, confirmed by the owner in the dashboard on 2026-08-26, so P2-12 has answered its first ask. Its other two are credential-and-account work at the handover, which is what this card is, so they move here as checklist items (e) and (f) and are written into defaults above.
(e) RESEND_FROM is unset in production. (f) owner_reminder_recipients() returns one address on rc-inventory.local, a domain that does not exist. Neither is a defect in P2-10, whose logic is proven by four green acceptance cases; both are environment and account facts that only exist to be fixed at the handover.

--- RESEQUENCED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-024) ---
depends_on now names P2-15 alone, and blocked_on ivan is CLEARED for the same reason as on P2-15: this card is waiting on a card, not on a person, and it becomes an owner action again the moment P2-15 ships. Nothing about the checklist changes and nothing about who executes it changes.
THIS CARD IS THE CREDENTIAL FIREWALL, so it is ordered by the capability it removes and not by the calendar. It revokes the migration-apply grant, rotates SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and retires the dev accounts. Every card that needs any of those must ship first. Today that is P2-08a, which needs a migration, and everything downstream of it.

--- R-037, 2026-08-27: depends_on gains P2-08b ---
The credential firewall must not flip before the live extraction round trip has
run. P2-13 reverts CLAUDE.md section 8 to Ivan-only applies and rotates both
credentials; after it lands, no terminal can apply a migration. P2-08b is the
first real supplier document travelling the whole path against the frozen
contract, and it is the run most likely to find a mapping or a constraint the
seven synthetic cases did not. That finding is usually a migration. Flipping the
firewall first would leave it unfixable without the owner doing it by hand, and
would force the round trip to be re-run to prove the fix. The edge costs nothing
today: P2-13 already waits on P2-15.

This does not soften section 8.7. The grant still dies at P2-13. The ruling
fixes when P2-13 runs, not whether it does.

--- R-044, 2026-08-28: depends_on GAINS P2-19 ---
depends_on is now P2-15, P2-08b and P2-19.

THE CAPABILITY TEST, APPLIED AS DOCTRINE-TRIAGE SECTION 3 CHECK 3 WRITES IT. Ask what this card takes away, list every card that needs it, and make those the dependencies. This card takes away, permanently, the ability of ANY terminal to open a database connection: section 8.7 reverts CLAUDE.md section 8 to Ivan-only applies with no connection from any terminal.

P2-19 IS A CARD THAT NEEDS EXACTLY THAT CAPABILITY. Its own defaults say so in one sentence: "If the connection ever becomes available to a terminal, this card is worked unattended under CLAUDE.md 8.5 as a normal three-phase apply and stops being an owner action." After this card lands, that sentence can never come true. P2-19 becomes an owner action forever, on a repair that nobody has to make twice.

AND THE HANDOVER INHERITS THE DEFECT IF THE ORDER IS WRONG. P2-19 exists because the migration ledger says 0009 while the schema is at 0012. This card is the handover. Handing over a database whose own record of what is installed is three versions behind means the first tool that reads that record after the door closes tries to re-apply three migrations. P2-19's own IMPACT IF UNANSWERED line already says it: "P2-13's handover inherits it."

ORDERING COSTS NOTHING HERE. This card is already waiting on P2-15 and P2-08b and cannot start today either way.

--- depends_on NARROWED 2026-08-28 BY R-054, AND STATED IN FULL ---
Was ['P2-15', 'P2-08b', 'P2-19']. Is now ["P2-08b"], and that is the whole set. Written out because this card has carried three different dependency sets in two days and a reader should not have to reconstruct which is current.
P2-15 REMOVED: shipped 2026-08-28, accepted under R-048.
P2-19 REMOVED: retired under R-054, because Bash(psql:*) is permitted and the ledger correction is no longer an owner action.
P2-08b REMAINS and is now the only entry.

--- R-072, 2026-08-31: THE CAPABILITY EDGE THAT CANNOT BE AN EDGE ---
DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 3 check 3 says a card that REMOVES a capability must depend on every card that needs it. R-044 applied that test here on 2026-08-28 and added P2-19. R-054 removed P2-19 because it was retired, correctly, and the reasoning did not survive the removal. Since then the board split in two and the cards that need the capability landed on the other side of the split.
WHAT THIS CARD TAKES AWAY: the ability of ANY terminal to open a database connection or apply a migration, the single permitted secrets read, and, per section 8.7 and R-059, the self-merge grant in CLAUDE.md section 3.1 on every path.
WHAT NEEDS IT: P3-27, which IS the apply of the thirteen pending migration files, and every future phase 3 schema card. And the sixteen unshipped phase 3 cards are being built under the self-merge grant, which section 8.7 says returns every PR to Ivan when it goes.
THE EDGE CANNOT BE AUTHORED. docs/board/validate-board.mjs resolves depends_on against the cards of the board being validated and fails with "is not a card id on this board", so adding P3-27 here makes the validator red and CLAUDE.md section 2 makes that commit revertible. The precondition is therefore written into acceptance above, as a box in the runbook this card's acceptance already counts.
THIS IS ORDERING AND NOT A GRANT, in the words R-037 used for the same distinction: the grant still dies at P2-13, and the ruling fixes when P2-13 runs, not whether it does. Section 8.6's other two death conditions are untouched, first real client data being the one that waits for no card.

--- R-095, 2026-09-02: THE CAPABILITY EDGE, THIRD SWEEP RUNNING, AND TWO CORRECTIONS ---
WHAT THIS CARD TAKES AWAY is unchanged and is written out above under R-072: the database connection, the single permitted secrets read, the migration-apply grant, and the self-merge grant on every path.
WHAT IS NEW SINCE R-072 WROTE THAT LIST. R-082 created a FOURTH grant of exactly that class on 2026-08-31, the migration applier, after this card's capability clause was written. It is now named in acceptance as its own box rather than left to the blanket phrase in section 8.7.
WHAT IS NEW SINCE R-089 TRIED TO WRITE THE SAME CORRECTION. R-089 made this finding on branch triage/20260901-070544, which is open as pull request 143 and CONFLICTING, so it has never reached main. It is carried here under R-090's disposition of that pull request rather than waited for.
THE THIRD BOX IS THIS RUN'S OWN FINDING. R-093 re-audited the phase 3 gate and found four of its nine conditions short of nothing but a read-only verification against production, now that every migration is applied. P3-35 is that verification. This card takes away the connection it needs, so the ordering is a capability edge under section 3 check 3, and it goes into acceptance for the same reason every other one has: a cross-board depends_on makes the validator red.

cards.title: Mihai acceptance: one full cycle completed by Mihai himself on production, upload, confirm, arrival, outbound.
cards.plain: Mihai does one complete cycle himself on the live site: upload a delivery, confirm it, mark it arrived, and issue material out. This is the moment the system is either accepted or not.
cards.question: DECISION NEEDED: Mihai runs one full cycle himself on production, unassisted, and Ivan reports the outcome. CONTEXT: this is the phase 2 acceptance gate and the only card no terminal can close. The cycle is four steps in order: upload a real supplier document, confirm the extraction on the review screen, mark the resulting order arrived, then issue material outbound to a project. Unassisted means nobody drives the screen for him and nobody narrates the next click. OPTIONS: (a) Mihai runs the cycle alone with Ivan available but silent, which is what acceptance means; (b) Ivan walks him through it, which proves the system works for Ivan and proves nothing about Mihai. RECOMMENDATION: (a). Every place Mihai hesitates is a real defect in the product and becomes a REVIEW BATCH (IVAN) card, which is worth more than a smooth guided demo. IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: gate G9 stays fail and phase 2 does not close. Every other card can be green and the phase is still open, because the phase is finished when the client can run it, not when the tests pass.
cards.acceptance: NAMED REPORT: Ivan reports that Mihai completed all four steps himself on production, on a stated date. That report is recorded as this card's evidence, kind screenshot, with the date and the four steps named in the ref. Gate G9 flips on that report and on nothing else.
cards.defaults: UNASSISTED MEANS UNASSISTED. No screen sharing with narration, no terminal driving the browser, no click-by-click instructions. Ivan may be present to observe and to unblock a hard stop. REAL DATA, NOT SEEDED. Mihai uses one of his own supplier documents and his own products, because the failure modes of a real document are the point. EVERY HESITATION BECOMES A CARD in REVIEW BATCH (IVAN), even where Mihai completed the step. A step completed after ten seconds of searching is a defect that succeeded. PARTIAL COMPLETION DOES NOT FLIP THE GATE. Three of four steps is a fail with three cards attached, not a pass with a caveat. IF THE CYCLE FAILS the card stays blocked, the defects become cards, they are worked, and Mihai runs the cycle again. There is no version of this card that closes on anything less.
cards.notes:
The last card of phase 2. Gate is stakeholder: client acceptance at phase end, per the gate vocabulary carried from phase 1. Closes gate G9, which is the gate the whole phase exists to flip. BLOCKED ON CLIENT AT AUTHORING TIME, and it stays that way until the other thirteen cards are shipped, the domain is live and the credentials are rotated. Nothing about this card is buildable; it is a scheduled event with a written pass condition.

--- STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-31 BY R-072 ---
Was status todo with blocked_on client, which CLAUDE.md section 4 does not permit: a card with a person in blocked_on is a blocked card. This card's own notes said BLOCKED ON CLIENT AT AUTHORING TIME, so nothing about it changed except the field that reports it. It now sits in the BLOCKED ON PEOPLE lane under the client column, where the board Ivan reads shows it as what it is. Found by the DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 3 sweep, not by the P3-13 report, which never touched this card. No eligibility changed: a card with a non-null blocked_on was never eligible.

ELEVEN AND NOT NINE SINCE 2026-08-27: ruling R-033 required the selector to cover what the extraction lane creates, and that added two deletes, for extraction_draft_lines and extraction_drafts. An acceptance line that a corrected file fails is a broken acceptance line, so the literal moves with the file and the parser check is named alongside it, because the count alone says nothing about whether the eleven are the right eleven. OWNER HALF, which is what ships the card: Ivan runs the file on production and reports the phase 3 post-check grid, in which every count is 0 except `POST products remaining` and `POST MIXED left alone`. That grid is the evidence, kind journal.
cards.defaults: NOT A MIGRATION. The file lives under scripts/, never under supabase/migrations/, because it is not schema history and must not enter any apply path. NO TERMINAL EXECUTES IT, ever, including the executor holding the R-001 migration grant: CLAUDE.md section 8.6 is absolute on DELETE and this card does not weaken it. ONE TRANSACTION, so a partial cleanup is impossible. PRE-CHECK INSIDE THE TRANSACTION, so the counts the owner reads are the counts at delete time rather than a stale snapshot. CHILDREN BEFORE PARENTS, respecting every ON DELETE RESTRICT in the schema: status_history first because it is polymorphic and carries no foreign key, then batches, then the two line tables, then the two parents, then reminders, then products, then categories last and only when nothing still points at them. MIXED ORDERS ARE NEVER TOUCHED and are printed by reference at the end. THE FILE IS NEVER EDITED AFTER IT HAS BEEN RUN; a correction is a new file, same rule as a migration. NO CREDENTIAL VALUE appears in the file or in this card, only table and column names. TWO PRECONDITIONS ADDED 2026-08-27 BY RULING R-033, and this card is NOT OFFERED TO IVAN until both are met. (1) migration 0011 applied, because 0010 shipped a CHECK constraint that this script's delete from inbound_orders can violate through on delete set null, which would have failed with 23514 and rolled the whole file back in the SQL editor with the owner watching. SATISFIED 2026-08-27, journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md. (2) the selector corrected to cover the EXT-<slug>-<hex> products the extraction review lane creates, because today they survive the reset and the orders containing them are classified mixed and survive too, while the post-check still reports zero because it counts what the selector selected.

--- RATIFIED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-009) ---
This card is a ratified exception to cancelled-never-deleted, not a violation awaiting argument. The reason the convention exists is now stated: it protects EVIDENCE OF REAL BUSINESS EVENTS. An order placed, a batch arrived, an issue shipped are facts about the warehouse and are never deleted, only cancelled. E2E residue records no business event at all; it is contamination in a client production project, produced by a suite pointed at the wrong environment.
OPTION (c) IS DECLINED AND MUST NOT BE BUILT. The cancel-instead-of-delete variant written into this card question as an alternative is closed. It is not a fallback, not a safer first step, and not something to offer again. It stays quoted in the question because the question records what was asked, and R-009 records what was answered.
The card stays blocked_on ivan: R-009 settles what the card IS, not that it has been run. The nine statements still need the owner in the SQL editor.

--- SQL PARSED 2026-08-26, THE UNPARSED CAVEAT IS CLOSED ---
The notes above said: THE SCRIPT IS AUTHORED BUT UNPARSED, no PostgreSQL binary and no running Docker on this machine, so no parser has seen this SQL, and syntax is not proven. That is no longer true and the sentence is superseded rather than deleted. scripts/poc-free/parse-reset-sql.mjs parses the file with pgsql-parser, which is the real PostgreSQL grammar compiled to WebAssembly, so a parse there is the parse the server does. It needs no connection, no credential and no Docker, which is why it runs in CI on every push as the named step Parse the production reset SQL inside the quality job. It is a step and not a second job, because branch protection names exactly one check.
EIGHT CHECKS, all green: the file parses (18 statements, grammar 180004); exactly 9 DELETE statements; no statement kind outside the allowed set, so DeleteStmt is the only thing that can change a row; no TRUNCATE, DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, ALTER or GRANT by name; every one of the 9 deletes carries a WHERE clause; all 9 delete targets are inside the expected table set; all 4 working tables are TEMPORARY so nothing permanent is left behind; and one BEGIN first with one COMMIT last, so a partial run is impossible.
ONE HONEST DEVIATION FROM THE CHECK AS REQUESTED. The request was statement count is 9 and every statement is a DELETE. The file parses to EIGHTEEN statements and that is correct rather than a defect: it opens a transaction, builds four temporary tables that freeze the target set, prints a pre-check, runs the nine deletes, prints two post-checks and commits. Asserting every statement is a DELETE would fail a correct file, and the only ways to make it pass are to weaken the assertion or to gut the transaction and the checks that make the file safe. The assertion implemented is the one that carries the intent: every statement that CAN MUTATE DATA is a DELETE, there are exactly nine, and every other statement is from a short list of kinds that cannot change a row. An INSERT or an UPDATE fails check 3 as loudly as a TRUNCATE fails check 4.
EVERY CHECK WAS PROVED TO FAIL BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED, on mutated copies of the file: removing a WHERE clause fails check 5 naming the table it would have emptied; adding a TRUNCATE fails checks 3 and 4; retargeting a delete at public.profiles fails check 6; making a working table permanent fails check 7 naming its relpersistence; removing the COMMIT fails check 8; and appending invalid SQL fails check 1. A check that has only ever been seen passing has not been seen working.
THE CARD STAYS BLOCKED ON IVAN. Parsing proves the file says what the card says it says. It does not decide whether to run it, and it does not run it.

--- RESEQUENCED 2026-08-26 (ruling R-024) ---

It goes back to blocked_on ivan the moment its dependencies ship and the question is his again.

(1) APPLY MIGRATION 0011 BEFORE RUNNING THE RESET. 0010 shipped a CHECK
constraint on extraction_drafts that a referential action can violate: the

--- SELECTOR CORRECTED 2026-08-27, PRECONDITION 2 MET (ruling R-033) ---
BOTH PRECONDITIONS ARE NOW MET AND THE CARD IS OFFERED. status is blocked and blocked_on is ivan, which on this board is an owner ACTION and not a review.

WHAT THE OLD SELECTOR MISSED. It identified test data by one marker, products.sku like TEST-%, which was every test product when it was written and stopped being every test product the day the extraction review lane shipped. P2-09 creates a flagged product when an extracted line names something the catalogue does not have, shaped EXT-<slug>-<hex>. Those survived. One acceptance run left behind a product, an order, its lines and its history row, and the post-check still printed zero, because the post-check counts what the selector selected.

AND THE DRAFTS THEMSELVES, which nobody had looked for. extraction_drafts and extraction_draft_lines were created by migration 0008, after this file was authored, and nothing here had ever touched them. A product is in scope only when it sits on an order that a SEED DRAFT became, and a seed draft is one carrying the suite's own filename marker TEST-%, or attached to an order already in the delete set, or confirmed into one. The only false positive either marker can produce is a real supplier document named TEST-, which is exactly the exposure the TEST- SKU marker has always carried and is no larger.

cards.title: Untrack the generated build artefacts that dirty every working tree.
cards.plain: Tidying up so that leftover build files stop cluttering the project. Nothing Mihai sees changes.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run build && npx tsc --noEmit && git status --porcelain` prints NOTHING and exits 0. Today the same command prints two modified files after every build, which is the defect.
cards.defaults: TWO FILES, BOTH GENERATED: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and next-env.d.ts. Both are written by the toolchain on every build and typecheck, both are currently TRACKED, so every build dirties the working tree of every session in this repository. GITIGNORE THEM AND git rm --cached BOTH. --cached and never a plain rm: the files must stay on disk, because Next regenerates next-env.d.ts on the next build anyway and deleting tsconfig.tsbuildinfo only costs a slow first typecheck. NEXT ITSELF SAYS SO: next-env.d.ts carries the comment that it should not be edited, and the Next documentation lists it among the generated files. THE COST OF LEAVING IT is not cosmetic. A dirty tree after a build means every session must decide whether a modification is its own work or toolchain noise, and the failure mode is a session committing a build artefact or, worse, running git checkout -- on a file it should have kept. NOTHING ELSE IS UNTRACKED IN THIS CARD. .next/ and node_modules/ are already ignored; this is two files and no more.

evidence.ref: PR #37. Acceptance run on the branch after the fix was committed: npm run build, then npx tsc --noEmit exit 0, then git status --porcelain printed NOTHING. The same command sequence on the same branch BEFORE the fix printed two lines, M next-env.d.ts and M tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, which is the defect the card describes. git rm --cached removed both from the index and left both on disk; ls confirms both files still present after the commit.

cards.notes:
Authored 2026-08-26 in the same dispatch that carried rulings R-012 through R-016. Small, and it earns its card because it has cost time in every session that touched this repository: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and next-env.d.ts appear as modified after every build and typecheck, and each session has had to run git checkout -- on them before staging in order to keep them out of unrelated commits. That reflex is the danger, not the noise: the same reflex applied to a file that was genuinely edited discards real work.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
DEFAULTS APPLIED AS WRITTEN: both files gitignored, both removed with git rm --cached and never a plain rm, both still on disk afterwards, and nothing else untracked. .next/ and node_modules/ were already ignored.
PROVED RED FIRST. On this branch, before any change, npm run build and npx tsc --noEmit followed by git status --porcelain printed two lines: M next-env.d.ts and M tsconfig.tsbuildinfo. After the commit the same sequence prints nothing. The card is small enough that skipping the red run would have been tempting and would have proved nothing.
ONE MISTAKE MADE AND CORRECTED BEFORE PUSHING. The first commit staged only the two cached removals: .gitignore had been edited but never git added, so the commit removed the files from the index WITHOUT the ignore rules in place, and the acceptance came back with M .gitignore still outstanding. The acceptance caught it, which is the point of running the command rather than reasoning about it. Amended rather than fixed forward, because the branch was unpushed and a follow-up commit would have left a bisect-hostile state in history: one commit that untracks two generated files without ignoring them, which is the exact configuration that puts them straight back on the next build.
NO DEFECTS DISCOVERED beyond the one the card exists to fix, so nothing was appended to docs/LEARNINGS.md for this card.

cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `node scripts/poc-free/check-categories.mjs` exits 0. It asserts that docs/contracts/categories.json exists, carries exactly 18 entries, that every entry in the committed migration appears in it and vice versa, and that TEST-Categorie is NOT among them. PLUS MIGRATION JOURNAL: the three phases of CLAUDE.md 8.5 recorded in this card evidence, with the post-check showing public.categories holding the 18 seeded rows plus the untouched TEST-Categorie row, 19 in total. PLUS APPLY LOG: docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md exists and carries this apply as an entry with version, actor, UTC timestamp and both check outputs, which is the P2-11 requirement taking effect for the first time. PLUS RE-RUN: the migration is executed a second time in the same session and the post-check row count is UNCHANGED, which is what proves idempotent rather than claiming it.
cards.defaults: ROWS, NOT AN ENUM, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. An enum would make every rename a migration. These are rows so Mihai can rename an entry at P2-14 without a code change, which is what a WORKING DEFAULT means: the list is a starting vocabulary and not a specification. INSERT ONLY. NO DELETE, NO UPDATE, NO TRUNCATE anywhere in the migration, which also keeps it inside CLAUDE.md 8.6 and lets the executor apply it. IDEMPOTENT ON RE-RUN via on conflict on the existing categories_name_unique constraint, do nothing. A seed that fails on a second run is a seed nobody dares re-run. THE TEST-Categorie ROW IS NOT TOUCHED. Not renamed, not deactivated, not deleted, not merged. It belongs to P2-15 and to the owner decision recorded there, and a seed migration that quietly tidied it would be taking that decision on his behalf. sort_order IS SET EXPLICITLY, 1 through 18, in the order the list was given, because the column exists to control display order and leaving every row at the default 0 makes the order arbitrary. ROMANIAN WITH PROPER DIACRITICS, comma-below forms, per CLAUDE.md section 11. Altele IS LAST deliberately: a catch-all sorted into the middle of an alphabetical list reads as a category rather than as the fallback it is.

evidence.ref: PR #39. MIGRATION 0007 APPLIED BY EXECUTOR under ruling R-012, three phases per CLAUDE.md 8.5, full journal at docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md which this card also opens as the first entry required by P2-11. POST-CHECK: categories 19 rows, the 18 seeded at sort_order 1 to 18 all active with correct comma-below diacritics, TEST-Categorie untouched at sort_order 0 still carrying 305 products, 11 tables all RLS enabled, 41 policies in public, 6 enums, journal now 0001 to 0007. IDEMPOTENCY PROVEN NOT CLAIMED: the same file applied a SECOND time in the same session, clean exit, row count unchanged at 19, no duplicate names. PARSED BEFORE APPLYING with pgsql-parser: 3 statements, TransactionStmt InsertStmt TransactionStmt, 18 VALUES rows, on-conflict action ONCONFLICT_NOTHING. ACCEPTANCE: npm run check:categories exits 0 on 8 checks, and each of the 5 mutable ones was proved to FAIL on a mutated copy first: a hand-added entry, TEST-Categorie smuggled into the vocabulary, a migration entry never exported, a DELETE sneaked into the migration, and a sort_order drift.

cards.title: The account_manager may create products through the extraction confirm path only, always flagged needs_review. Direct catalogue creation stays owner-only.
cards.plain: The daily operator can add a product the first time a supplier mentions it, and it is flagged for the owner to check afterwards. Before this, their work stopped dead the first time a supplier sent something new.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0, with two new cases. (8) SIGNED IN AS THE ACCOUNT_MANAGER, not the owner: the manager uploads a document, confirms a draft whose line names a product the catalogue does not have, the confirm SUCCEEDS, and the product exists carrying the extracted name verbatim and needs_review true. Before migration 0012 that confirm was refused by products_insert. (9) THE BOUNDARY, AND THAT THE GRANT WIDENED RATHER THAN MOVED: the same account_manager is offered no direct creation control on the catalogue screen, and the OWNER still creates a product directly with needs_review false, which is the branch of the policy 0012 left untouched. PLUS the database-level proof, which no screen can give: the three products policies, dumped verbatim into docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md by the 0012 post-check, showing products_insert with its two branches and products_update still owner-only.
cards.defaults:
THE RULE GOES IN THE DATABASE, NOT IN THE APPLICATION. An application-level check is a check the next screen can forget; a row level security policy is enforced wherever the write comes from, including a hand-written request with a valid session. So this card is a migration plus its test, and the application changes only if the policy needs a helper to lean on.

WHAT MAKES THE TWO PATHS DIFFERENT, and it must be something the DATABASE can see, not something the application promises: a product created at confirm carries needs_review true. A product created from the catalogue screen carries needs_review false, because the owner filling the form is the review. So the policy is: an account_manager may INSERT a product only when needs_review is true; an owner may INSERT any product. That is checkable in a WITH CHECK clause and needs no new column.

NEEDS_REVIEW IS NOT EDITABLE DOWN BY AN ACCOUNT_MANAGER. Clearing the flag is the act of accepting the product into the catalogue, which is the owner's. products_update already checks is_owner() and stays as it is; this card does not touch it.

NO NEW ROLE, NO NEW COLUMN, NO NEW TABLE. The role enum is frozen at owner and account_manager by 0001 and the client has two people.

THE MIGRATION REPLACES A POLICY, which under ruling R-031 is permitted: DROP POLICY removes a rule about rows and no row. Quoted verbatim in the report, parsed with pgsql-parser, journalled.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-27 BY RULING R-032, which answers a question P2-09 surfaced and deliberately did not decide.

WHAT IS BROKEN TODAY. products_insert in migration 0001 checks is_owner(). An account_manager confirming a document that names a product the catalogue does not have is refused, in Romanian, at the moment of confirm. The account_manager is the operator who uploads supplier documents every day; the extraction lane exists to save that person typing, and it stops working the first time a supplier sends something new, which is the most ordinary thing a supplier does.

WHY THE GRANT IS NARROW. A product created at confirm is anchored to a document that was uploaded, fired, extracted and reviewed, and it arrives flagged for the owner to complete. A product created from the catalogue screen is anchored to nothing. Those are different acts and only the first is granted.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS CARD MUST NOT CREATE: an account_manager who can mint catalogue rows at will. The needs_review discriminator is what prevents it, because a row created by that role is always visibly unfinished and always waiting for the owner. If a future change makes needs_review editable by an account_manager, this grant becomes unlimited creation and must be re-ruled.

--- IN FLIGHT 2026-08-27, MIGRATION 0012 APPLIED ---
MIGRATION 0012 APPLIED under R-012, three phases, one transaction, journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md. The policy is now `is_owner() OR needs_review = true`, products_update is untouched and still owner-only, and anon still cannot insert at all.

THE PRE-CHECK NUMBER WORTH READING TWICE: products_flagged = 0. Not one product in the client's catalogue carries needs_review today, so this change grants nothing retroactively and touches no existing row. It only decides what may be inserted next.

THE DROP POLICY, quoted verbatim as R-031 requires:

cards.title: Login form submits natively before hydration and writes the password into the URL query string.
cards.plain: Fixed: the sign-in page could put a typed password into the web address, where browsers keep a history. Anyone with access to the machine could have read it later.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits 0 with two new cases added to that file. Case one: the login inputs carry no `name` attribute, asserted by `expect(page.locator('#password')).not.toHaveAttribute('name')` and the same for `#email`, so a native submit can serialise nothing. Case two: navigating to /autentificare with `waitUntil: 'commit'` and clicking the submit control before hydration completes never produces a navigation whose URL contains a `password` search parameter, asserted by listening to `framenavigated` across the whole attempt and requiring `new URL(u).searchParams.has('password') === false` every time. PLUS: `grep -n 'name="password"' components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` exits 1.
cards.defaults: REMOVE THE `name` ATTRIBUTES FROM THE EMAIL AND PASSWORD INPUTS. React state drives the request, so the names serve no purpose and their only effect is to serialise credentials into a native GET. `id` and `autoComplete` stay, because those are what a password manager reads. THE FORM ALSO STOPS BEING SUBMITTABLE BEFORE HYDRATION: track readiness in a `useEffect` and keep the submit control disabled until it runs, so a click that would be swallowed is visibly not-yet-ready instead of silently dead. That is the second half of this defect and shipping only the first half leaves the operator staring at a button that does nothing. DO NOT ADD A SERVER ACTION or move authentication to the server to solve this. The Supabase browser client has to set the session cookie in the browser, that is P2-02's decided shape, and rewriting it here is scope. DO NOT ADD `method='post'` as the fix: it stops the query-string leak but posts the credentials to a route that does not handle them, which trades a visible defect for a confusing one. NO COPY CHANGES beyond a disabled-state label if one is needed, and if one is needed it is Romanian.
cards.notes:
FOUND ON PRODUCTION, NOT REASONED ABOUT. `components/auth/LoginForm.tsx` renders `<form onSubmit={...} noValidate>` with no `action`, and both inputs carry `name="email"` and `name="password"`. Before React hydrates, the submit button is still a native `type="submit"` control, so a click performs the browser default: a GET to the current URL with every named input serialised into the query string. Reproduced against https://www.rapidconstructmd.com in 1 of 4 runs of the same script: the browser navigated to /autentificare?email=<email>&password=<password> and the password parameter matched the account password exactly, 32 characters, verified by comparison rather than by eye and never printed. Evidence: scratchpad critic-wave1/hydration.mjs, attempt 3. The same race was hit first by accident: a two-role sweep found the account_manager sitting on the login screen after a click that produced zero calls to /auth/v1/token and displayed no error, then succeeded on the third try (critic-wave1/mgr-login.mjs). WHY THIS IS THE TOP CARD OF THE WAVE. The password reaches the request line, so it lands in the browser URL bar, in browser history on a shared warehouse machine, in the Vercel edge access log, and in the Referer of anything the page fetches next. It is also a silent failure for the operator: no error, no spinner, nothing happened. TWO SECOND-ORDER NOTES. The other two forms in the repository, CategorySettings and ProductForm, share the pre-hydration dead-click behaviour but carry no `name` attributes, so they leak nothing into the URL; they are out of scope here and are named so the next reader does not have to re-derive it. And once this card ships, the leaked dev password should be treated as exposed and rotated, which is already a checkable item on P2-13.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-26 ---
Both halves of the defaults applied: the name attributes are gone from both inputs, and a hydrated flag set in a useEffect keeps the submit button disabled until React has attached, which also blocks Enter-key implicit submission. No server action was added and authentication was not moved to the server, per the defaults. No copy changed: the disabled state is carried by the existing disabled:opacity-60 class, so no new string was needed and none was invented. DEFAULTS APPLICATION LOGGED: the defaults did not say what to do about the two other forms in the repository, CategorySettings and ProductForm, which share the pre-hydration dead-click behaviour but carry no name attributes and therefore leak nothing. Treated as out of scope for this card rather than fixed quietly, per CLAUDE.md section 3, and recorded in docs/reports/critic-wave1.md instead. ONE THING THIS CARD DOES NOT DO: the dev password that was exposed into a production URL during the review is not rotated here. Rotation is already a checkable item on P2-13 and doing it here would strand the .env.local that every local test run reads.
