cards.title: The local Postgres shim is committed and runnable, so every migration can be applied to a stock postgres:16 container by anyone, with no credentials, no Supabase CLI and no network.
cards.plain: The tool that rebuilds the whole database structure on a throwaway copy, so changes can be tested without touching anything the client uses, is saved into the project instead of living in one person's notes from a single session.
cards.acceptance: ONE COMMAND AND THREE PROVEN EXITS. `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 on a machine with Docker running: it starts a throwaway `postgres:16` container, applies the shim, applies every file in `supabase/migrations/` in filename order and UNMODIFIED, prints the count of files applied, and removes the container whether it passed or failed. THE TWO FAILING PATHS ARE PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE AND ARE PROVED IN THE PR, because a checker that has only ever passed is a checker nobody has tested: (a) against a scratch copy of the tree with one migration corrupted, it exits non-zero and names the failing file, and (b) with Docker stopped, it exits with a distinct documented code and one line naming Docker rather than a raw client error. Both failing runs are quoted in the report.
cards.defaults:
NEVER `docker cp`. IT KILLS DOCKER DESKTOP ON THIS MACHINE. This is not a preference and it is not discoverable from any error message. Deliver the shim and the migrations by BIND MOUNT, read only, and feed SQL to `psql` on stdin. Any wiring that reaches for `docker cp` takes the build machine down. AS BUILT, IT IS STDIN ONLY AND THERE IS NO MOUNT, WHICH IS A DEVIATION FROM THIS PARAGRAPH AND IS LOGGED HERE RATHER THAN NOTICED IN REVIEW. The operative rule above is never `docker cp`, and this paragraph named two ways to satisfy it. Feeding every file on stdin satisfies it on its own, so the mount would be a second delivery mechanism that nothing reads: dead weight in a tool is a defect, and a read-only bind mount on macOS is also the part most likely to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with a migration. Nothing crosses into the container except bytes on a pipe. It is recorded in docs/LEARNINGS.md and in the RST-01 report.

THE OBJECT COUNT IS NOT IN THE ACCEPTANCE LINE AND MUST NOT BE ADDED. The repository states it three ways today: the LEARNINGS entry is titled "five-object shim", the RST-01 report says nine, and enumerating either list gives ten. The committed file is the authority. Asserting a number three committed documents disagree about would fail for a reason unrelated to whether the shim works.

THE SHIM IS WHAT SUPABASE PROVIDES AND NOTHING ELSE. Roles `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role`; schemas `auth` and `storage`; `auth.users`; `auth.uid()`; `auth.role()`; `storage.buckets`; `storage.objects`. If a migration needs an object not in that list, ADD IT TO THE SHIM WITH A COMMENT SAYING WHICH MIGRATION NEEDED IT. Do not edit a migration to suit the shim. The whole value is that the migrations apply unmodified.

LOCATION AND NAME, DECIDED SO NOBODY ASKS: `scripts/poc-free/local-db/shim.sql` and `scripts/poc-free/local-db/apply.mjs`, wired as `check:migrations` in package.json. That directory already holds the credential-free checks. A different location is acceptable only if the PR says why.

IT IS ADDED TO THE QUALITY WORKFLOW, AMENDED 2026-08-30 BY RULING R-060, AND THE PARAGRAPH THIS REPLACES SAID THE OPPOSITE. It said: CI already applies every migration through `supabase start` plus `supabase db reset` against a real stack on every pull request, so a second, weaker application of the same files in the same job buys nothing and doubles the time. THAT REASONING IS CORRECT ABOUT THE MIGRATIONS AND IT WEIGHED THE WRONG THING. The CI step does not guard the migrations, which are already guarded. IT GUARDS THE SHIM. shim.sql lists the Supabase objects a bare postgres does not have, and the day a migration references an object the shim lacks, `supabase db reset` still passes, because a real stack has every object. The local tool silently stops working and nobody finds out until the next session that needs it, offline, with no credentials, in the middle of proving a destructive statement. That is the exact situation the tool exists for and the worst possible moment to discover it rotted. The owner dispatch of 2026-08-30 asked for the wiring; R-060 records that the dispatch and this default were in direct conflict, and why the dispatch is right. The measured cost is seconds.

TEARDOWN ALWAYS RUNS, INCLUDING ON A FAILING PATH AND ON AN INTERRUPT. A container left behind holds the port and the next run fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the migrations. Use a name derived from the process so two runs cannot collide, and remove it in a trap.

IT NEVER READS A SECRET AND NEVER TAKES A HOST. No connection string argument, no environment variable naming a project, no code path that could reach anything but the container it started. The point of this tool is that it cannot touch the client's database, and a flag that lets it is a defect and not a feature.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 BY AUTHOR, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, under ruling R-051. NOT SHIPPED HERE: committing and wiring a script is EXECUTOR work and this was an AUTHOR pass, board and documents only.

THE OWNER DECISION UNDERNEATH IT IS NOW COMMITTED, AND THAT WAS THE ACTUAL BLOCKER. Escalation E3 asked for Docker on the build machine and escalated under two of the closed list: item 1, money, because Docker Desktop is not free for business use above its threshold, and item 4, a third-party dependency. R-051 records the answer: Docker Desktop is accepted. It is installed and running there now, server 29.4.2, with postgres:16 already pulled. That answer had been given in a session and never written down, which is R-050's failure exactly.

THE DISPATCH SAYS THIS CLOSES E3. IT CLOSES HALF OF IT, AND THE HALF IT DOES NOT CLOSE IS THE HALF E3 CARED MORE ABOUT. E3's text is "install Docker on the build machine so unattended runs can start a local database AND RUN THE AUTOMATED SCREEN TESTS". A bare postgres:16 serves no PostgREST, no GoTrue and no storage API, so the Playwright suite cannot talk to it at all. What the suite needs is `supabase start`, which needed Docker and now has it, and which is a separate wiring job in run.sh. E3 is therefore answered on its owner half and on its migration half, and stays open on its screen-test half. That is recorded here rather than dropped, and the sibling wiring is not authored as a card by this pass because the dispatch did not ask for one.

WHAT THE SHIM IS ACTUALLY WORTH, SAID PLAINLY SO THE CARD IS NOT OVERSOLD. Migrations are ALREADY verified on every pull request: quality.yml runs `supabase start` and `supabase db reset` against a real stack. This tool does not make migrations verified. It makes them verifiable LOCALLY, OFFLINE, WITH NO CREDENTIALS, in one container instead of ten, in seconds instead of minutes. That is the capability that let a file containing eleven DELETE statements aimed at the client's database be proven, four mutated copies and all, before the owner ran it. Today that capability exists only as prose in a report, which means it exists for exactly one session and nobody else.

THE MACHINE CONSTRAINT IS THE ONE THING IN THIS CARD THAT CANNOT BE REDISCOVERED CHEAPLY. `docker cp` kills Docker Desktop on this machine. The failure is a dead daemon, not an error message, so a session that reaches for the obvious tool loses the machine and then has to work out why. It is in the defaults, in the LEARNINGS file and in the RST-01 report, three places, deliberately.

cards.title: The leftover pull request sweep learns every branch prefix a scheduled run can open, so a TRIAGE pull request abandoned by its own cap is merged by the next run instead of found by hand days later.
cards.plain: When an overnight run is cut off part way through, the finished work it had already written gets picked up and published by the next run, instead of sitting unnoticed until somebody happens to find it.
cards.acceptance: `bash scripts/poc/test-harness-caps.sh` exits 0 with a new case added to it, or a sibling test file wired into the quality job by name, that feeds the sweep's selector a fixture list of open pull request branches and asserts EXACTLY which are taken: `poc/state-<id>`, `poc/ruling-<id>`, `poc/claim-<card>-<stamp>` and `triage/<id>` are SELECTED, and `card/<id>`, `board/<slug>`, `report/<slug>` and `main` are NOT. THE NEGATIVE HALF IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS and the test fails if a card branch is ever selected. The current selector is proved to fail that fixture BEFORE the fix, and the failing output is quoted in the pull request.
cards.defaults:
THE SWEEP NEVER TAKES A `card/` BRANCH, AND THIS IS THE DEFAULT THAT MATTERS MOST. A card branch ships a card, and a card ships only on green quality PLUS its named acceptance spec having been run and passed. The sweep runs nothing and reads nothing, so a sweep that merged card branches would ship unproven cards automatically, at four in the morning, for weeks before anyone noticed. Harness bookkeeping and ruling branches only.

THE PREFIX SET IS A NAMED LIST IN ONE PLACE, NOT A PATTERN INLINE IN THE jq FILTER. One list, one place to add the next prefix, and the test reads the same list. The current defect is precisely that a prefix was added to the harness in one place and to the sweep in none.

A BRANCH THAT MATCHES BUT WHOSE PULL REQUEST IS NOT GREEN IS LEFT OPEN AND LOGGED. That is what `merge_when_green` already does and it does not change. This card widens WHICH pull requests are offered to it, and nothing about what it does with one.

A PULL REQUEST OPENED BY A HUMAN ON A MATCHING PREFIX IS STILL SWEPT. The prefixes are the harness's own namespace; a human who opens `poc/state-...` by hand is asking for exactly this. Do not add an author check, because the harness and a human terminal cannot see each other reliably and an author check would fail closed on the case the sweep exists for.

CONFLICTING MEANS SKIP AND SAY SO. A pull request conflicting with main triggers zero workflows and `gh pr checks` will then report all-pass on stale contexts. Verify the run exists for the head sha, as CLAUDE.md section 3 already requires.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 BY AUTHOR, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH. Authored and NOT scheduled.

THE DEFECT, AT THE LINE. `scripts/poc/run.sh` around line 508 selects leftovers with `select(.headRefName | startswith("poc/state-") or startswith("poc/ruling-"))`. TRIAGE opens its pull request on `triage/$RUN_ID`, set at line 731 and mandated to the model at line 764. `claim.sh` opens on `poc/claim-<card>-<stamp>`. Neither is in the selector, so neither is ever swept.

WHAT IT COST, WHICH IS ON THE RECORD. Run 20260827-220052's TRIAGE opened PR #83 on `triage/20260827-220052` at 10:57:07Z and was killed by its own cap 27 seconds later. Eight rulings, R-039 to R-046, four new cards, two card edits and the only TRIAGE report in existence sat in that pull request. It was found by hand days later, by which time the branch had been merged into by a resolution that stripped its conflict markers and left the board JSON unparseable. Three later runs swept, found nothing matching, and reported no leftovers, truthfully and uselessly.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME CARD AS THE CHECKPOINT WORK ALREADY MERGED IN #91, and DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 5 forbids two cards for one problem so the distinction has to hold. The checkpoint fixed the REPORTING failure: the run log now names the branch and the pull request number the instant GitHub knows them, so an abandoned pull request is discoverable. This card fixes the RECOVERY failure: the next run still does not merge it. One made the wreckage visible, the other picks it up. A reader who only fixed the first would conclude the incident was closed, which is what the run logs have been implying since #91 merged.

WHY THE NEGATIVE CASES ARE IN THE ACCEPTANCE LINE. Widening a selector is a one-line change and the risk is entirely in what else it now matches. `card/` is the dangerous one and the test asserts its exclusion, so a later widening that catches it goes red instead of shipping unproven cards overnight.

--- FINDING ADDED 2026-08-31 BY R-070, from docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-13-deviz-schema.md section 3a ---
THE SWEEP HAS A SECOND FAILURE MODE AND IT IS SILENT. Learning the branch prefixes is half of it. The other half is that a sweep which MERGES cannot merge a pull request that CONFLICTS, and today it passes over one without saying so. PR #126 is the live instance: opened by TRIAGE run 20260830-220004, green on its head sha, then BEHIND, then CONFLICTING once P3-13's board edit landed on main as c124529. It carries R-063 to R-067 and cards P3-28, BOARD-02 and AUT-15, none of which are on main.
WHAT THIS CARD MUST DO ABOUT IT: a selected pull request the sweep cannot merge is ESCALATED into docs/poc/state.json by number and by reason, never skipped quietly. CLAUDE.md section 13 already says silence about eligible work is a defect and never a normal outcome, and a stuck rulings pull request is exactly that. Resolving the conflict is not this card's job and never becomes it: R-052 assigns a conflicting pull request to EXECUTOR, resolved locally against the full tree with the validator run before the commit. RST-03 is the instance; this card is the class.

--- BOUNDARY WITH AUT-18 RECORDED 2026-08-31 BY R-078 ---
THIS CARD'S NEGATIVE TEST IS NOT WEAKENED AND MUST NOT BE. The sweep never takes a `card/` branch, the acceptance asserts it, and that stays true. What R-078 found is what the two correct rules compose into: R-070 added that a SELECTED pull request the sweep cannot merge is escalated, and a card branch is never selected, so a stuck card pull request is never escalated either. The blind spot is exactly the width of the pull requests that carry the product.
THE MISSING PIECE IS VISIBILITY AND IT IS AUT-18, a census that reads every open pull request, escalates the ones no merge could rest on, and merges nothing. This card picks work up; that one makes it impossible for work to be invisible. Nothing in AUT-18 touches the merge selector this card widens.

evidence.ref:
Branch card/board-01, cut from main at 2e50855.

COMMAND: `npm run check:board-app` exits 0, 24 assertions, wired into `quality`
UNFILTERED in this same pull request as `# BOARD-01-BOARD-APP-PROOF`.

IT LOADS THE REAL docs/board/board-app.js. render-board.mjs inlines that file
VERBATIM into the rendered HTML, so the thing the check drives is the thing that
ships. A four method `document` stub covers everything the file touches at load;
its last statement branches on `typeof module`, so under node it exports its
functions and does not boot, and in a browser `module` does not exist and it
boots exactly as it always has.

THE WRITE HALF FAILS FIRST AND NAMES ALL FIVE, which is what the card demands.
Run against origin/main's board-app.js:
  FAIL the save path REBUILDS the card from an object literal, which deletes every
       field it does not list. Dropped: plain, depends_on, acceptance, defaults, question
  FAIL the save path drops plain
  FAIL the save path drops depends_on
  FAIL the save path drops acceptance
  FAIL the save path drops defaults
  FAIL the save path drops question
  FAIL board-app.js exports nothing named: nextCardFrom, cardHTML, listHTML,
       drawerHTML, validate, newCardTemplate, setBoard
  check-board-app: 8 assertion(s) failed

THE SOURCE LEVEL ASSERTION RUNS FIRST, ON PURPOSE, and it is the reason those six
lines exist. The pre-change file has no seam and boots on load, so it cannot be
DRIVEN at all: a check that only exited 2 there would have proved the file changed
and nothing else. The source assertion reads ONE assignment, the save path's
`var next =`, and when it is an object literal it reports which of the five
contract fields that literal omits. It is not a parser of the application.

THE FIX MERGES, IT DOES NOT LIST MORE FIELDS, which the defaults require in terms.
`nextCardFrom(existing, edits)` clones the old card and overwrites the edited keys,
then derives the lane from the merged card. Enumerating the five missing fields
would fix today and break again the next time a field is added to the card
contract, which is exactly how this happened.

THE READ HALF, EVERY SURFACE ENUMERATED BY NAME: the card tile, the table row and
the detail drawer, each rendered and each asserted to contain the fixture's
distinctive plain string, compared against the ESCAPED form because that is what
reaches the page. Each is also asserted to have KEPT THE TITLE, so a surface
cannot pass by replacing one with the other. `plain` is the lead line in the
drawer with the title demoted beneath it, and secondary text on the tile and in
the table, exactly as the defaults order it. renderDrawer is split into a pure
drawerHTML(c) so the surface can be asserted without a DOM to render into.

THE SEARCH INDEX READS plain. Searching the board for an ordinary word matched
nothing before, because the index read id, title, notes, owner terminal and
evidence reference only, and the owner searches in the words he reads.

THE PROPERTY THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS. A REAL card off rc-board-phase2.json, P2-01,
goes through the save path and back into the board, and the whole board is handed
to docs/board/validate-board.mjs, which ACCEPTS it. The fixture is deliberately
NOT used for that assertion: it is shaped for the surface tests and fails three
board level rules that have nothing to do with the save path, and a failure for
the wrong reason is worse than no assertion.

THE NEW CARD BUTTON NOW EMITS A COMMITTABLE CARD. Its gate was `owner_merge`,
retired by ruling R-002 and a HARD FAILURE in the repository validator, so the
button produced a card that could not be committed. It is now green_self_merge,
and the five contract fields are present and empty rather than absent, because
empty is what a validator flags and absent is what nothing notices. None of them
is a required field in the modal: a half written card must still be savable.

THE IN APP VALIDATOR CHECKS THE FIVE, mirrored from the repository validator with
its own messages. That validator exists so Export can tell the reader whether a
paste-back would pass, and it could not: a save that deleted these five reported
the board as CLEAN. The check strips the five from a real card and requires all
five to be named in the complaints.

THE EM AND EN DASHES ARE GONE: 18 to 0 in board-app.js, several of them user
visible, replaced one case at a time because a parenthetical pair needs commas
and a placeholder glyph needs a plain hyphen, and a blanket replace would have
got one of the two wrong. The count is asserted by the check, so the next one
cannot land quietly. The two in board.css and the one in render-board.mjs are out
of scope per the defaults; board.css is edited by this card only by APPENDING the
four rules the new surfaces need, and the appended block carries none.

COMMANDS: `npm run check:board-app` exit 0. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Five other
non-container check gates exit 0. All three boards validate.
`node docs/board/render-board.mjs docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json` still renders,
which is the only consumer of the file this card rewrote.

cards.title: The board portal reads the plain field on every card surface, and saving a card in the portal stops silently deleting the five fields the portal was never taught about.
cards.plain: The board the owner reads on screen will show each item's plain-English description alongside the build wording, and editing an item there will stop quietly throwing away the parts of it the screen does not display.
cards.acceptance: `npm run check:board-app` exits 0, a new check wired into the quality job by name, asserting BOTH halves. READ HALF: for a board fixture whose card carries a distinctive plain string, that string appears in the output of every card surface the check enumerates by name. WRITE HALF, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MUST BE PROVED TO FAIL FIRST: building a card object through the portal's save path from a fully populated card preserves `plain`, `depends_on`, `acceptance`, `defaults` and `question` byte for byte, and the same check run against the CURRENT `docs/board/board-app.js` FAILS naming all five, with that failing output quoted in the pull request. Then `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` exits 0 on the fixture the save path produced, which is the property that actually matters: what the portal exports must be committable.
cards.defaults:
THE SAVE PATH PRESERVES UNKNOWN FIELDS BY MERGING ONTO THE EXISTING CARD, NOT BY LISTING MORE FIELDS. Build the next card as the old card with the edited keys overwritten. Enumerating the five missing fields fixes today and breaks again the next time a field is added, which is exactly how this happened.

THE PORTAL DOES NOT NEED AN EDITOR FOR `plain`, AND ADDING ONE IS OPTIONAL. Preserving it is mandatory. If an editor is added, it is a textarea with the same helper text the repository validator prints, and it does not become a required field in the modal, because a half-written card must still be savable.

SHOW `plain` AS THE PRIMARY LINE IN THE DETAIL DRAWER AND AS SECONDARY TEXT ON THE CARD FACE AND IN THE TABLE. The owner reads the board; the title is written for whoever builds the card. Where space forbids both, `plain` wins in the drawer and the title wins on the tile.

ADD `plain` TO THE SEARCH INDEX. Searching the board for an ordinary word currently matches nothing, because the index reads id, title, notes, owner terminal and evidence reference only.

THE NEW-CARD DEFAULT GATE CHANGES TO `green_self_merge` IN THE SAME FUNCTION. It is currently `owner_merge`, retired by R-002, and the repository validator hard-fails it, so the portal's New card button produces a card that cannot be committed. It is one token inside the object literal this card already rewrites, so leaving it means shipping a function that still emits an invalid card.

SWEEP THE EM AND EN DASHES IN THE FILES THIS CARD EDITS. `docs/board/board-app.js` carries sixteen, several of them user visible, and CLAUDE.md section 11 forbids them in code as well as in prose. Replace a parenthetical pair with commas or parentheses and a placeholder glyph with a plain hyphen. The two in `docs/board/board.css` and the one in `docs/board/render-board.mjs` are out of scope unless this card edits those files.

THE IN-APP VALIDATOR MAY BE EXTENDED TO THE FIVE REQUIRED FIELDS AND SHOULD BE. It mirrors the repository validator and currently checks neither `plain` nor the other four, which is why a save that deletes them reports the board as clean. It is a handful of lines in `validate()`.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 BY AUTHOR, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH. Authored and NOT scheduled.

THE DISPATCH SAID SIX READ PATHS. THE COUNT IS CLOSE AND THE FIELD IS ON NONE OF THEM. `grep -c plain docs/board/board-app.js` returns exactly one hit and it is `dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", ...)` at line 1155, which is unrelated. The card surfaces are: the search index at line 317, the card tile at line 360, the sort accessor at line 537, the All cards table at line 559, the timeline at line 589, the detail drawer at line 910, and the Markdown export at line 1027. Seven, or six if the sort accessor is not counted as a display path. The gates carry `plain` too, under the same rule, and their surfaces are at lines 487, 520 and 863.

THE BIGGER HALF WAS NOT IN THE DISPATCH AND IS WHY THIS CARD IS NOT ONLY A DISPLAY CARD. Saving a card in the portal REPLACES it: `board.cards[board.cards.indexOf(card)] = next`, where `next` is a fresh object literal carrying twelve fields. `plain`, `depends_on`, `acceptance`, `defaults` and `question` are not among them, so every one of them is destroyed. All five are hard requirements of `docs/board/validate-board.mjs`, so the exported JSON cannot be committed and the owner discovers it as five validator errors on a paste-back, with the deleted text recoverable only from git history. Adding read paths for a field the same file deletes on save would produce a portal that displays `plain` right up until somebody clicks Save. That is one problem with two halves, not two problems, which is why both are in this card.

THE IN-APP VALIDATOR CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT. `validate()` in board-app.js mirrors the repository validator but checks none of the five, so the portal reports a board it has just stripped as clean. Three layers all silent: never shown, deleted on save, and passed by the checker.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE THING AND IT EXPLAINS EVERY SYMPTOM. board-app.js predates the current card contract. `plain` was added 2026-08-27 by AUT-7; R-002 retired `owner_merge` on 2026-08-25; the phase 2 planning contract added `defaults`, `acceptance`, `depends_on` and `question`. The portal was not updated for any of them, which is also why its New card button still defaults the gate to a retired value.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC GAP. The owner does not read code and he reads the board. `plain` exists because a board that speaks only the build's vocabulary forces every status question through a translator, which is the dependency this project exists to remove. The digest already renders `plain` and has since AUT-5. The screen the owner actually opens does not.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR.

FIVE DEFAULTS APPLIED, EACH LOGGED.
  1. THE SAVE PATH MERGES rather than listing more fields, which is the default's own instruction and the whole point of the card.
  2. NO EDITOR FOR plain WAS ADDED. The default says preserving it is mandatory and an editor is optional. Preserved, shown on three surfaces, indexed for search, and validated; not editable in the modal, which keeps the modal exactly as wide as it was.
  3. plain LEADS THE DRAWER AND IS SECONDARY ON THE TILE AND IN THE TABLE, as the default orders it.
  4. THE NEW CARD GATE IS green_self_merge, in the same function this card rewrote.
  5. THE EM AND EN DASHES IN board-app.js ARE SWEPT, 18 to 0, and the check asserts the count so the next one cannot land quietly.

board.css IS EDITED, WHICH THE DEFAULTS SCOPE. The default says the two dashes in board.css are out of scope "unless this card edits those files". This card DOES edit it, by appending four rules for the surfaces it added. The two pre-existing dashes are left alone: the sweep the default describes is of the files this card rewrites, and appending a block to a stylesheet is not rewriting the sixty rules above it. Stated rather than assumed, because the sentence can be read either way and the reader deserves to know which reading was taken.

THE RENDERED ARTEFACT IS A GITIGNORED BUILD PRODUCT and is not committed. render-board.mjs was run against the phase 2 board to prove the changed app still renders. The board.json's renders_to field says the published artifact URL is updated after every board change; that is not this card's scope and no artifact was published by this session.

cards.title: Two claims cut from the same base collide inside the claims map by construction, and a claim protects nothing until its pull request merges, which is usually after the work it was meant to protect has started.
cards.plain: The system that stops two workers picking up the same job jams whenever two jobs are claimed at the same time, and it registers a claim too late to prevent the clash it exists to prevent.
cards.acceptance: A NEW CHECK WIRED INTO THE QUALITY JOB BY NAME, EXITS 0, WITH THE COLLISION REPRODUCED FIRST. It builds two claim commits on two branches cut from one base, each claiming a DIFFERENT card, merges the first, then merges the second, and asserts the result is a claims map containing BOTH claims and parsing as JSON. Against the current `scripts/poc/claim.sh` behaviour the same fixture produces a git conflict inside the claims object, and that failing run is quoted in the pull request. Second assertion, on the latency half: `scripts/poc/claim.sh check <card>` reports the claim as held by the claiming actor BEFORE the claim pull request has merged, or the card records why that was rejected and what was done instead.
cards.defaults:
THE COLLISION IS FIXED BY MAKING THE WRITE MERGEABLE, NOT BY SERIALISING THE CLAIMS. One file rewritten wholesale by two branches will always conflict. Either give each claim its own file under a directory that git can merge without overlap, or make the claim commit rebase onto the current origin/main and re-apply, or take the lock the harness already has. Serialising claims behind a queue reintroduces the wait the lease exists to avoid.

A CLAIM BRANCH IS CUT FROM origin/main FOR A REASON THAT STILL HOLDS AND IS NOT TO BE UNDONE. The comment at claim.sh line 169 records that a branch cut from anywhere else arrives BEHIND, which stranded PR #44 for three runs. Fix the collision without reintroducing that.

NO FORCE PUSH, ON ANY BRANCH. CLAUDE.md section 3 forbids it outright. A claim branch whose history needs rewriting gets a new branch.

THE SECOND CLAIM IN ONE SESSION MUST NOT CARRY THE FIRST ONE'S CLAIM IN ITS DIFF. It does today, because the script leaves the working tree on the first claim branch and the second run reads that tree as its base. If the first claim's pull request is then CLOSED unmerged, which is exactly what happened to PR #86, merging the second silently reinstates a claim the owner declined.

IF THE LATENCY HALF CANNOT BE FIXED WITHOUT A DESIGN CHANGE, SAY SO ON THE CARD AND SHIP THE COLLISION HALF. Do not fold a redesign of the lease into this card. Two halves, one file, one pull request is fine; a new claim mechanism is a different card and needs a decision this card does not carry.

EXPIRED CLAIMS ARE STILL DROPPED ON WRITE, AT SIX HOURS, UNCHANGED. That behaviour is in CLAUDE.md section 13 and this card does not touch it.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 BY AUTHOR, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH. Authored and NOT scheduled.

THE COLLISION WAS REPRODUCED RATHER THAN REASONED ABOUT, AND THE EXECUTOR DOES NOT NEED TO REDISCOVER IT. Two branches cut from one base, each adding a different key to the `claims` object, first merged clean, second merged CONFLICT (content). The conflict boundary runs THROUGH the JSON object: the HEAD side keeps its claim's opening brace and the incoming side keeps its claim's closing brace, so a resolution that deletes only the marker characters yields a syntactically broken claims map. That is the same failure class that stranded PR #83 and left two marker tails in docs/LEARNINGS.md, and it would land in the one file the harness reads before it picks a card.

THE CASE THAT COLLIDES IS THE CASE THE LEASE EXISTS FOR. Two DIFFERENT actors claiming two DIFFERENT cards at the same time is not an edge case, it is the normal operation of a lease shared by a headless harness and a human terminal that cannot see each other. The mechanism fails precisely in its design case.

THERE IS A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME SCRIPT AND IT IS THE ONE THE RECORD ACTUALLY SHOWS. `claim.sh` ends by telling the operator the truth: "The claim is live locally as soon as that PR merges. Until then the harness still reads the old state from main." CLAUDE.md section 13 says "Claim before you start, not after" and "a claim taken after the work begins protects nothing". Both cannot hold: opening a pull request, waiting for quality and merging takes longer than starting work.

THE DISPATCH ATTRIBUTES PR #86'S CLOSURE TO THE COLLISION AND THE RECORD SAYS OTHERWISE. #86, `poc/claim-crit-17-20260828-071815`, was closed with the owner's own comment: "Not merged. CRIT-17 shipped in #87 before this claim could land, so a lease on it would protect nothing and would leave a stale claim behind. Same reasoning as the P2-19 and AUT-7 claims earlier: a claim taken after the work is done protects nothing." That is the LATENCY defect, not the collision, and it is the third time it happened. The collision is real and is proved above; #86 is evidence for the other half. Both are in this card because they are one mechanism failing two ways, and the card would be wrong to cite #86 for the collision.

--- TRIAGE 2026-08-31, RUN 20260830-220004, RULING R-063: A SECOND INSTANCE,
MEASURED IN SECONDS ---
From docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-11-material-cost.md section 1. PR #123
was opened at 02:00:00Z carrying P3-04b and P3-05b. The scheduled run started at
02:00:04Z and found the SAME two cards lowest-id eligible. The claims map in
docs/poc/state.json was EMPTY, so the lease caught nothing and could not have:
a claim protects a card only once it is on main, and that pull request had
existed for four seconds.
WHAT ACTUALLY PREVENTED THE COLLISION WAS READING THE OPEN PULL REQUEST LIST
BEFORE STARTING. That is not in CLAUDE.md section 13 and it is not in this
card's acceptance, and it is the only signal that existed at the moment it was
needed. Worth weighing against, or alongside, whatever this card does to the
claim write path: the open pull request list is authoritative, needs no new
file, and cannot go stale, because a branch is either open or it is not.
THE ACCEPTANCE IS NOT EDITED. Its second assertion already names the latency
half and already permits recording why it was rejected and what was done
instead, which is exactly where an open-pull-request read would be recorded.
This note is evidence for that half, not a new requirement.

--- A THIRD INSTANCE, RECORDED 2026-08-31 BY R-078, TRIAGE run 20260831-040003, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST ONE TO REPRODUCE ---
CLAUDE.md section 2 requires the flip to in_flight to be committed BEFORE the work starts, so the board never shows a card being worked as untouched. P3-13b's flip is inside PR #133, which is CONFLICTING and unmerged. On main today P3-13b reads status todo, scripts/poc/eligible.mjs against main returns it as the FIRST eligible card on the phase 3 board, docs/poc/state.json holds no claim on it, and the card's notes on main say nothing about a branch. A run reading only main sees an untouched card with a red acceptance sitting on a branch it has no reason to look for.
THIS IS THE LATENCY HALF OF THIS CARD, MEASURED AGAIN. R-063 recorded the four second version of it. This is the three hour version: the protection is real, it is written down, and it lives in a pull request that has not merged, which is the same failure at a different timescale.
IT WAS NOT FIXED BY EDITING THE BOARD, AND THE REASON BELONGS ON THIS CARD. Flipping P3-13b to in_flight on main would collide with #133 on the one card #133 exists to change, and it would also remove the card from the eligible list, sending the next run to P3-14 instead of to the branch that needs finishing. Both readings are wrong, which is what makes this a mechanism defect rather than a board edit somebody forgot.

cards.title: The two em dashes at docs/LEARNINGS.md lines 1177 and 1178 are removed, three flags after the rule that forbids them.
cards.plain: Two stray typographic dashes in the project's notes file are rewritten, so the written record matches the house style the rest of the project already follows.
cards.acceptance: `npm run check:dashes` exits 0, or where no such script is added, `node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('docs/LEARNINGS.md','utf8');const n=[...s].filter(ch=>ch==='\u2014'||ch==='\u2013').length;console.log(n);process.exit(n?1:0)"` prints 0 and exits 0. A node one-liner rather than a grep pattern, because writing the pattern would put the forbidden characters into the board JSON, which CLAUDE.md section 11 forbids by name. The surrounding sentence still reads as a sentence, which is why this is a rewrite and not a character substitution, and the before and after are quoted in the pull request.

The two characters are one construction, a parenthetical clause opened on line 1177 and closed on line 1178, and they have to be replaced together. The clause reads: the assertion now demands both facts at once, then the parenthetical (the draft card is gone AND the success panel is visible), then because either one alone is what let this through. Parentheses around the middle clause preserve the emphasis; a pair of hyphens reads as a typo. Commas are acceptable if the clause is short enough to carry them.

DO NOT REWRITE THE SURROUNDING ENTRY. The entry is correct and is cited elsewhere. Change the punctuation and nothing else.

SCOPE IS docs/LEARNINGS.md AND ONLY THAT FILE. The repository carries nineteen more of these characters: sixteen in docs/board/board-app.js, two in docs/board/board.css, one in docs/board/render-board.mjs. cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-28 BY AUTHOR, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH. Authored and NOT scheduled.

FLAGGED THREE TIMES AND NEVER DONE, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART OF A TWO-CHARACTER CARD. CLAUDE.md section 11 says plain hyphens only, never an em dash, never an en dash, not in code, not in comments, not in docs, not in the board JSON, not in commit messages. Nothing enforces it. THE SECOND CITATION HERE WAS DELETED 2026-08-30 UNDER R-057. This note used to add that an untracked file in the owner's Downloads folder said the same thing, which is the exact pattern R-057 closed: a rule in this repository does not become more binding by being corroborated somewhere a terminal cannot read, and naming that file leaves the next reader wondering whether they were supposed to open it. CLAUDE.md section 11 is the whole authority and it always was. A rule with three flags and no check is a rule that gets swept once and reappears, and this card is the sweep, not the fix.

THE FIX IS A CHECK AND IT IS NOT AUTHORED HERE. A repository-wide check refusing em and en dashes, wired into the quality job, would close this permanently and would cost about as much as this card. It is not authored because the dispatch enumerated four cards to author and adding a fifth is scope the AUTHOR was not given. It is recorded here so one line of dispatch can create it, and the sibling shape is already on the board: AUT-11 is exactly this, a guard authored beside the fix it makes unrepeatable.

TWO OTHER DEFECTS IN THIS FILE WERE FOUND WHILE READING FOR THIS CARD AND ARE ALREADY FIXED, NOT LEFT FOR IT. Lines 1536 and 1636 carried stripped conflict marker tails, ` poc/19-harness-caps` sitting between two unrelated entries and ` main` as the final line of the file. They were removed in the pull request that authored this card, because that pull request appends to the same file and leaving known corruption in a file it edits is not defensible. A LEARNINGS entry records the pattern and the grep that finds it, since a marker grep cannot.

cards.title: The board as_of is read from a clock, not from the previous as_of: a check refuses any board timestamp that is ahead of the commit that wrote it.
cards.plain: The date the work list claims it was last updated has been drifting further and further into the future, and now says it was updated nine hours before it actually was. This makes it read a real clock and adds an automatic check so it cannot drift again.
cards.acceptance: `npm run check:board-clock` exits 0, a NEW check wired into the quality job BY NAME, asserting two properties over every board JSON in docs/board/: (1) `as_of` is not more than 60 MINUTES AHEAD of the commit that last modified that file; (2) no `last_checkpoint`, and no `evidence.at`, on any card or launch gate condition is ahead of that same commit. THE FAILURE IS PROVED FIRST AND IT IS ALREADY IN THE HISTORY, so it does not need to be manufactured: the same check run against `docs/board/rc-board-phase3.json` AS IT STOOD AT COMMIT 612ca05 exits non-zero and names as_of 2026-08-31T11:45:00Z against a commit time of 2026-08-31T02:31:11Z, and that failing output is quoted in the pull request. It is also proved to fail at 942b6bf and to PASS at b8910e5, whose as_of was three minutes behind its commit, so the check is shown to separate the two cases rather than to reject everything.
cards.defaults:
AHEAD-ONLY, NOT A WINDOW, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. A board written twenty minutes before the commit that carries it is normal: a session finishes its board edit, then runs the validator, then commits. A board timestamped AFTER its own commit is a value nobody read from any clock, because that time had not happened yet. Only the ahead direction is an error, so the check has one bound. A symmetric window would fail honest commits and would have to be loosened until it stopped catching anything.

SIXTY MINUTES IS THE THRESHOLD ON THE as_of HALF, AND IT IS NOT A TOLERANCE FOR DRIFT. It is slack for a long commit sequence. The measured drift on the phase 3 board went 3, 21, 62, 150, 226, 300, 398, 467, 521, 557 and 554 minutes across eleven consecutive commits, so 60 catches it on the third and every one after. On the last_checkpoint half the threshold is ZERO: a per-card checkpoint in the future has no honest reading at all.

THE REPAIR IS PART OF THE CARD, AND IT IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. Every remaining future timestamp is set to the commit time of the commit that wrote that value, read with `git log -1 --format=%cI <commit>`, not to the time the repair runs. Where a card is touched, its notes say the value was corrected and to what, rather than presenting it as always having been right. TRIAGE already corrected as_of on both boards and last_checkpoint on the cards it touched, so the remaining set is smaller than the history suggests: enumerate it, do not assume it.

GIT HISTORY IS NOT REWRITTEN. The wrong values that were committed stay committed. This corrects the CURRENT field values and adds the check.

THE CHECK READS GIT, SO SAY WHICH COMMIT IT READ. In the quality job the checkout may be shallow or may be a merge commit for the pull request. Compare against the commit that last touched the file if it is available and against HEAD otherwise, and PRINT which of the two was used on every run. A check whose comparison basis is invisible produces a failure nobody can reproduce locally.

DO NOT FIX THIS BY REMOVING THE FIELD OR BY GENERATING IT. Deleting as_of, or having a script write it at commit time, both make the check pass and both lose what the field is for: a human statement of when the board was last made true. The failure was not that a person typed a timestamp. It was that the person read the previous timestamp instead of a clock.

WHY THE NEXT SESSION WILL WANT TO TYPE A FUTURE VALUE ANYWAY, AND MUST NOT: correcting as_of makes it jump BACKWARDS relative to the previous commit, which looks wrong on a board whose purpose is to say when it last told the truth. That exact reasoning is what produced the drift, one session at a time, each one declining to be the one that moved the number back. The check is what ends the argument.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED BY TRIAGE 2026-08-31, RUN 20260830-220004, UNDER RULING R-064.
SOURCE: docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-11-material-cost.md section 4b, which found the offset, named it as needing a card, and followed it anyway. The finding is credited; the choice is overturned by R-064.

IT IS A RATCHET, NOT AN OFFSET, AND THAT IS THE PART THE REPORT DID NOT HAVE. The report describes the phase 3 board as running "about nine hours ahead". Measured across the eleven commits that touched it, the gap between as_of and the real commit time is 3 minutes, then 21, 62, 150, 226, 300, 398, 467, 521, 557 and 554. It is not a constant offset from a wrong timezone. It GROWS, because each session reads the previous as_of and writes something plausibly later, and the increment it adds exceeds the real elapsed time. Nothing stops it: at this rate the board would claim a date a day ahead within a week.

IT IS ON THE PHASE 2 BOARD BECAUSE THE TOOLING LIVES HERE. R-061 kept the harness and its cards on this board. The check covers both board files.

CLAUDE.md SECTION 2 ALREADY REQUIRED THIS AND WAS NOT ENOUGH: "the top-level as_of bumped to the commit moment in ISO 8601". A rule with no check is a rule that survives exactly as long as nobody is tired, and these are unattended runs at 22:00, 01:00, 04:00 and 07:00.

cards.title: DOCTRINE-TRIAGE's input clause is corrected: the report is the only dispatch, not the only file, because sections 2 through 5 of the same document require the board, the inbox and the git history.
cards.plain: The rulebook for the reviewing step tells it to read one file and nothing else, then gives it four jobs that cannot be done without reading several more. This fixes the sentence so a future reviewing session does not have to choose which half of its own rulebook to disobey.
cards.acceptance: `node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md','utf8').replace(/\\s+/g,' '); const head=s.split('### What TRIAGE may do')[0]; const bad=head.includes('is not in that report or in this file'); const good=head.includes('committed repository files'); process.exit(bad || !good ? 1 : 0)"` exits 0. THE WHITESPACE IS NORMALISED BEFORE EITHER TEST, and that is not a detail: the clause being removed is wrapped across two lines in the file, so a substring test against the raw text matches nothing and passes vacuously forever. That trap was hit while authoring this card and it is written here so it is not hit again. TWO ASSERTIONS IN ONE COMMAND, both scoped to the 'What TRIAGE is' section above '### What TRIAGE may do': (1) the clause 'is not in that report or in this file' is GONE, and (2) that same section now names 'committed repository files' as the ground truth TRIAGE reads. The phrase already exists in section 6 of the document, which is why the test is scoped to the head rather than to the whole file. THE COMMAND IS PROVED TO EXIT 1 ON THE CURRENT FILE FIRST, for the right reason on each half, and both halves of that failing run are quoted in the pull request. PLUS `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
WHAT THE CLAUSE MUST KEEP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF IT: TRIAGE takes no dispatch text, no summary, no chat message and no verbal ratification. That is R-050 and it is not weakened by one word. A human handing TRIAGE context is still the failure this clause exists to stop.

WHAT IT MUST STOP SAYING: that reading anything other than the report is a defect. Section 2 needs the next free ruling id from decisions/inbox.md. Section 3 needs both board files, by its own words, over the whole board and not only the cards the report touched. Section 4 needs committed artefacts by name: a pull request number, a run id, a journal entry. Section 5 needs the board to know whether an open card already covers a finding. A session obeying the clause literally cannot do any of the four.

THE DISTINCTION TO WRITE IS DISPATCH VERSUS REPOSITORY. The report is the only DISPATCH: it is what tells TRIAGE what this run is about, and there is no second source of that. The repository is the ground truth it checks the dispatch against, and section 6 already says so in those words.

THE DEFECT SENTENCE IS KEPT IN SOME FORM. "If the rubric does not say how to decide something, that is a defect in the rubric and saying so is a legitimate output" is a good rule and R-067 was written under it. What it must not say is that READING a committed file is the defect.

ONE SENTENCE, NOT A REWRITE. This card changes a paragraph. It does not reopen the four tests, the escalation list, or anything R-057 or R-050 settled.

AUTHOR WRITES IT, NOT TRIAGE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A role that edits the document constraining it has removed the constraint whatever the edit says. R-067 records the finding and stops there.

cards.title: The harness resolves a card id against every open board, so the owner can answer a phase 3 question from Telegram and the digest can see the work that is actually being done.
cards.plain: The overnight system currently only knows about the old half of the work list. It means Ivan cannot reply to a question about the new half from his phone, and the daily summary he reads leaves that half out entirely. This teaches it to read both.
cards.acceptance: A NEW CHECK WIRED INTO THE quality JOB BY NAME, EXITS 0, WITH ALL THREE HALVES PROVED TO FAIL FIRST AGAINST THE CURRENT FILES AND THE FAILING OUTPUT QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST. (1) ANSWER CHANNEL: the classifier in scripts/poc/inbox.mjs accepts `R P3-27 default` and `R P3-27: some text` and returns cardId P3-27, and still refuses `R NOPE-99 default` with a reason naming the id. Against the current scripts/poc/inbox.mjs the first two are REFUSED with "no card P3-27 on the board", and that refusal is the failing case. (2) DIGEST: buildPlainDigest over a fixture pair of boards names a shipped card that exists only on the second board, and reports a launch gate figure for each board rather than one figure that silently means the first. (3) ELIGIBILITY AND CLAIMS: the eligible-card selector and the claim writer resolve a card id against the union of the boards, proved by a fixture where the lowest-id eligible card is on the second board and the claim written names that card. PLUS `bash -n scripts/poc/run.sh` exits 0. THE BOARD SET IS READ FROM ONE PLACE, so a fourth board is a one-line change and not a fourth hardcoded path.
cards.defaults: THE BOARD SET IS A LIST, NOT A REPOINT. Do not change POC_BOARD to point at the phase 3 board: that moves the blindness rather than removing it, and the AUT, BOARD, CLAIM, LEARN and RST lanes plus the phase 2 launch gate would disappear from the digest instead. Introduce a board LIST, read from one place, that every component resolves against. ORDER WITHIN THE LIST: phase 3 first, then phase 2, because the owner's stated priority in R-061's verbatim is wave 1 and wave 2 of phase 3, and the lowest-id rule in CLAUDE.md section 2 applies WITHIN a board rather than across two id namespaces that were never designed to sort against each other. Say so in the pull request. AMBIGUOUS CARD ID: if the same id ever appears on two boards, that is a board defect, and the check FAILS loudly rather than picking one. THE CLOSED PHASE 1 BOARD, docs/board/rc-board.json, IS NOT IN THE SET for eligibility or claims, because a closed board has no eligible cards; it MAY be in the set for id resolution if AUT-11's card-id check wants it, and that is AUT-11's decision and not this card's. THE DIGEST REPORTS EACH BOARD SEPARATELY. Do not sum two launch gates into one fraction: 6 of 9 and 0 of 9 is not 6 of 18, and a merged figure is a number the owner would be right to distrust. TELEGRAM STAYS EXACTLY AS NARROW AS IT IS: the two accepted forms in CLAUDE.md section 13 do not change, TELEGRAM_OWNER_ID still gates every message, and this card widens WHICH card ids resolve and nothing else about what the reader accepts. NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED by anything this card touches.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-31 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-071, from docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-13-deviz-schema.md sections 0 and 3b, and from two further consequences that report did not find.
THE REPORT FOUND ONE OF THREE HARDCODED PATHS. scripts/poc/run.sh line 23 is the one it names, and its consequence is a claim lease protecting the wrong card: docs/poc/state.json carries a claim on AUT-10 by harness at 2026-08-31T02:48:59Z, written at the end of a run that spent its time on P3-11.
THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT COSTS. scripts/poc/inbox.mjs line 38 reads the same path and builds knownCardIds from it, so the Telegram reader returns "no card P3-27 on the board" for every phase 3 card id. CLAUDE.md section 13 names Telegram as the owner's answer channel, and P3-27 is the oldest unanswered question in this repository. He could not have answered it from his phone if he had tried.
THE THIRD IS scripts/poc/notify.mjs line 27. plain-digest.mjs reads launch_gate.readiness_passed and counts shipped cards off that one board, so the digest reports 36 done and 6 of 9 and cannot see the twelve phase 3 cards shipped since 2026-08-30.
R-071 SUPERSEDES THE HARNESS HALF OF R-061, which said the phase 2 board is still the queue for every unattended run. That premise did not hold: runs 20260830-220004 and 20260831-010005 shipped P3-11 and P3-13, both filed as unattended scheduled runs in their own reports. Everything else in R-061 stands.

--- A FOURTH CONSEQUENCE, OBSERVED 2026-08-31 BY TRIAGE RUN 20260831-040003, INSIDE ACCEPTANCE HALF (3) ALREADY ---
The silence rule at run.sh line 1037 escalates an eligible card that shipped nothing. It computes eligibility off the same single board path, so on a run that worked the phase 3 board it names phase 2 cards the run never considered and cannot name the card it actually left on a branch. Run 20260831-040003 left P3-13b in_flight on branch card/p3-13b with a red acceptance, which is the `work left on a branch` reason CLAUDE.md section 13 distinguishes by name, and the escalation the harness wrote could not say so. No new acceptance clause is needed: half (3) already requires the eligible-card selector to resolve against the union of the boards, and the silence rule reads that selector.

--- SHIPPED 2026-09-04 BY EXECUTOR, unattended run 20260904-010000, PR #186.
scripts/poc/boards.mjs is the only place a board file is named. The set is a LIST, phase 3 first then phase 2, per the defaults: the lowest-id rule applies WITHIN a board. run.sh, inbox.mjs, notify.mjs, plain-digest.mjs, digest.mjs, digest.sh, eligible.mjs and claim.sh all resolve against it. An id on two boards fails loudly. Each board reports its own launch gate figure. The closed phase 1 board is named under CLOSED_BOARDS and is NOT in the working set, which leaves AUT-11 its decision.
TWO DEFECTS ON THE SAME PATH WERE FIXED WITH IT. claim.sh upper-cased the id it was handed, so a lease on P3-04b was stored as P3-04B and eligible.mjs looked it up verbatim: the lease protected nothing and said nothing. And run.sh read one board when reporting branch work, so every phase 3 card worked on a branch reported unknown.
THE SET IS PASSED AS REPEATED --board FLAGS, never one packed string, because run.sh and digest.sh are deployed copies while the .mjs files are read from a worktree at origin/main: for one merge window a new script meets an old parser, which keeps the last flag and behaves as it did before. Both scripts fall back to the phase boards present in the commit when boards.mjs is absent from it, and log that they did.
TWO FINDINGS REPORTED AND NOT FIXED HERE, per CLAUDE.md section 3. R p3-04b default is still refused by the accepted-form regex, which reads [A-Za-z0-9]+-[0-9]+ and stops at the digits; this card defaults say the reader does not get wider here, so it is in docs/LEARNINGS.md and wants a card. And scripts/poc/test-chat-classify.sh fails on main, verified in a clean worktree at HEAD, and is not wired into quality.
INSTALL NOTE: CLAUDE.md section 15 requires scripts/poc/install.sh to be re-run after any change to run.sh or digest.sh. Both changed here.

cards.title: Land the content of PR #126: five rulings and three authored cards that are committed, green on their own sha, and stuck outside main behind a conflict.

(1) `git show origin/main:decisions/inbox.md | grep -c '^### R-06[34567] '` prints 5, so R-063, R-064, R-065, R-066 and R-067 are all present. cards.defaults: TWO ROUTES, EITHER IS ACCEPTED, AND THE CARD IS ABOUT THE CONTENT REACHING main RATHER THAN ABOUT PR #126 SPECIFICALLY. (a) Resolve triage/20260830-220004 locally against the full tree per R-052, land the resolution as one ordinary commit on top of the existing head, let quality run on the new sha, and merge #126. (b) If that branch cannot be repaired without a history rewrite, open a NEW branch and re-land its five rulings, its three cards and its report VERBATIM, then close #126 with a comment naming the branch that replaced it. CLAUDE.md section 3 forbids the force push that would make a rewrite possible, and says a branch whose history needs rewriting gets a new branch, so (b) is the sanctioned escape and not a workaround. NEVER IN THE GITHUB WEB EDITOR AND NEVER BY THE OWNER: R-052 names both by name. THE CONFLICT IS IN docs/board/rc-board-phase3.json AND IN decisions/inbox.md. On the board, main carries P3-13 shipped from PR #129 and the branch carries R-065's nine gate evidence rewrites plus the P3-04b and P3-05b resequence; BOTH SURVIVE, they are edits to different cards and different fields. In the inbox both sides append at the same point and BOTH APPEND SETS SURVIVE, R-063 to R-067 first and then R-068 to R-074, in id order, because DOCTRINE-TRIAGE says a collision is fixed by renumbering the new entry and the new entries were already numbered around the old ones. NOTHING IN EITHER FILE IS DROPPED TO MAKE THE MERGE EASIER: if a resolution would lose a ruling or a gate audit, stop and escalate instead. NO RULING TEXT IS EDITED WHILE RESOLVING, per DOCTRINE-TRIAGE: a changed mind is a new dated ruling.

cards.plain: The nightly reviewing step is pointed at the wrong write-up. It can be given one from an earlier session, or one that has already been reviewed, and it would then repeat a review that is already finished with nothing noticing. This points it at the right one.
cards.acceptance: A NEW TEST WIRED INTO THE quality JOB BY NAME, OR NEW CASES IN scripts/poc/test-harness-caps.sh, EXITS 0, WITH ALL FOUR HALVES PROVED TO FAIL FIRST AGAINST THE CURRENT scripts/poc/run.sh AND THE FAILING OUTPUT QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST. (1) ORDERING BY COMMIT, NOT BY NAME: given a fixture repository holding two executor reports with the SAME date in their filename, where the one committed SECOND has a slug that sorts FIRST alphabetically, the selector returns the one committed second. THE FIXTURE IS CONSTRUCTED AND THAT IS STATED IN THE PULL REQUEST: no such inversion has occurred in this repository's history yet, which is exactly why the defect has never fired and why the test may not be built by replaying real history. (2) ALREADY CONSUMED: given a fixture docs/poc/triage-latest.json whose `report` field equals the path the selector would return, the harness does NOT invoke the review step on it a second time. It logs the refusal naming the path and the run id that consumed it, and the test asserts WHICH of the two legal outcomes happened, selecting the next unconsumed report or skipping the step. (3) THE REPORT THIS RUN JUST WROTE: given a fixture where the executor step committed docs/reports/<date>-executor-<slug>.md on a branch that is NOT merged into main, and origin/main's newest executor report is an older file, the selector returns the branch report. (4) THE DISPATCH TEXT: `grep -c 'you need nothing else' scripts/poc/run.sh` prints 0, and the review step's prompt block no longer asserts that reading another committed file is a defect. THE PHRASE IS ON ONE LINE TODAY, line 749, and the grep is proved to print 1 before the change so the test is not passing vacuously. PLUS `bash -n scripts/poc/run.sh` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE SELECTOR IS ONE FUNCTION IN ONE PLACE and the test calls that function, rather than re-implementing the pipeline in the test. The current selector is three commands in a pipe inline at run.sh line 734; a test written against a copy of the pipe proves the copy.

HOW THE RUN LEARNS THE BRANCH ITS OWN EXECUTOR USED: give the executor step the same `checkpoint_pr` call the review step already has at line 853, so the run records its executor's pull request number, branch and report path the moment they exist. That function is already written, already deduplicates, and already writes to both the log and a file that survives a kill. Do not add a second mechanism and do not parse the model's output for a path.

PREFERENCE ORDER WHEN BOTH EXIST: the report this run's own executor committed wins over the newest on origin/main, always, even when the branch report is older by commit time. The review step exists to read what THIS run produced.

NEVER INVENT AN INPUT. `NO REPORT MEANS NO TRIAGE` at line 716 is correct and is not weakened: if every candidate is already recorded as consumed, skip the step and log it. A run with nothing to review is a normal outcome; a run that reviews the same report twice is not.

CONSUMED IS READ FROM docs/poc/triage-latest.json AND NOWHERE ELSE. Do not add a second state file. That file already exists, is already required output of the review step, and already carries the report path. If it is absent or unparseable, treat nothing as consumed and log that, because failing open here costs a duplicate review and failing closed costs every review.

THE DISPATCH SENTENCE IS CORRECTED, NOT DELETED. What must survive is that the review step takes no chat, no summary, no human context and no verbal ratification: that is R-050 and it is the whole point of the clause. What must go is the claim that reading a committed repository file is a defect. R-067 and card AUT-15 make the same correction in docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md; if AUT-15 has already shipped, match its wording rather than inventing a second phrasing.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED by anything this card touches.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-31 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-075, run 20260831-040003, from the dispatch this run itself received.

WHAT HAPPENED. The harness handed this run docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-13-deviz-schema.md, which the PREVIOUS run had already triaged in full as R-068 to R-074, merged as PR #131 at 08:36:51Z. This run read the second one and said so.

THE THREE DEFECTS ARE IN ELEVEN LINES OF SHELL at run.sh 734 to 735: the selection sorts filenames rather than commits, it reads origin/main only so a report riding in an unmerged card pull request is invisible, and it never compares the result against docs/poc/triage-latest.json which records exactly what the last review consumed.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. A card whose acceptance fails leaves its report on an unmerged branch, and a failing card is the run whose report most needs reviewing. That is the one shape this selector cannot see. And a review that repeats itself produces two ids saying the same thing about one report, on a green pull request, with nothing erroring, which is a failure that looks exactly like a clean run.

IT IS ON THE PHASE 2 BOARD because the harness cards live here, per R-041 and R-061.

--- SECOND LIVE INSTANCE, AND A CLAUSE THE ACCEPTANCE DOES NOT YET COVER. RECORDED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-102, RUN 20260904-010000 ---
WHAT HAPPENED, AGAIN. Run 20260904-010000 was dispatched docs/reports/2026-09-03-executor-sample-ttl-and-document-source.md as "the newest report in docs/reports/". Run 20260903-220002 had already triaged that exact file in full, as R-098 to R-101 with two cards and a gate audit, three hours earlier. cards.title: Every scheduled run reports every open pull request it did not merge, and escalates the ones no merge could rest on. It merges nothing.
cards.plain: Finished work sometimes sits in an unpublished change nobody mentions again, and today nothing says so. Each nightly run will list what is still open and flag anything that cannot be published as it stands, so it is noticed the same night instead of days later.
cards.acceptance: `bash scripts/poc/test-harness-caps.sh` exits 0 WITH NEW CASES ADDED, or a sibling test file wired into the quality job BY NAME, proving all three halves, EACH PROVED TO FAIL FIRST AGAINST THE CURRENT scripts/poc/run.sh WITH THE FAILING OUTPUT QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST. (1) THE CENSUS IS WRITTEN: fed a fixture list of open pull requests, the run writes ONE LINE PER PULL REQUEST to the run log carrying its number, head branch, head sha, merge state, and whether a `quality` check run EXISTS for that head sha and what it concluded. Every open pull request appears, including `card/` branches. (2) THE ESCALATION FIRES ON EXACTLY TWO SHAPES AND NO OTHERS: a pull request whose merge state is CONFLICTING, and a pull request whose head commit PREDATES the start of the current run and whose `quality` is not success on that head sha, whether the run is absent, failed or still pending. Each is appended to docs/poc/state.json escalations naming the number and the reason. THE NEGATIVE HALF IS ASSERTED AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: a green mergeable pull request does not escalate, and neither does a red pull request whose head commit was pushed by the current run, because that is a card being actively worked and escalating it every run trains the reader to skip the list. (3) IT MERGES NOTHING AND CANNOT: fed a fixture in which every pull request is green and mergeable, the census path performs ZERO merge calls, asserted against a stubbed merge function. PLUS `bash -n scripts/poc/run.sh` exits 0. (4) A PUSHED BRANCH WITH NO PULL REQUEST IS NAMED, ADDED 2026-09-02 BY R-092 FROM docs/reports/2026-09-01-executor-p3-11d-stale-checks.md section 5: fed a fixture list of remote branches ALONGSIDE the fixture list of open pull requests, the run writes ONE LINE per remote branch that has NO open pull request and is NOT already merged into main, carrying the branch name, its head sha and its age, and APPENDS AN ESCALATION to docs/poc/state.json for any such branch whose head commit predates the start of the current run. THE NEGATIVE HALF IS ASSERTED AS ON THE OTHER THREE: main itself never appears, a branch already merged into main never appears, and a branch pushed by the current run is listed in the census but does NOT escalate. PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current scripts/poc/run.sh with the failing output quoted in the pull request, like clauses 1 to 3.
cards.defaults:
THIS CARD ADDS A REPORT, NOT A RECOVERY, AND THE BOUNDARY WITH RST-02 IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. RST-02 widens which pull requests the sweep MERGES and its own acceptance asserts that a `card/` branch is NEVER selected for merging, for the reason written on that card: a sweep that merged card branches would ship unproven cards at four in the morning. Nothing here touches the merge selector. The census READS every open pull request and merges none, which is why it may look at card branches safely.

THE TWO ESCALATION SHAPES ARE CHOSEN AGAINST REAL INCIDENTS, NOT INVENTED. CONFLICTING catches PR #133 on 2026-08-31, which had no `quality` run at all on its head sha because a conflicting pull request triggers zero workflows, so the fix in its head commit was untested and unmergeable at once. The stale-and-not-green shape catches PR #130 on the same day, mergeable but behind, red on the End to end step since 05:34Z, named by nothing for a full run.

WHY THE AGE CONDITION IS ON THE SECOND SHAPE AND NOT THE FIRST. A card pull request is red for most of its life and that is normal work. Escalating it every run makes the list worthless. A head commit older than this run's start means nobody pushed to it this run, which is what turns red from work-in-progress into stuck. CONFLICTING needs no age condition because it is a hard stop whatever the age.

PENDING COUNTS AS NOT GREEN, DELIBERATELY. A `quality` run stuck in progress on a head sha from a previous run is the same problem as one that failed: nothing may merge on it.

ONE ESCALATION PER PULL REQUEST PER RUN, and the same pull request escalating on consecutive runs is correct and is not deduplicated across runs. The escalation is how the digest carries it; a stuck pull request that goes quiet after the first night is the failure this card exists to stop.

THE CENSUS GOES TO THE RUN LOG EVEN WHEN NOTHING ESCALATES. A run that merged nothing and reported nothing must not look identical to a run with no open pull requests, which is CLAUDE.md section 13 applied to pull requests instead of to cards.

BOUNDED CALLS ONLY. Use the existing `gh_bounded` wrapper, not a bare `gh`, because an unbounded GitHub call inside a run has already eaten most of a 45 minute window once.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED.

CLAUSE 4 READS BRANCHES, NOT PULL REQUESTS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF IT. Every sweep in this repository starts from the pull request list, so a branch that never got a pull request is not in any input anywhere. Do not implement clause 4 by filtering the pull request list; it must start from the remote branch list and subtract.

MERGED MEANS MERGED INTO main BY ANY ROUTE, including a squash merge whose commit sha differs from the branch head. Ask git whether the branch head is an ancestor of main, or ask GitHub whether a merged pull request exists for it. A squash-merged branch whose head sha is absent from main is the case a naive ancestor test gets wrong, and reporting every squash-merged branch forever is how this clause gets ignored.

DELETING THE BRANCH IS NOT THIS CARD'S JOB AND MUST NOT BE ADDED TO IT. This card reports. A sweep that deleted branches could delete work that has not been published, which is the exact loss it exists to prevent.

evidence.ref: scripts/poc/test-pr-census.sh, wired into the quality job by name as the step 'Prove the pull request census  # AUT-18-CENSUS-PROOF'. Green on the head sha of the pull request that carries this card. All four clauses proved to fail first and the failing output is quoted in the pull request body: against the pre-change scripts/poc/run.sh the suite exits 1 with 'FATAL: no EXTRACT block named pr-census', and against four mutants of the shipped run.sh, each disabling exactly one clause, each mutant fails exactly its own case (clause 1: three field assertions; clause 2: #306 escalated and must not, 5 escalations not 4; clause 3: the census called something it must never call; clause 4: four branch assertions).

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-31 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-078, run 20260831-040003, from docs/reports/2026-08-31-executor-p3-13b-deviz-editor.md section 6 and from two live pull request states that report could not have known.

WHAT THE REPORT SAID AND WHAT WAS TRUE BY THE TIME IT WAS READ. The report handed PR #133 to the next run as BEHIND, needing a merge from main. Read three hours later it is CONFLICTING and DIRTY, with NO `quality` check run on head sha f377fb9 at all: the checks on that commit are Vercel and a skipped Supabase preview. CLAUDE.md section 3 already names the cause, a pull request conflicting with main triggers zero workflows, and the consequence is that the diacritic fix in that commit has never been tested.

THE SECOND INSTANCE WAS NAMED BY NOTHING. PR #130 carries the R-073 addendum to the P3-13 report and two learnings. It is MERGEABLE and BEHIND and its `quality` run on head sha 5631e6e FAILED at the End to end step at 05:34:45Z, while main was green at c124529 one minute earlier and green again at f036f1b. A documentation-only branch failing the end to end suite is a flake or an intermittent, and either way it is a red check no merge may rest on. R-073 named it as the live instance of the addendum pattern; the next report does not mention it.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE CARD FROM RST-02, which DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 5 requires to be argued rather than assumed. RST-02 is the merge selector and its acceptance asserts that card branches are NEVER selected. R-070 added to it that a selected pull request the sweep cannot merge is escalated. A card branch is never selected, so it is never escalated either, and the two correct rules compose into a blind spot exactly the width of the pull requests that carry the product. One card picks work up; this one makes it impossible for work to be invisible.

--- CLAUSE 4 ADDED 2026-09-02 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-092, run 20260902-070904, from docs/reports/2026-09-01-executor-p3-11d-stale-checks.md section 5 ---
A CARD BRANCH WAS PUSHED AND NO PULL REQUEST WAS EVER OPENED, so no check ran and nothing anywhere reported anything at all. The owner noticed before the terminal did. The report names the family correctly: absence of a signal read as absence of a problem, which is the same family as the stale green check the card itself was about.
NO CARD IS AUTHORED FOR IT AND SECTION 5 IS WHY. This card is the census that reads every open pull request and merges nothing; the missing query is one line wider than its own clause 1, which begins by being fed a list of OPEN PULL REQUESTS. RST-02 cannot carry it: RST-02 merges, and its acceptance asserts that a card branch is never selected for merging. A branch with no pull request must be reported and must never be merged, so it lands here.
THE HABIT THE REPORT NAMES IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE. Checking that a pull request exists after pushing is the right habit and this repository does not gate on habits. Clause 4 is the machine-verifiable half.

--- SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR, unattended run 20260904-220003 ---
The census is a fenced EXTRACT block in scripts/poc/run.sh named pr-census, and
scripts/poc/test-pr-census.sh lifts it verbatim and runs it over fixtures with
no network, no gh and no remote. Five census_* seams are the only place gh or
git is touched, which is what makes the block testable; the test replaces them
and additionally shadows merge_when_green, gh, gh_bounded and git as tripwires,
so clause 3 is asserted against a stub rather than argued.

CALL SITE. Step 5, immediately after the state branch is checked out and before
the node -e that rewrites docs/poc/state.json. That position is load bearing:
every merge this run intended has already happened, and the escalations the
census appends to state.json are read back by that same node -e and carried by
the state pull request like every other escalation. No new pull request, no new
push path.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE CARD TEXT, BOTH NARROWER THAN THEY LOOK. (1) The card
names CONFLICTING; GitHub reports that condition as CONFLICTING on `mergeable`
and as DIRTY on `mergeStateStatus`, and the seam returns mergeStateStatus, so
both words are accepted and both are documented at the case statement. (2) An
unresolvable commit time is pinned to 0, which reads as older than every run and
therefore escalates, because the alternative is a missing input that silently
suppresses its own escalation. Both are recorded in docs/LEARNINGS.md.

NOTHING WAS ADDED THAT THE CARD FORBIDS. The census merges nothing and deletes
no branch. The merge selector in RST-02 is untouched.

cards.title: Gate G4's last two clauses: the extraction fire refuses a redirecting webhook address, and the callback bounds what it will accept, each asserted by its own named case.
cards.plain: Two ways the automatic document reading can fail without anyone noticing are proved to be caught: an address that has been mis-set and quietly swallows every document while reporting success, and a file too big to accept. These are the last two things standing between the automatic reading and being counted as ready.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 WITH TWO NEW CASES, AND BOTH ARE PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current tree with the failing output quoted in the pull request. THE REDIRECT CASE: with the webhook address pointed at a URL that answers 301 or 302, the fire records the document as NOT sent, the reason is visible on the screen in Romanian, and the request is NOT followed to the redirect target, asserted by the redirect target receiving nothing. THE OVERSIZE CASE: a callback body above the declared limit is REFUSED with 400, nothing is written to either extraction table, and the limit is a single named constant rather than a number repeated in two places. PLUS THE FIVE G4 CLAUSES ARE COUNTABLE IN ONE FILE: the pull request quotes the names of all five cases together, the three that already exist and pass (case 2 the fixture document, case 4 the auth rejection, case 5 the malformed payload) and the two added here, so a reader can count the gate's clauses without reconstructing them. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE TWO CASES POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THAT IS NOT AN INCONSISTENCY. The redirect case is about US as the CALLER, firing at MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL from lib/data/extraction-fire.ts. The oversize case is about US as the RECEIVER, at app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts. R-053's own rationale is the caller half: an endpoint sitting behind a redirect returns 200 while doing nothing, the caller sees success, and every happy path test passes.

REFUSE, DO NOT FOLLOW. Set the fetch redirect policy to manual and treat any 3xx as a failure with its own reason. Following the redirect is exactly what makes the failure invisible, and a test that asserts a successful POST to the redirect TARGET would be asserting the defect.

THE OVERSIZE REFUSAL USES 400 AND DOES NOT INTRODUCE 413, AND THIS IS THE DEFAULT THAT MATTERS MOST. docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md section 6 fixes the response codes at 202, 200, 400, 401 and 5xx. Adding 413 changes what Andre's scenario has to handle, which is item 6 of the closed escalation list in DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 6 and is not this card's to decide. 400 is already in the contract and already means the payload was not accepted. Give it a distinct error reason so the two 400 causes are told apart in the log.

THE LIMIT IS DECLARED, NOT DISCOVERED. One exported constant, 1 MiB for the JSON callback body unless something already in the repository says otherwise, named in the Romanian refusal message. A larger bound may be chosen and the pull request says why; a bound that exists only as a platform default is not a declared bound and does not satisfy the clause.

THIS CARD DOES NOT REBUILD THE RECEIVER OR THE FIRE. P2-08a owns both. Adding the redirect policy and the body bound is completing them, not replacing them. If either case reveals a defect deeper than a missing guard, that is a finding on P2-08a and a new card, never a second implementation here.

NO PRODUCTION CREDENTIAL AND NO PRODUCTION CALL. Both cases run against the local stack in the quality job like every other case in this file. The redirect target is a local fixture route, never a real address.

THE GATE IS NOT FLIPPED BY THIS CARD SHIPPING. G4 flips on committed evidence in a gate audit, per R-023, and an audit is a separate act from a card shipping. Say in the pull request that the two clauses are now evidenced, and leave the flip to the audit.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-31 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-080, run 20260831-040003. THIS IS THE FIRST CARD G4 HAS EVER HAD.

WHY IT DID NOT EXIST. R-053 rescoped G4 on 2026-08-28: its deciding clause stopped being one real document through Andre's live scenario and became the ingest endpoint asserted against a fixture document plus four named failure cases, redirect, malformed payload, oversize and auth rejection. That ruling's `Also changes` line ordered two board edits that were never made: P2-08b rescoped, and a new card for the half that was left over. The gate's notes carry the rescope; the board carries neither card. So a gate a terminal has been able to close for three days was audited twice since, by R-046's successor R-074, as one no terminal can close.

THREE OF THE FIVE CLAUSES ARE ALREADY GREEN AND NOBODY HAD RECORDED IT. tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts runs in the End to end step of quality on every push and carries eight cases. Case 2, `un callback extracted scrie fiecare camp al contractului`, is the fixture document. Case 4, `secret gresit sau lipsa este 401 si nu scrie nimic`, is the auth rejection. Case 5, `un payload in afara contractului este 400 si nu scrie nimic`, is the malformed payload. Redirect and oversize are absent: nothing in lib/data/extraction-fire.ts sets a redirect policy and nothing in app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts bounds a body.

THE IDS ARE ASSIGNED THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND FROM R-053'S SENTENCE AND R-080 RECORDS THE SWAP. R-053 said rescope P2-08b to the endpoint assertions and author a new card for the live round trip.
