Done that way, P2-08b's title, acceptance, defaults and the Andre question preserved inside it would all have to be rewritten to mean something else, and TRIAGE does not edit titles. So P2-08b keeps the live round trip it is written for and this card carries the endpoint assertions. The substance of R-053 is applied exactly; only which id holds which half differs.

IT DEPENDS ON P2-08a AND NOTHING ELSE. P2-08a is shipped, so this card is eligible today. It does NOT depend on P2-08b: the whole point of R-053 is that this half needs nobody outside this repository.

cards.title: A role that hits a decision it may not make asks Ivan on Telegram and BLOCKS on the answer, against a wall clock deadline, and writes the question onto the card rather than taking its own recommendation when nobody replies.
cards.plain: When the system hits something only you can decide, it now asks you directly and waits for your answer instead of stopping quietly where nobody sees it. If you do not reply within six hours it writes the question down against the job, marked as needing you, and moves on to something else rather than guessing.
cards.acceptance: bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh exits 0, wired into the quality job by name as the step 'Prove the question channel and the scheduled digest'. It runs the REAL scripts/poc/ask.sh end to end in a throwaway git repository and asserts, among others, the three the dispatch names specifically. (1) A SUSPEND ACROSS THE DEADLINE: the fenced ask-deadline block is lifted verbatim from ask.sh, run against a shadowed `date` whose offset jumps 3600 seconds forward, and required to return expired within seconds; the 2026-08-27 sleep-counter shape is run on the identical input and REQUIRED TO FAIL, and a mutant whose loop condition is not the wall clock is required to fail the same case. (2) AN EXPIRED QUESTION LANDS AS blocked_on: ask.sh with --deadline-seconds 1 exits 12 and prints `expired`, never 0 and never `go`; the card is status blocked, blocked_on ivan, lane derived, its question carries DECISION NEEDED, RECOMMENDATION and IMPACT IF UNANSWERED with the payload text intact; the board validator is green; the edit is COMMITTED and the tree is clean; an expire mutated to leave the card unblocked is required to fail the case, with an unmutated control in the same scratch tree proved to run first. (3) A NON-OWNER REPLY IS IGNORED: a stranger sending `go` while a question is outstanding is classified ignored, spools nothing, leaves the question open and is logged with the reason; an instruction-shaped message from a stranger reaches nothing; an unset owner id accepts nothing even from the right numeric sender; and a classifier with the identity check removed is required to ACCEPT the stranger, with a control proving that copy runs. PLUS the message shape, the plain-register assertion over the sent text, the three answer forms, reply-to routing with two questions outstanding, the refusal to guess when two are outstanding, and `bash -n scripts/poc/ask.sh` exit 0.
cards.defaults:
THE ANSWER COMES THROUGH THE EXISTING 60 SECOND POLLER, NOT THROUGH A SECOND READER OF THE BOT. Telegram getUpdates is destructive: acknowledging an offset deletes every update below it, so two pollers race for one queue and the loser never sees the message. chat-classify.mjs writes an answer spool under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-logs/asks/ and ask.sh reads that.

EXIT 12 FOR AN EXPIRY, NOT EXIT 0. The dispatch says the script exits clean so the harness can move to another card, and it does: it terminates promptly with the board committed. It does not report success, because exit 0 is the code that means `go`, and a caller that cannot tell an expiry from an approval is the exact failure the deadline exists to prevent.

WHAT SILENCE COSTS IS IN THE MESSAGE. The dispatch's four line shape did not show it. It is a required payload field, and a message headed `Blocked on you` that does not say what ignoring it costs is the message that gets left unread.

WITH TWO OR MORE QUESTIONS OUTSTANDING AND NO REPLY AND NO CARD ID, NOTHING IS ROUTED. A bare `go` would have to guess which decision was approved.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED. The secrets file is sourced with tracing suppressed across the whole block, as responder.sh does and for the reason it documents.

evidence.ref: PR #149. `bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0 with 72 assertions and zero failures, run in the quality job as the step `Prove the question channel and the scheduled digest`, GitHub Actions run 33520527441 on 3699821, step conclusion success. The full run is quoted in docs/reports/2026-09-01-poc-builder-ask-01-digest-01.md section 5. THE THREE PROOFS THE DISPATCH NAMED, EACH MUTATION TESTED. (1) The fenced ask-deadline block, lifted verbatim from scripts/poc/ask.sh, returns expired within seconds when a shadowed `date` jumps 3600 seconds forward; the 2026-08-27 sleep-counter shape on the identical input is REQUIRED TO FAIL and does; a mutant whose loop condition is not the wall clock is required to fail and does. (2) The real ask.sh with --deadline-seconds 1, in a throwaway git repository, exits 12 and prints `expired`, and the card is status blocked, blocked_on ivan, with DECISION NEEDED, RECOMMENDATION and IMPACT IF UNANSWERED carrying the payload text; the board validator is green on the committed board and the tree is clean; an expire mutated to leave the card unblocked fails the case, with an unmutated control in the same scratch tree proved to block first. (3) A stranger sending `go` while a question is outstanding is classified ignored, spools nothing, leaves the question open and is logged; an unset owner id accepts nothing even from the right numeric sender; a classifier with the identity check removed is REQUIRED to accept the stranger and does, with a control proving that copy runs.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND BUILT 2026-09-01 BY POC-BUILDER, FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH naming ASK-01 and DIGEST-01 and asking for one pull request. That is a deviation from the one card, one branch, one pull request rule in CLAUDE.md section 2, made by the owner in the dispatch itself, and it is recorded here rather than inferred.

WHAT IT REPLACES. A foreground executor hit a decision it could not make, printed the question to a terminal nobody was watching, and stopped. Nothing was red, nothing was blocked on the board, nothing reached Telegram, and the run was gone. CLAUDE.md section 14 now names printing and stopping as a defect.

THREE REAL BUGS WERE FOUND BY THE TEST AND FIXED IN THIS PULL REQUEST, and they are worth recording because they are the shape this whole card is about: a guard that reports success while doing nothing. The entry-point guard compared process.argv[1] against import.meta.url without resolving symlinks; on macOS /var is a symlink to /private/var, so the module invoked by a path under /var compared unequal to itself, main() never ran, AND THE PROCESS EXITED 0. ask.sh read that as a question sent. It now resolves both sides with realpathSync, and separately refuses to wait unless the open-question record actually exists on disk, because a zero exit is not proof that anything happened. The board validator also printed its PASS lines to stdout, which is ask.sh's machine interface, so a caller parsing the first line would have read a validator banner as a verdict. And the credential shape check copied from inbox.mjs is unanchored, so its bare sk- alternative matches the middle of test-ask-digest.sh: it fired 20 times on this pull request's own diff, every one of them on the filename. A guard that refuses a legitimate commit gets switched off. The shapes are now anchored, fenced, and tested in both directions.

A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND AND IS NOT FIXED HERE, because it is somebody else's card: responder.sh acknowledges the Telegram offset for EVERY message it read, ruling forms included, so a ruling sent while the responder is running is consumed before inbox.mjs ever sees it. Recorded in docs/LEARNINGS.md rather than fixed, per CLAUDE.md section 3. This card is unaffected: it does not use the ruling path.

cards.title: A launchd agent sends the plain digest twice a day on a fixed schedule, renders from the plain field only, stays silent when nothing changed, and leads with any outstanding question until it is answered.
cards.plain: You get a short written update twice a day, morning and evening, without having to ask for one. It only arrives when there is something to say: something finished, something got stuck, something is waiting on your answer, or a run went wrong. If a question is waiting on you it goes at the top of every update until you answer it.
cards.acceptance: bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh exits 0, wired into the quality job by name, cases 6 to 9. SILENCE: the first run records a baseline and sends nothing, and two further runs against an unchanged board send nothing; a decide() mutated to always send IS required to send on that same unchanged board, with an unmutated control in the same scratch tree proved to send first, so the silence assertion is not passing vacuously. SPEAKING: each of the four conditions independently produces send=true with its reason named, against an unchanged baseline: a card shipped, a card became blocked, a question is outstanding, a run failed. LEADING AND REPEATING: three consecutive runs with one question outstanding send three digests, the first line of each is STILL WAITING ON YOU, the repeated text still carries the question, the recommendation and the reply line, and the whole rendered text passes assertPlain with zero card ids, ruling ids, pull request numbers, links or file paths; once the question is answered and consumed, the next run goes quiet again. WIRING: install.sh installs com.ai.rc-poc-digest and creates the answer spool, `bash -n scripts/poc/digest.sh` exits 0, and `plutil -lint docs/poc/com.ai.rc-poc-digest.plist.template` passes.
cards.defaults:
08:00 AND 19:00 LOCAL, as two StartCalendarInterval entries. launchd reads those as wall clock in the machine's timezone, and it runs a missed firing once the machine wakes, which is the behaviour this needs: a morning digest that arrives at 09:20 because the lid was shut is still the morning digest.

A RUN FAILED IS READ AS A NEW ESCALATION IN docs/poc/state.json. That is the repository's own existing signal for silence on an eligible card being a defect, it needs no log parsing, and it is already written by run.sh. The limitation is stated rather than hidden: escalations are also written for benign claim skips, so this condition is broader than the words a run failed.

THE FIRST RUN EVER RECORDS A BASELINE AND STAYS QUIET unless a question is outstanding or a run failed. A digest whose entire content is the state of a system he has been watching for a week is the noise this card removes. install.sh prints the one line that sends a proof digest by hand.

STALENESS IS BY CONTENT, NEVER BY DATE. Two digests on the same day with different content are two different digests, and a date comparison hides the second one.

RunAtLoad IS FALSE. Installing the agent is not news, and a digest that fires on every reinstall trains him to ignore the ones that fire on a schedule.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED.

evidence.ref: PR #149. `bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0 with 72 assertions and zero failures, run in the quality job as the step `Prove the question channel and the scheduled digest`, GitHub Actions run 33520527441 on 3699821, step conclusion success. The full run is quoted in docs/reports/2026-09-01-poc-builder-ask-01-digest-01.md section 5. SILENCE, CASE 6: the first run records a baseline and sends nothing, two further runs against an unchanged board send nothing, and a decide() mutated to always send IS required to send on that same unchanged board and does, with an unmutated control proved to send first. SPEAKING, CASE 7: each of the four conditions independently produces send=true with its reason named. LEADING AND REPEATING, CASE 8: three consecutive runs with one question outstanding send three digests, the first line of each is STILL WAITING ON YOU, the repeated text still carries the question, the recommendation and the reply line, the whole rendered text passes assertPlain with zero card ids, ruling ids, pull request numbers, links or file paths, and once the question is answered and consumed the next run goes quiet. WIRING, CASE 9: install.sh installs com.ai.rc-poc-digest and creates the answer spool, `bash -n scripts/poc/digest.sh` exits 0, and plutil lints the plist. NOT YET INSTALLED ON THE MAC: digest.sh is a deployed copy under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin and the launchd agent does not exist until scripts/poc/install.sh is re-run.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND BUILT 2026-09-01 BY POC-BUILDER, FROM THE SAME OWNER DISPATCH AS ASK-01, in the same pull request at the owner's instruction.

WHY IT IS A THIRD AGENT AND NOT A STEP IN THE WORK HARNESS. The harness runs on a cycle chosen for building and can hold its lock for forty five minutes, so a digest attached to it arrives when the build finished rather than when he starts work, and goes silent on exactly the night the build did not run, which is the night he most needs to hear something. The responder's sixty second agent is the wrong clock in the other direction. Three labels, three schedules, three locks.

THE SILENCE RULE IS THE POINT OF THE CARD AND IS THE EASIEST THING TO QUIETLY REMOVE, which is why its assertion is mutation tested rather than merely asserted: a decide() that always sends is required to fail case 6.

IT IS ON THE PHASE 2 BOARD because the harness cards live here, per R-041 and R-061.

scripts/poc/install.sh MUST BE RE-RUN ON THE MAC before this agent exists. digest.sh is a deployed copy under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin like run.sh and responder.sh, and the launchd agent is not bootstrapped until the installer runs.

cards.title: The digest stops truncating the escalation recommendation, which is the one field the escalation rubric calls mandatory.
cards.plain: When the system asks the owner a question, it currently cuts his recommended answer off mid-sentence before sending it, and the cut is invisible on the receiving end. Send the whole thing.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0, extended with a case that PROVES the defect and its fix: an escalation whose recommendation is longer than 200 characters is rendered by the digest with its LAST characters present in the output. THAT CASE MUST FAIL BEFORE THE FIX AND THE PR MUST SHOW BOTH RESULTS. PLUS: no other field's truncation is changed by this card, asserted by the same run still passing every existing case.
cards.defaults:
THE RECOMMENDATION IS RENDERED WHOLE, ACROSS LINES IF IT MUST BE. A message split over several lines is legible; a sentence that stops mid-word is not, and the reader cannot tell which happened.

THE OTHER TRUNCATIONS STAY. notify.mjs cuts titles to 90, questions to 200 and change lines to 140, and those are summaries of things that have a full text somewhere the reader can reach. The recommendation has no such elsewhere: the digest IS where it is read.

IF THE TRANSPORT HAS A HARD LIMIT, THE MESSAGE SPLITS. It does not silently shorten. A limit belongs to the transport and the fix belongs to the transport, never to the field.
cards.notes:
SALVAGED FROM PULL REQUEST #143, closed unmerged 2026-09-02. Its LEARNINGS entry deliberately authored no card, on the reasoning that a second digest renderer was in flight and a card written against notify.mjs might be a card against a renderer on its way out. That entry says in terms: 'The next TRIAGE that still sees the truncation on main should author it.'

IT IS STILL ON MAIN AND IT IS IN TWO PLACES. scripts/poc/notify.mjs line 397 renders firstLine(e.recommendation, 160) and line 415 renders firstLine(e.recommendation, 180). scripts/poc/digest.mjs, the newer renderer, passes it through sanitize with no limit, so the two paths disagree about the same field.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS. DOCTRINE-TRIAGE's escalation rubric says an escalation with no recommendation is not finished. The owner reads the digest. So the field the rubric protects is the field the transport cuts, and the cut is silent: a recommendation of 800 characters and one of 160 look identical on the receiving end, with the alternative option and the whole IF UNANSWERED line gone. The run that found it was writing escalations averaging 900 characters.

cards.title: P2-13's rotation checklist names R-082's grant explicitly, because a checklist that names two grants by id and leaves the third to a blanket phrase will revoke two.
cards.plain: The credential shutdown list must name every permission it is meant to take away. One permission was created after that list was written and is covered only by a vague phrase, so it would survive the shutdown it was supposed to end.
cards.acceptance: ARTEFACT: P2-13's acceptance field on docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json names R-082 explicitly as a tickable item, alongside the grants it already names. PLUS COMMAND: `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0. PLUS: a check that fails when a ruling in decisions/inbox.md grants a terminal capability and no revocation checklist names its id, OR, if that check is judged not worth its false positives, a written statement in the PR of why, with the alternative that was chosen.
cards.defaults:
NO EXISTING RULING IS EDITED. R-082 stands untouched. This card changes a CHECKLIST, which is a forward-looking instrument, not a record.

THE STALE PRECONDITION LINE STAYS A PRECONDITION. P2-13's capability clause ends 'THIRTEEN FILES ARE PENDING TODAY', and none are. The box is not converted into a statement of fact: it is a precondition to be re-checked on rotation day against whatever the highest migration number is then. Rewording it to say 'no files are pending' would make it false the next time somebody authors a migration.

THE CHECK IS THE PREFERRED HALF AND THE BOARD EDIT IS THE FLOOR. A checklist that has to be maintained by remembering is the instrument that already failed here once.
cards.notes:
SALVAGED FROM PULL REQUEST #143, closed unmerged 2026-09-02. Verified on main before authoring: P2-13's card carries no occurrence of the string R-082 anywhere in any field, and CLAUDE.md 8.7's checklist covers it only through the blanket phrase 'reverting section 8 to Ivan-only applies'.

THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART. R-072 wrote P2-13's capability clause. R-082 created a NEW grant of exactly the class that clause exists to revoke, AFTER it was written, so the clause could not have known about it. Nothing in the repository connects the two. This is the second capability edge that has gone unauthorable, and the first was recorded and then not acted on.

cards.title: Id allocation becomes atomic and CI refuses a duplicate ruling id or a duplicate card id across all boards.
cards.plain: Two different pieces of work were given the same reference number, twice now, because the rule that was supposed to keep them apart was written down and never enforced by anything. Make the numbering impossible to collide, and have the build refuse a collision.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a new check exits 0 on a clean tree and is wired into quality.yml as its own named step. IT MUST BE PROVEN ON FIXTURES THAT FAIL, each shown in the PR with its non-zero exit: two cards sharing an id on the SAME board; two cards sharing an id on DIFFERENT boards; two rulings sharing an id in decisions/inbox.md. PLUS: allocation is made atomic by a committed counter or by a role prefix in the id, and whichever is chosen, a second terminal allocating at the same time cannot produce the same id. PLUS COMMAND: `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards still exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE MECHANISM IS THE EXECUTOR'S JUDGEMENT, on the owner's instruction: a committed counter or a role prefix in the id, whichever holds up better under two terminals running at once. Whichever is chosen is written down with the reason, because the next collision will be argued about.

NO EXISTING ID IS RENUMBERED. Rulings and cards already on main keep their ids, collisions included, and history is never rewritten to make a check pass. Where two ids already collide, the check's baseline records the pair with the reason, exactly as check-card-ids does for its allow-list.

THE CHECK READS ALL THREE BOARDS AND decisions/inbox.md, and the file list is explicit rather than a directory glob, for the same reason check-card-ids gives: a new board appearing in docs/board/ should be a line in a diff.

IT ASSERTS ITS OWN INPUT COUNT AGAINST ITS MATCH COUNT AND FAILS WHEN THEY DIVERGE. A duplicate check that parses zero ids reports no duplicates. That is the defect class docs/LEARNINGS.md names, and this check is exactly the shape that falls into it.

evidence.ref: #PENDING, scripts/poc-free/check-unique-ids.mjs and decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID, both wired into quality. npm run check:unique-ids exits 0 over 129 card ids across three boards and 86 ruling ids, 0 redefined against main. npm run prove:unique-ids exits 0 over eleven fixture cases: a duplicate card id on one board, the same card id on two boards, a duplicate ruling id, AN ID REDEFINED AGAINST origin/main which is the #143 case, a counter that has not advanced, a ruling-shaped heading the regex cannot parse, and a board with zero cards, each paired with a control that passes on the same fixture.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, as a ruling on the second collision of this class: 'Namespaced by author is doctrine and is not enforced by anything.'

THE SECOND COLLISION IS THE ONE THAT CLOSED PULL REQUEST #143. R-083 through R-089 were written on that branch while R-083 through R-086 were being written on main with completely different meanings. Three ruling ids ended up stranded on a conflicting pull request that was then closed unmerged, and the only thing that caught it was a human reading both.

WHY A COUNTER OR A PREFIX AND NOT JUST A CHECK. A check catches the collision after both authors have done the work; allocation being atomic prevents the work from being done twice. The card requires both because they solve different halves and neither substitutes for the other.

SHIPPED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR.

THE MECHANISM IS A COMMITTED COUNTER, NOT A ROLE PREFIX, and the judgement the card left to the executor is recorded here with its reason. decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID holds one id and is advanced in the SAME COMMIT as the ruling that consumes it. It is one line, so two terminals allocating at once produce a merge conflict on that line, which is the loudest signal git has. A role prefix would make collisions structurally impossible and would fork a namespace that ninety rulings and every cross reference already use, so every future reader would have to know both schemes and which era a citation belongs to.

THE COUNTER ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT #143, AND THAT IS WHY THERE ARE TWO HALVES. Both branches were cut from the same main and neither merged, so no conflict ever surfaced. The check therefore reads origin/main as well as the working tree and refuses a ruling id whose heading differs from the same id on main. Within each side the ids were perfectly unique; the collision existed only between them, and nothing in the repository was asking that question.

IT ASSERTS ITS OWN INPUT COUNT AGAINST ITS MATCH COUNT, because a duplicate check that parses zero ids finds zero duplicates. Every heading that LOOKS like a ruling is counted, every one PARSED as a ruling is counted, and a divergence not explained by the one documented exception, the R-NNN template line at the top of the inbox, is a hard failure. That is docs/LEARNINGS.md's named class applied to the shape most likely to fall into it.

THE TOLERATED LIST IS COMMITTED EMPTY, on purpose. The check was written against a record with no duplicates, so the first entry anybody adds is a decision to tolerate one, with a reason next to it, rather than a silent widening. No id is renumbered to make the check pass and no history is rewritten.

CLAUDE.md GAINS SECTION 8b, because a rule that lives only in a script is a rule the next session does not read before it allocates.

cards.title: The ruling allocator reads open pull request branches as well as main, and REFUSES rather than hand out an id somebody has already claimed.
cards.plain: Two people writing decisions at the same time can be given the same decision number, because the numbering only looks at work that has already been accepted. It has happened. The numbering must look at work still in review too, and stop rather than hand out a number that is taken.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named check exits 0 on a clean tree and exits NON-ZERO, naming the branch and the id, when any open pull request branch has written or reserved the id that decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID is about to hand out. THAT REFUSAL MUST BE PROVEN ON THE THREE CASES THAT ACTUALLY OCCURRED, each as its own fixture and each failing before the change: (a) two open branches writing the SAME id with different headings, which is triage/20260902-070904 and triage/20260903-070005 both writing R-090 and R-091; (b) main handing out an id a branch had already reserved in its own counter, which is R-096, written on main by PR #179 while triage/20260902-070904 had already advanced its counter to R-096; (c) a counter advanced on a branch that never merged, leaving a permanent hole, which is R-087 to R-095 absent from main while main sits at R-097. PLUS: a control case where two branches allocate DIFFERENT ids and the check exits 0, so it does not refuse every concurrent author. PLUS: the check runs in quality on every pull request and is NOT path-filtered. PLUS COMMAND: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
cards.defaults:
REFUSE, NEVER RENUMBER. CLAUDE.md 8b says no id is ever renumbered to make a check pass, and that binds this card: the check reports the collision and the human decides, it does not silently pick the next free number.

READ THE BRANCHES FROM THE REMOTE, NOT FROM A LOCAL CLONE. A local clone can be stale by hours and a stale clone reading clean is exactly the failure this check exists to prevent. Prefer the GitHub API for the open pull request list, and fall back to `git ls-remote` plus `git show origin/<branch>:decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID`.

A CLOSED OR MERGED PULL REQUEST DOES NOT RESERVE ANYTHING. Only OPEN ones. An id on a closed branch is free, and treating it as taken would burn ids for nothing.

THE HOLE IS NOT REPAIRED BY THIS CARD. R-087 to R-095 stay missing from main. History is not rewritten and a gap in a ruling sequence costs nothing except a reader wondering; this card stops the NEXT one.

WHERE THE CHECK LIVES IS THE EXECUTOR'S CHOICE, but it belongs beside npm run check:unique-ids, which already answers the sibling question and answers it only against main. Extending that script is preferred to adding a second one, because two checks asking about the same file is how one of them stops being read.

IT MUST NOT REQUIRE A CREDENTIAL TO PASS. A check that is skipped when a token is absent is a check that is absent. With no API access it falls back to the remote refs, and if it can obtain neither it FAILS rather than reporting clean, which is the rule check-removal-safety already follows.

evidence.ref: Branch card/rule-04, cut from main at d3a8474. THE CHECK: scripts/poc-free/check-open-branch-ids.mjs, run in quality as check:open-branch-ids, NOT path-filtered. It reads every OPEN pull request branch, compares the ruling ids THIS branch adds beyond main against the ids each other open branch adds beyond main, and REFUSES when one id carries different heading text on two branches. Redefinition against main is left to check-unique-ids, so the two checks do not fight over one finding. THE PROOF: npm run prove:open-branch-ids, 8 of 8, each case on a throwaway repository built for it. REFUSING CASES: two open branches claiming one id with different headings, which reproduces the R-090 and R-091 pair; and an unreadable branch, which REFUSES rather than reporting clean. CONTROL CASES THAT MUST PASS: two branches allocating different ids; the SAME ruling on both branches from a shared base, which is one ruling on two branches and not two wearing one id; and an id redefined against main, which belongs to the other check. THE INPUT COUNT IS ASSERTED AGAINST THE COMPARISON COUNT, so a silently skipped branch is a failure rather than a clean report. FAILS CLOSED WITH NO BRANCH LIST: without the GitHub API it exits 2 rather than reporting OK, because 'I could not look' and 'nothing is claimed' must never render as the same result. RUNS AT MERGE TIME AND NOT AT AUTHORING TIME: required_status_checks.strict is true on main, so a branch must be up to date before it merges, and this check's LAST run is therefore the one immediately before the merge.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 BY EXECUTOR, FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, WHICH NAMED R-096 AS THE INSTANCE. Verified against the live repository before authoring rather than transcribed, and the verification found the defect is WIDER than the dispatch described.

WHAT WAS READ, AND WHEN: 2026-09-03, from origin.

  decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID on main            R-098
  ruling headings on main                     R-080..R-086, then R-096, R-097
  triage/20260903-070005 (PR #172) writes     R-087..R-091, counter R-092
  triage/20260902-070904 (PR #157) writes     R-090..R-095, counter R-096

THREE DISTINCT FAILURES, NOT ONE:

  1. TWO OPEN PULL REQUESTS WRITE R-090 AND R-091 WITH DIFFERENT HEADINGS. Neither has merged, so npm run check:unique-ids is green on both: it compares each branch against MAIN, and within each side the ids are perfectly unique. This is the same shape as the incident CLAUDE.md 8b was written about, and the mechanism 8b installed does not catch it.
  2. R-096 WAS HANDED OUT TWICE. PR #179 took it from main's counter and merged it. PR #157 had already advanced its own counter to R-096 on an open branch. The dispatch names this instance.
  3. R-087 TO R-095 ARE A HOLE ON MAIN. Nine ids are reserved on branches that have not merged, and main jumped from R-086 to R-096. check:unique-ids requires only that the counter is AHEAD of the highest written, which R-098 over R-097 satisfies, so the hole is invisible to it.

WHY THE COUNTER DID NOT PREVENT ANY OF IT. CLAUDE.md 8b says the counter is one line so two terminals allocating at once produce a merge conflict, which is the loudest signal git has. That is TRUE ONLY WHEN BOTH BRANCHES REACH THE SAME MERGE. Two branches that never merge into each other never conflict, and both were cut from main independently. THE COUNTER CONVERTS A RACE INTO A CONFLICT ONLY AT MERGE TIME, AND ALLOCATION HAPPENS HOURS EARLIER.

NOT BUILT. Authored only, per the dispatch. RULE-03 WAS NOT TAKEN AND THE REASON IS THIS CARD'S OWN SUBJECT: RULE-03 is already claimed on triage/20260903-070005, which is open and unmerged, so taking it would have been the exact defect being carded. RULE-04 was checked against main and against all six open branches before it was used.

BUILT 2026-09-04. IT HAD BITTEN THREE TIMES BY THEN, AND THE THIRD HAPPENED WHILE THIS CARD SAT OPEN:

  R-096  PR #179 took it from main's counter and merged it, while PR #157 had already advanced its own counter to R-096.
  R-098  allocated on board/dispatch-20260903 after a MANUAL SWEEP of main and six open branches found it free. By the next morning PR #184 existed and had also taken it. THE SWEEP WAS TRUE WHEN IT RAN.
  R-090  and R-091 written by BOTH #172 and #157, with different headings, neither merged.

R-098 IS THE CASE THAT SETTLES THE DESIGN. A human sweep cannot be the mechanism, because branches are opened while you work. That is why the answer is a check running in CI on every pull request rather than a procedure in a document, and why it must run at merge time: under required_status_checks.strict the branch is refreshed immediately before merging, so the last run of this check is the one whose answer is still true when the merge happens.

cards.title: MERGE IS APPLY on this repository, and the migration doctrine does not know it. Decide whether the integration keeps writing production, then make CLAUDE.md section 8 describe whichever answer is chosen.
cards.plain: Right now, the moment a database change is approved and merged, it goes straight into the live database on its own. Nobody runs it and nothing checks it first. Every safety rule we wrote assumes a person or a script does that step. Either we turn the automatic path off, or we accept it and rewrite the rules to match what actually happens, but the two cannot stay in disagreement.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: does the Supabase GitHub integration keep applying merged migrations to production, or is it turned off so the applier is the only path?
CONTEXT: a Supabase Preview check from the GitHub app `supabase` runs on every push to main against the production project and applies merged migrations. PROVEN BY PREDICTION WITH A CONTROL on 2026-09-03: before merging, applied_ledger_version() was 0031 and both extraction_drafts.page_count and extraction_drafts.document_source returned 42703 absent. PR #180 carrying page_count was merged, PR #177 carrying document_source was left open, and within two minutes the ledger read 0032, page_count was PRESENT and document_source was still absent. The unmerged twin is the control. CLAUDE.md 3.1 says merging a migration file changes nothing in any database, and that sentence is the basis of the grant separating merge from apply. It is false here. This is a vendor and a console decision, items 4 and 7 of the closed escalation list in DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 6 under R-057, so it is not the executor's to make.
OPTIONS: (a) TURN THE INTEGRATION OFF for production applies. scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs becomes the only path again, every apply is journalled and asserted, and 8.5, 8.6 and 8.8 mean what they say. Cost: someone runs the applier for every migration, which is the friction R-082 was written to remove. (b) KEEP IT AND REWRITE SECTION 8 TO DESCRIBE IT. Merging becomes applying, review moves entirely to the pull request, and the destructive-statement stop must be enforced BEFORE merge by a check rather than at apply time by the applier. Cost: a merge becomes irreversible against production, and that check has to exist before this is safe. (c) LEAVE IT. Not viable, listed only to be refused: the rules and the behaviour already disagree, and the next DROP TABLE merge finds out which wins.
RECOMMENDATION: (b), keep it and rewrite section 8, but ONLY AFTER a pre-merge check refuses a row-destroying statement in any migration file on a pull request. That check is small, it is the same pgsql-parser pass the applier already performs, and it restores the one protection (b) otherwise removes. Why (b) over (a): the integration has applied at least five migrations correctly and the friction it removes is real, while the danger is concentrated entirely in the destructive class, which a pre-merge check covers completely.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: every migration merged from now on applies to production with no pre-check, no in-transaction assertion, no post-check and no journal, and 8.6 protects nothing. A merged DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE would execute against production despite the rule saying it is never auto-applied. Nothing else on either board is blocked by this.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named check, run in quality, exits 0 on a clean tree and exits NON-ZERO naming the file and quoting the statement when any migration file added by the pull request contains DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE. It parses with pgsql-parser, the same real PostgreSQL grammar the applier uses, and never with a regex. PROVEN ON FOUR FIXTURES, each failing before the change: one DROP TABLE, one TRUNCATE, one DELETE, and one CONTROL containing DROP CONSTRAINT and DROP INDEX which must PASS because neither removes a row. PLUS: it is NOT path-filtered, because a filter would skip it on exactly the pull request that renames a migration into scope. PLUS: CLAUDE.md section 8 states in its own words which of the two paths writes production and what each guarantees, and 3.1's sentence that merging a migration changes nothing in any database is removed or corrected. PLUS: docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md says which applies are terminal-run and journalled and which are integration-applied. PLUS COMMAND: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE VENDOR ANSWER IS IVAN'S. THE PRE-MERGE CHECK IS NOT. Build the check whichever way he rules: under (a) it is a second line of defence behind the applier, under (b) it is the only one. It is therefore NOT blocked on the answer and may be built first, and building it first is recommended precisely because it is what makes (b) safe to choose.

DO NOT DISABLE THE INTEGRATION FROM A TERMINAL. It is a console action on a third-party vendor, on the R-057 closed list twice over, and turning off a path that has been silently applying migrations correctly could strand a merged migration unapplied with nobody realising the path changed.

DO NOT PATH-FILTER THE NEW CHECK. CLAUDE.md 3.1 says a paths filter on the workflow kills the self-merge grant; the same reasoning applies in miniature. A check that skips is a check that reports success without running.

DROP CONSTRAINT, DROP INDEX, DROP POLICY, DROP TRIGGER AND DROP DEFAULT ARE NOT IN THE FORBIDDEN SET, and the control fixture exists so that stays true. CLAUDE.md 8.6 already draws the line at statements that REMOVE ROWS, and a check refusing a constraint drop would make a wrong constraint permanent.

DROP FUNCTION IS ALSO NOT IN THE FORBIDDEN SET AND IS ALSO NOT IN THE CONTROL FIXTURE, because 8.6 permits it only under an additional assertion about dependents that a pre-merge check cannot evaluate without a database. Left out of this card deliberately, and said out loud rather than decided quietly.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 BY EXECUTOR, from a finding this session PROVED rather than suspected.

HOW IT WAS ESTABLISHED, because a claim this large should say. APPLY-LOG.md listed 0028 to 0031 as pending while production reported them applied, and every card report said authored and merged, NOT applied. The obvious reading was a missing journal entry. Searching for the applies AS EVENTS found nothing: no commit ever wrote an APPLIED heading for any of the four, PRODUCTION-WRITES.md has no row, and there is no pre-check, post-check, assertion count or actor anywhere.

THE MECHANISM WAS THEN CONFIRMED BY PREDICTION, WITH A CONTROL. Two migrations both numbered 0032 existed the same day: page_count on PR #180 and document_source on PR #177. Before merging either, applied_ledger_version() was 0031 and both columns returned 42703. #180 was merged, #177 was left open. Within two minutes the ledger read 0032, page_count was PRESENT, document_source still absent. The Supabase Preview check on the merge commit completed 2026-09-03T21:33:39Z. Same day, same register, same shape: only the merged one landed.

WHAT IT BREAKS, each a sentence somebody relied on:

  - CLAUDE.md 3.1: merging a migration file changes one text file and changes nothing in any database. FALSE HERE.
  - CLAUDE.md 8.6: a migration containing DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE is never auto-applied. Every TERMINAL obeys it; the integration is not a terminal.
  - CLAUDE.md 8.8: a production write with no row in one of the two journals is a violation. Written for terminals, broken by a party it does not describe.
  - R-082: the applier is the only permitted path to a production apply. It is the only path a TERMINAL may take, which is a much smaller claim.
  - The pending register is not a statement about production. It is a statement about what a terminal has applied.

THE GENERALISATION IS IN docs/LEARNINGS.md: a repository's doctrine describes the actors it knows about, so before relying on a control, ask what ELSE can perform the action it controls. The gap is invisible precisely because every actor you audit is compliant.

BLOCKED ON IVAN FOR THE VENDOR DECISION ONLY, per section 4, and the question carries a recommendation and a stated impact. The pre-merge check in the defaults is NOT blocked and is the recommended first move under either answer. NOTHING ELSE ON EITHER BOARD IS BLOCKED BY THIS.

cards.title: check-pending-schema-reads is blind to `alter type ... add value`, so no enum addition can ever force a capability gate.
cards.plain: One of our safety checks reads database changes and warns when new code would use something the live database does not have yet. It only recognises some kinds of change. For one common kind it stays silent, so that mistake would reach the live system with nothing complaining.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run check:pending-schema-reads` exits NON-ZERO, naming the file and the label, when a source file under lib/, app/ or components/ writes an enum label that a PENDING migration adds and that file imports no capability gate. THAT CASE MUST FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE, proven by a fixture in scripts/poc-free/prove-schema-direction.mjs reconstructing EXT-16's shape: a pending `alter type ... add value` plus a source file naming the new label. PLUS: a CONTROL where the same file DOES import a gate and the check exits 0, so it does not refuse every mention of a string. PLUS: the extraction stops using a hand-written pattern per statement kind and asks the grammar, or states in the file why it cannot. `scripts/poc-free/check-no-destructive-migration.mjs` already parses migrations with pgsql-parser and can be read for how. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run prove:schema-direction` still passes every existing case, so the widening breaks nothing. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
WIDEN THE EXTRACTION, DO NOT SPECIAL-CASE ENUMS. The defect is that objectsAddedBy names three statement shapes by regex and everything else is invisible. Adding a fourth regex for `alter type` fixes this instance and leaves the next one. Parsing with pgsql-parser and enumerating what is seen is the shape that stops recurring, and there is now a working example of exactly that in the repository.

FALSE POSITIVES ARE ACCEPTABLE HERE AND SILENCE IS NOT. The check's own header says the rule is deliberately crude and that a short list a human reads beats a heuristic nobody trusts. Widening it will flag files that name a label for unrelated reasons; those go in EXEMPT with a written reason, exactly as the twelve current entries do.

DO NOT REMOVE THE KEYWORD SANITY CHECK. EXT-15 added a refusal for an extracted object name that is a SQL keyword, after the `if` incident. A grammar-based extraction makes it redundant in principle and keeping it costs nothing, and it is the thing that would catch the next wrong capture if the parse is ever bypassed.
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-09-04 WHILE BUILDING EXT-16, and the card exists because the gap was real for that card rather than hypothetical.

WHAT WAS READ: objectsAddedBy in scripts/poc-free/check-pending-schema-reads.mjs matches exactly three shapes, `create table`, `alter table ... add column` and `create or replace function`/`create function`. A grep for `alter\s+type` in that file returns ZERO. An enum addition is therefore invisible to it.

WHY THAT MATTERS CONCRETELY. EXT-16's migration 0034 adds the label `reconciliation_failed` to public.extraction_error_code. Code writing that label before the migration is applied gets 22P02, invalid input value for enum, on the callback path, which surfaces as a 500 to Make. NOTHING WOULD HAVE REFUSED IT: EXT-16 added hasReconciliationFailedCode because its absence would not have been caught, not because a check demanded it. That is the exact inverse of how the guard is supposed to work.

THE COMPARISON THAT MAKES THE FIX OBVIOUS. check-no-destructive-migration.mjs, built the same day, parses with pgsql-parser, enumerates every statement kind it classifies, and FAILS CLOSED on anything outside that set. It sees AlterEnumStmt without anybody having thought about enums, because it asks the grammar instead of guessing shapes. That is the difference between the two designs and it is why this card recommends the second.

NOT BUILT. Authored only, per the dispatch.

cards.title: supabase/setup-cli is pinned to `version: latest`, which makes CI non-reproducible and rate-limits under ordinary pull request volume.
cards.plain: Our automated checks download a tool without saying which version they want. That means the same code can pass today and fail tomorrow for reasons nobody changed, and on a busy day the download itself is refused and the check fails for no real reason.
cards.acceptance: PLUS: `.github/workflows/quality.yml` pins `supabase/setup-cli` to an EXACT version rather than `latest`, and the version is written next to a comment saying which behaviours the suite depends on, naming at minimum that `supabase db reset` wraps each migration FILE in one transaction, because that is the behaviour P3-33 already paid for. PLUS COMMAND: a named check exits NON-ZERO when any GitHub action in that workflow is pinned to `latest` or to a floating major, and exits 0 otherwise, so the next unpinned action is refused rather than discovered. THAT CHECK MUST FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE, proven against the workflow as it stands today. PLUS: the run that follows the change is green, which is the only evidence that the pinned version is actually usable.
cards.defaults:
PIN, DO NOT ADD A TOKEN. Passing GITHUB_TOKEN to setup-cli removes the rate limit and leaves the reproducibility half untouched, which is the larger of the two problems. Pinning fixes both, because a pinned version needs no API call to resolve.

PICK THE VERSION THAT IS GREEN TODAY, not the newest. The point is to stop the version moving, and choosing a version the suite has never run is a different change wearing this card's number.

THE CHECK COVERS EVERY ACTION IN THE FILE, not only setup-cli. actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 are floating majors and a major can change runner behaviour. Whether to pin those to a sha is the executor's call; if they are left floating, the check's allow-list carries them with a written reason, the way check-pending-schema-reads carries its exemptions.
cards.notes:
OBSERVED 2026-09-03 ON RUN 33810964883, pull request #177, head be2a249:

  ##[error]Failed to resolve latest Supabase CLI release: rate limit exceeded

The job failed at `Start local Supabase`, before a single test ran. Re-running it passed with no change to the code, which is the signature of a flake rather than a defect in the branch.

TWO DEFECTS IN ONE LINE, AND THE TRANSIENT ONE IS THE LESS IMPORTANT.

  1. `version: latest` resolves through an UNAUTHENTICATED GitHub API call, which rate-limits. Six pull requests in one evening was enough on this account.
  2. `latest` ALSO MAKES CI NON-REPRODUCIBLE. The same commit can pass today and fail tomorrow because a CLI released in between changed behaviour, and the failure would present as the pull request's fault. This is not theoretical here: P3-33 had to split migration 0030 from 0031 because `supabase db reset` wraps each FILE in one transaction, which is precisely the kind of behaviour a CLI release can change.

The second is why this card is not just "add a token".

NOT BUILT. Authored only, per the dispatch.

cards.title: A test whose fixture is live state passes on an accidental property of that state, and test-ask-digest.sh case 6 is the instance.
cards.plain: One of our tests copies the real work board and then checks that nothing needs attention. That only worked because nothing happened to need attention that day. The moment something legitimately did, the test failed and the work was blamed instead of the test.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named check exits NON-ZERO when any file under scripts/poc/ or tests/ copies a board JSON, a state JSON or any other live artefact out of the repository into a fixture WITHOUT a neutralisation step, and exits 0 otherwise. THAT CASE MUST FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE against test-ask-digest.sh as it stood on 2026-09-03, and PASS against it as it stands now. PLUS: every site the check finds is either neutralised or carries a written exemption naming the property the assertion depends on, the way check-pending-schema-reads carries its twelve. PLUS COMMAND: `bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
NEUTRALISE, DO NOT FREEZE. A checked-in snapshot of the board would make the test reproducible and would then rot: it would keep passing against a board shape the product no longer has, which is a worse failure because it is silent. Copying the live file and then clearing the specific properties the assertion depends on keeps the fixture current AND makes the dependency explicit.

THE NEUTRALISATION REPORTS WHAT IT DID. test-ask-digest.sh prints `(neutralised N card(s) blocked on ivan for the quiet baseline)`. A silent fixture edit is the same defect one layer down: the test would again be passing for a reason nobody can see.

THIS IS ABOUT FIXTURES, NOT ABOUT READING LIVE STATE. Checks that deliberately read the live board to assert something about it, like check-card-ids and the board validators, are correct and are out of scope. The defect is a test that reads live state and then asserts something the live state is not guaranteed to satisfy.
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 BY BEING BITTEN BY IT. Card MIG-01 was authored blocked_on ivan, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md section 4 requires of a decision a terminal may not make, and three assertions in test-ask-digest.sh turned red:

  FAIL  the first run sent 1 digest(s) with nothing outstanding
  FAIL  an unchanged board produced 3 digest(s)
  FAIL  the digest kept nagging after the question was answered

THE CARD WAS CORRECT, THE DIGEST WAS CORRECT, THE FIXTURE WAS WRONG. Proven rather than assumed: `digest.mjs decide` against the branch board returned send true with reason "a question is outstanding"; against the same board with MIG-01 removed it returned send false. digest.mjs counts a card that is status blocked with blocked_on ivan as outstanding, and it is right to, because that is an owner action nobody else can discharge.

THE ACCIDENTAL PROPERTY, MEASURED: the number of cards blocked on ivan on origin/main was ZERO. The assertion had been passing on that and on nothing else since it was written.

THE FIXTURE WAS FIXED AND THE CARD WAS NOT, and that direction is the point. The cheap exit was to drop MIG-01's blocked_on and go green. A GATE THAT GOES RED WHEN THE DOCTRINE IS OBEYED TRAINS TERMINALS OUT OF OBEYING IT: the next terminal to meet this learns that blocking a card correctly costs a red build. docs/LEARNINGS.md carries that as its own entry.

GENERALISED AS THE DISPATCH ASKED: ANY test whose fixture is live state passes on an accidental property of that state. The fixture carries every property the data happens to have, including the ones nobody chose and nobody wrote down, so the test does not fail when the code breaks, it fails when the data moves.

NOT BUILT. Authored only, per the dispatch.

cards.title: Pull request 143 is disposed of: its three rulings are superseded on main, its new card collides with a card id already there, and it is closed with the record of which ruling replaced what.
cards.plain: A night of finished review work was written up but never published, because the change it sits in clashes with the current version of the project. Everything still worth keeping from it has been rewritten into this batch, so the old one is closed off with a note saying where each piece went, instead of being left open and re-read every week.
cards.acceptance: TWO COMMANDS, BOTH EXIT-CHECKED. (1) `gh pr view 143 --json state --jq .state` prints exactly `CLOSED`, and `gh pr view 143 --json comments --jq '.comments[-1].body'` prints a comment naming R-090 and naming, for each of R-087, R-088 and R-089, the ruling on main that superseded it. (2) `grep -c '^### R-087\|^### R-088\|^### R-089' decisions/inbox.md` prints 0, proving the three ids were never reused on main. THE SECOND COMMAND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS and it must stay in the acceptance line even though it passes today: it is what makes a later run that reaches for R-087 as 'the next free id' go red instead of shipping a second ruling under a number a committed line already carries. PLUS `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json docs/board/rc-board-phase3.json` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE PULL REQUEST IS CLOSED, NOT MERGED, AND NOT RESOLVED. R-090 disposes of all three of its rulings against rulings that are on main: R-087 by R-094's re-audit, R-089 by R-095's re-sweep, and R-088 half void and half re-authored as card P3-36. Resolving the conflict would land three rulings whose content is already on main under different ids, plus a card whose id belongs to a different card. There is nothing left in it to save.

DO NOT REUSE R-087, R-088 OR R-089, EVER, WHATEVER HAPPENS TO THE PULL REQUEST. They are committed lines with ids. The gap in the sequence on main is explained by R-090 and is correct.

DO NOT DELETE THE BRANCH. Closing the pull request is enough and the branch is the only remaining copy of three rulings a future reader may want to read. Deleting it is the loss AUT-18 clause 4 exists to prevent.

IF THE PULL REQUEST HAS ALREADY BEEN CLOSED BY SOMEBODY ELSE BY THE TIME THIS CARD IS WORKED, the comment is still required, because the comment is the record and the closure is not.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-090, run 20260902-070904, from the board sweep rather than from the input report.
WHAT IS IN PULL REQUEST 143. Branch triage/20260901-070544, opened by the previous scheduled review run, merge state CONFLICTING, carrying R-087 the phase 2 gate audit, R-088 the applier finding, R-089 the board sweep, and a new card P3-29.
WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE RESOLVED AND MERGED. A DIFFERENT card P3-29 landed on main in pull request 150 four hours after 143 was opened. Two different cards would answer to one id on one board, which the board validator fails on, and the alternative outcome is that one silently overwrites the other.
THIS IS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE AND THE FIRST ONE IS STILL OPEN. RST-03 is the instance for pull request 126 and has been todo since 2026-08-31. RST-02 and AUT-18 are the class: one picks stuck work up, the other makes it impossible for it to be invisible. Neither has shipped, which is why this is the second time a night of review work has had to be disposed of by hand.

cards.title: The Telegram answer path allocates its ruling id from the counter and advances it, so the repository has one allocator instead of two.
cards.plain: When Ivan answers a question from his phone, the system files that answer under a number it works out for itself instead of taking the next one from the shared list. Two things can end up with the same number, and the published change then fails its own checks. This makes the phone answers use the same list as everybody else.
cards.acceptance: NEW CASES IN A NAMED TEST WIRED INTO THE quality JOB BY NAME, EXITS 0, EACH PROVED TO FAIL FIRST AGAINST THE CURRENT scripts/poc/inbox.mjs WITH THE FAILING OUTPUT QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST. (1) THE ID COMES FROM THE COUNTER: given a fixture repository whose decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID holds R-500 while the highest ruling written in decisions/inbox.md is R-086, the ruling the inbox reader writes is R-500. Against the current file it is R-087, computed by nextRulingId() at line 244 as highest plus one, and THAT IS THE FAILING CASE. (2) THE COUNTER IS ADVANCED IN THE SAME COMMIT: after that run decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID holds R-501, and it is in the SAME commit as the ruling, asserted from `git show --stat HEAD` naming all three of decisions/inbox.md, decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID and the board. Against the current file the counter is neither staged nor changed, and that is the second failing case. (3) A MISSING OR MALFORMED COUNTER REFUSES RATHER THAN FALLING BACK: given a fixture whose counter file is absent, and a second whose counter holds text that is not R-NNN, the reader writes NO ruling, exits non-zero, and logs the reason naming the file. (4) THE CHECK AGREES: `node scripts/poc-free/check-unique-ids.mjs` exits 0 against the fixture tree after a successful write, and exits 1 against the same tree with the counter left where it was. PLUS `npm run check:unique-ids` exits 0 on this repository and `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE COUNTER IS READ, NOT RECOMPUTED. Do not have inbox.mjs derive a value from the inbox and then write that into the counter: that is the same allocator with an extra step, and it collides with a branch holding the counter exactly as it does today. Read the file, use what it says, write what comes next.

REFUSE, NEVER FALL BACK. If the counter is missing or malformed the reader writes no ruling and exits non-zero. A silent fallback to highest-plus-one is the exact defect this card removes, and a fallback that fires only when something is already wrong is the hardest kind to notice.

THE OWNER'S ANSWER IS NOT LOST BY A REFUSAL. The message is already on the spool under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-logs/asks/ and the responder is the only reader of the bot, so a refusal parks the write rather than dropping the answer. Say so in the log line, because a terminal reading 'refused' needs to know whether Ivan has to be asked again. He does not.

CHECK BEFORE COMMIT, LIKE THE VALIDATOR ALREADY IS. inbox.mjs already runs docs/board/validate-board.mjs before it commits, at line 452. Run check-unique-ids.mjs there too, for the same reason and in the same place: the gate belongs before the commit, not before the pull request.

NOTHING ALREADY WRITTEN IS RENUMBERED. R-001 through R-091 stand. CLAUDE.md 8b forbids it and every one of them is cited somewhere.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-070005, under ruling R-087. Produced by docs/reports/2026-09-02-executor-rule-02-id-allocation.md, whose section 2 states that the counter makes allocation atomic because two terminals allocating at once conflict on one line.

VERIFIED ON main AT 3642d79 BEFORE AUTHORING, so the premise is not taken from the report: `grep -rn NEXT-RULING-ID` over the tree returns CLAUDE.md, that report, scripts/poc-free/check-unique-ids.mjs and scripts/poc-free/prove-unique-ids.mjs, and NO caller in scripts/poc/. scripts/poc/inbox.mjs line 244 defines nextRulingId(inboxText) as the highest R-NNN matched plus one; line 430 calls it; line 456 stages decisions/inbox.md and the board and nothing else.

THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE IS RED CI ON THE OWNER'S OWN ANSWER. check-unique-ids.mjs lines 259 to 263 refuse a counter that has not moved past the highest ruling written, so a responder run that appends a ruling makes quality fail on the pull request carrying it.

NOT COVERED BY AUT-16, WHICH WAS CHECKED. AUT-16 is about inbox.mjs resolving a CARD id against every board. This is about the RULING id it allocates. Same file, different defect, and neither acceptance line reaches the other.

cards.title: DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 2's id-allocation requirement is rewritten to match CLAUDE.md 8b, because a role whose rubric must be disobeyed to be correct has a rubric defect.
cards.plain: The rulebook the reviewing role follows still describes the old way of numbering decisions, which was replaced yesterday. A session that follows its own rulebook now produces work that fails the automatic checks. This brings the two documents back into agreement.

evidence.ref: #PENDING-AUT19. All four acceptance clauses run on the head sha: grep -c 'namespaced by author' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md prints 0; grep -c 'renumbering the NEW entry' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md prints 0; grep -c 'NEXT-RULING-ID' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md prints 1 and section 2 requirement 1 carries the three steps of CLAUDE.md 8b; the replacement text names RULE-02 and R-088. node docs/board/validate-board.mjs over all three boards exits 0 and npm run check:unique-ids exits 0.

cards.acceptance: ARTEFACT PLUS COMMANDS, ALL FOUR. (1) `grep -c 'namespaced by author' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md` prints 0. (2) `grep -c 'renumbering the NEW entry' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md` prints 0. (3) `grep -c 'NEXT-RULING-ID' docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md` prints 1 or more, and section 2 requirement 1 carries the three steps of CLAUDE.md section 8b: read the counter, use that id, advance the file in the same commit as the ruling. (4) THE SUPERSESSION IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN SILENT: the replacement text names RULE-02 and R-088, so a reader arriving from an older ruling or report that cites 'the next free one' or 'namespaced by author' lands somewhere that says the rule changed rather than somewhere the phrase has quietly stopped existing. PLUS `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0 and `npm run check:unique-ids` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
DO NOT RESTATE 8b, POINT AT IT. Two copies of an allocation procedure drift, and this card exists because two copies already did. Section 2 requirement 1 states the rule in one line and cites CLAUDE.md section 8b as the authority, the way section 6 cites R-057.

THE OTHER TWO REQUIREMENTS IN SECTION 2 ARE UNTOUCHED. Requirement 2, that Answer-verbatim quotes the report and never writes in Ivan's voice, and requirement 3, that Unblocks names cards or says nothing, are both correct and both load-bearing. Only requirement 1 is stale.

NO EXISTING RULING IS EDITED. R-088 records the finding and stands; this card changes a doctrine file, which is a forward-looking instrument, not a record.

IF THE SWEEP FINDS THE SAME STALENESS ELSEWHERE, FIX IT HERE. Both board doctrine strings and docs/reports/README.md are worth a grep for the same three phrases. A second card for the second copy is how both get half-done.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-070005, under ruling R-088. Produced by docs/reports/2026-09-02-executor-rule-02-id-allocation.md sections 1 and 2.

THIS RUN IS THE EVIDENCE. DOCTRINE-TRIAGE opens by saying it is the whole of TRIAGE's rubric. A session that read it and nothing else would have scanned decisions/inbox.md, found R-086, written R-087 without touching the counter, and shipped a pull request that quality refuses on the counter assertion at check-unique-ids.mjs lines 259 to 263. This run allocated from decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID instead, which is correct and is against the letter of its own rubric.

TRIAGE DOES NOT EDIT GOVERNING DOCUMENTS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A CARD. Its permitted set is rulings, card fields, gate flips, new cards and escalations. AUT-15 is the precedent: the previous correction to this same file was an authoring card, not a TRIAGE edit.

DISTINCT FROM AUT-15, WHICH WAS CHECKED ON ITS BRANCH. AUT-15 corrects the INPUT clause in 'What TRIAGE is', about the report being the only dispatch rather than the only readable file. This corrects requirement 1 of SECTION 2, about id allocation. Different sections, different defects, and AUT-15's branch card/aut-15 at f5c5066 does not touch section 2.

--- SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR, unattended run 20260904-220003 ---
Requirement 1 of section 2 now states the rule in one line and CITES CLAUDE.md
section 8b as the authority, the way section 6 cites R-057. 8b is not restated,
per the card's defaults: two copies of an allocation procedure drift, and this
card exists because two already did. Requirements 2 and 3 are untouched and no
existing ruling was edited.

THE ONE JUDGEMENT THIS CARD FORCED, AND IT IS A CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO RULES.
CLAUDE.md section 9c says a superseded doctrine sentence is QUOTED, marked false
and left in place. This card's acceptance clause 1 requires
`grep -c 'namespaced by author'` to print 0. Quoting the old wording satisfies 9c
and fails the acceptance. THE ACCEPTANCE WON, because it is the machine-checkable
half and section 6 does not ship a card on a clause it fails. The supersession is
written as description instead of quotation: what the old rule told a session to
do, why it is gone, R-088 as the ruling that recorded a session obeying CLAUDE.md
against its own rubric, RULE-02 as the card that changed it, and a closing
sentence addressed to a reader who arrived carrying the old wording. Logged in
docs/LEARNINGS.md as a rule for the next instance.

THE SWEEP THE DEFAULTS ASKED FOR WAS RUN. docs/reports/README.md: clean. The
`doctrine` string on all three boards: clean. docs/LEARNINGS.md line 778 carried
the same stale rule and got a SUPERSEDED paragraph appended rather than an edit,
because a learnings entry is a record and a record is not rewritten. No second
card was authored, per the defaults.

cards.title: The next-card pick sorts on lane then number, not on the raw string, so an unpadded id does not queue two cards behind three that were authored three days later.
cards.plain: The overnight system picks the next job by sorting the job numbers as text, so job 16 comes out ahead of job 8. Two jobs from a week ago are stuck behind three newer ones and will stay there for ever. This makes it count numbers as numbers.
cards.acceptance: NEW CASES IN A NAMED TEST WIRED INTO THE quality JOB BY NAME, EXITS 0, EACH PROVED TO FAIL FIRST AGAINST THE CURRENT scripts/poc/eligible.mjs WITH THE FAILING OUTPUT QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST. (1) THE LIVE CASE: `node scripts/poc/eligible.mjs --board docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json --ids` returns AUT-8 and AUT-9 BEFORE AUT-16, AUT-17 and AUT-18. Against the current file at line 101 the output begins AUT-16,AUT-17,AUT-18,AUT-8,AUT-9 and THAT IS THE FAILING CASE. (2) THE SUFFIX PROPERTY IS PRESERVED, AND IT IS THE HALF MOST LIKELY TO BE BROKEN BY THE FIX: over a fixture board carrying P3-04, P3-04b and P3-05, the order is P3-04, then P3-04b, then P3-05. (3) AN UNPARSEABLE ID IS NOT SILENTLY DROPPED: a fixture card whose id carries no number sorts deterministically and STILL APPEARS in the output, asserted by count, rather than vanishing from the eligible set. PLUS ARTEFACT: CLAUDE.md section 2's Pick paragraph and the ELIGIBILITY sentence in both board doctrine strings are corrected to describe the sort the code performs, since a rule that no longer describes the code is the same defect one layer up. PLUS `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0.
cards.defaults:
SORT ON A TUPLE, NOT ON A PADDED STRING. Build a key of (prefix, number, suffix) and compare it. Padding the string at compare time works until a lane reaches three digits, and it hides the intent.

NOTHING IS RENUMBERED. CLAUDE.md 8b forbids it, and AUT-8 and AUT-9 are cited in reports, rulings and pull requests. The sort changes; the ids do not.

FALL BACK TO THE RAW STRING FOR AN ID THE KEY CANNOT PARSE, NEVER DROP IT AND NEVER THROW. An eligibility selector that silently omits a card is worse than one that orders it oddly, and docs/LEARNINGS.md already names the class where an empty result reads as nothing-to-do.

ONE SORT, ONE PLACE. If digest.mjs, notify.mjs or claim.sh sort ids too, they import the same comparator rather than growing a second one.

THE OTHER PATH WAS WEIGHED AND REJECTED, AND THE REASON IS IN R-090. Enforcing zero padding on NEW ids and tolerating the old ones fixes future lanes and leaves AUT-8 and AUT-9 behind AUT-16 for ever, because the existing ids cannot be renumbered. Do not implement that instead.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-070005, under ruling R-125. NOT FROM THE DISPATCH REPORT: it surfaced at the step of CLAUDE.md section 1's mandatory boot report that requires the next eligible card be named.

VERIFIED BY COMMAND, NOT BY READING. `node scripts/poc/eligible.mjs --board docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json --ids` returns AUT-16,AUT-17,AUT-18,AUT-8,AUT-9,BOARD-01,BOARD-02,CLAIM-01,DIG-01,GATE-03,LEARN-01,P2-20,RST-02,RST-03. scripts/poc/eligible.mjs line 101 sorts with a bare a.id.localeCompare(b.id), which is faithful to CLAUDE.md section 2 as written.

WHAT IT COSTS, NAMED CONCRETELY. AUT-8 strips credentials the scheduled run does not need out of the model process. AUT-9 makes the wall clock cap actually stop a run, which is the defect that cost nine hours and three scheduled windows on 2026-08-27. Both were authored 2026-08-28, both are eligible, and both sit behind three cards authored 2026-08-31.

P3-04b IS THE CONSTRAINT THE FIX MUST NOT BREAK. The phase 3 board's doctrine string depends by name on P3-04b sorting between P3-04 and P3-05, and a naive numeric parse would lose it.

cards.defaults:
ONE COMMIT, AND THE ORDER IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. Restoring card MIG-01 to the board WITHOUT restoring the scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh hunk turns three assertions in that script red, because the fixture copies the live phase 2 board and the digest counts a card that is blocked on ivan as an outstanding question. That script runs in quality on every pull request. The two halves land together or main goes red. This is also why TRIAGE did not restore the two cards itself: it may not write a test file, and the board edit alone is a broken commit.

VERBATIM MEANS VERBATIM. Nothing is improved, reworded, resummarised or brought up to date while restoring it. If a restored line is wrong today, that is a NEW card or a NEW ruling, never an edit made during the restore. A restore that also rewrites is a restore nobody can verify with a diff.

decisions/inbox.md AND decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID ARE OUT OF SCOPE. R-098 is already restored verbatim and the counter is already at R-102, both by the TRIAGE pull request that authored this card, under R-100. Touching either here produces a collision on the two files this repository can least afford one on.

DO NOT RE-AUTHOR MIG-01 OR RULE-04 FROM SCRATCH. Both exist in full at b25dc75. Re-authoring produces a second card for one problem, which DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 5 forbids, and it silently drops whatever the original said that the re-author did not think of.

IF A FILE HAS LEGITIMATELY MOVED ON SINCE b25dc75, THE SUPERSET TEST IS THE RIGHT ONE AND THE EXACT-DIFF TEST IS WRONG. That is why LEARNINGS.md is checked for missing lines only. For APPLY-LOG.md, extraction-v2.md and test-ask-digest.sh the exact diff is correct today, because every change to those three between b25dc75 and now IS the deletion being undone. Check that before assuming it.

THE SIX STALE `pending` LINES GO. `0028` to `0033` are applied, and b25dc75 records them as applied with the evidence. Leaving both the applied entries and the pending lines puts every one of those files in BOTH lists, which tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts fails on.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-220002, under R-099. INPUT REPORT: docs/reports/2026-09-03-executor-sample-ttl-and-document-source.md, section 2 finding 1 and section 6 item 1.
