cards.title: A check refuses a commit that DELETES a ruling id, a card id, or an applied-migration entry that exists on origin/main. check:conflict-residue catches the marker tails a bad resolution leaves; this catches the clean resolution that keeps its own side and drops the other.
cards.plain: Nothing we run can currently notice when a merge silently drops finished work. A merge that resolves a clash by keeping only one side deletes the other side entirely and every check still passes. Add a check that refuses any change which removes a decision, a piece of planned work, or a record of a database change that already exists on the main copy.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named check wired into `.github/workflows/quality.yml`, NOT path-filtered, exits 0 on a clean tree and exits NON-ZERO naming every id or heading that is present on `origin/main` and absent on the branch. It covers three sets: every `### R-NNN` heading in `decisions/inbox.md`, every card `id` across all three boards, and every applied-migration heading in `docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md`. PLUS: it also refuses a `decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID` that is LOWER than the value on `origin/main`. PROVEN ON FOUR FIXTURES, each failing before the change and passing after: one deleting a ruling id, one deleting a card id, one deleting an applied-migration heading, one rolling the counter backwards. PLUS ONE CONTROL FIXTURE THAT MUST PASS: a branch that ADDS ids and headings and deletes none. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:assertion-register` exits 0, so every assertion added here carries its failing case. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
IT COMPARES AGAINST origin/main, THE SAME BASE check:unique-ids ALREADY USES. Do not invent a second notion of the base. When the base cannot be resolved, FAIL OPEN THE OTHER WAY: run the check rather than skipping it, exactly as the applier-proof step does, because the case where the base is unresolvable is the case where a merge is happening.

DO NOT PATH-FILTER IT. CLAUDE.md 3.1 says a paths filter on the workflow kills the self-merge grant, and the same reasoning applies to a step-level filter here: this check exists for merges, and a merge touches whatever it touches. A filtered version would have skipped on 29afb21, which changed thirty-three files.

DELETION IS REFUSED, NOT MADE IMPOSSIBLE. A deliberate removal is legitimate now and then. The escape is an explicit, committed allow-list entry naming the id and the reason, in the shape check-card-ids already uses, committed EMPTY so the first entry is a decision somebody made and can be read in a diff. It is never a flag on the command line and never an environment variable.

APPLIED-MIGRATION HEADINGS ARE MATCHED ON THE FILE NAME, not on the prose around it. APPLY-LOG.md is append-only and its headings carry the migration file name, which is the stable part. Do not parse the descriptive tail.

THE PENDING REGISTER IS NOT IN SCOPE. A file legitimately MOVES from pending to applied, and the pending line is removed in the same pull request by design. Refusing that would refuse every correct apply. Only the APPLIED headings are protected.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-220002, under R-099. INPUT REPORT: docs/reports/2026-09-03-executor-sample-ttl-and-document-source.md.

DEPENDS ON RESTORE-01 AND THE EDGE IS DELIBERATE. This check, run today, would go red against origin/main, because the deleted ids ARE absent right now. Building it before the restore lands means either a red main or an allow-list entry excusing the exact loss the check exists to catch. RESTORE-01 first, then the guard, and the guard is then green from its first run.

WHY IT IS NOT A WIDENING OF check:conflict-residue. That check answers 'did this resolution leave residue behind'. This one answers 'did this resolution leave something OUT'. CLAUDE.md's conflict section already records that a grep for the markers is not the check, because a bad resolution deletes exactly the characters the grep looks for. 29afb21 is the next case along: it deleted whole hunks cleanly, so there was no residue, no invalid JSON, no unparseable markdown and nothing for any existing guard to bite on.

THE FOUR EXISTING GUARDS AND WHY EACH ONE MISSED IT, so this card can be read without R-099 open beside it:
  check:conflict-residue   looks for marker tails; none were left
  check:unique-ids         compares headings that EXIST on both sides; it has no
                           concept of an id that used to exist, and it accepted a
                           counter that had gone backwards because it only
                           requires the counter to be AHEAD of the highest
                           WRITTEN, and deleting R-098 lowered that too
  headers.spec.ts          requires each migration file in EXACTLY ONE of applied
                           or pending; moving all six back to pending keeps them
                           in exactly one
  validate-board.mjs       validates the cards present; a deleted card is not an
                           invalid card

THE GENERALISATION, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE MIG-01 RECORDS IN ITS OWN NOTES: every guard here was built to check that what is PRESENT is correct. None of them checks that what WAS present is still there. Absence is the one state a validator cannot be handed.

cards.title: Land the four stranded pull requests as one reconciliation: fifteen ruling ids, eleven cards, and the apply journal that is currently false about production, three of them conflicting and two pairs of ids colliding with each other.
cards.plain: Four finished pieces of work are sitting unpublished because the files underneath them have moved, and two pairs of them have been given the same reference numbers by mistake. One of the four corrects a record that currently tells us six database changes are waiting when they are already live. This publishes all four together and settles the numbering, because fixing them one at a time makes each next one worse.
cards.acceptance: AGAINST origin/main AFTER THIS CARD SHIPS, ALL SIX EXIT 0, AND EACH IS QUOTED IN THE PULL REQUEST WITH ITS OUTPUT. (1) EVERY STRANDED RULING IS PRESENT EXACTLY ONCE: `git show origin/main:decisions/inbox.md | grep -oE "^### R-[0-9]+" | sort | uniq -d` prints NOTHING, and the count of distinct ruling headings has risen by at least fifteen against e15e928. (2) NO ID MEANS TWO THINGS: `npm run check:unique-ids` exits 0, run AFTER the merge, not only on the branch. (3) THE ELEVEN CARDS ARE ON A BOARD: a node script over all three boards finds MIG-01, RULE-03, RULE-04, AUT-19, P3-35, P3-36, P3-37, BOARD-03, RST-04, RESTORE-01 and GUARD-02, or, for any that this card deliberately drops, the pull request names it and says under which ruling it was dropped. Each surviving card has a non-empty plain, acceptance and defaults. (4) THE APPLY JOURNAL IS NO LONGER FALSE: `grep -c "card de aplicare" docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md` returns a number that matches the count of files under supabase/migrations/ NOT recorded applied, and `npx playwright test tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts` passes, which is the suite that requires every migration file to be in exactly one of the two lists. (5) EVERY COMMITTED REPORT SURVIVES: `git show origin/main:docs/reports/2026-09-04-triage-the-aut-15-merge-revert.md | head -1` and the equivalent for the reports on #157, #172 and #181 each print their title line, per CLAUDE.md section 9b. (6) THE RESOLUTION IS CLEAN: `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` exits 0 on all three boards AND `npm run check:conflict-residue` exits 0, both run BEFORE each commit and quoted, because this card is four conflict resolutions and R-052 exists because three of them landed carrying residue.
cards.defaults:
THE ID RULE IS ALREADY DECIDED AND IS NOT REOPENED. R-107 rules it: a ruling that has never been on main is not history and may be re-allocated a fresh id before it lands, and WHICH SIDE KEEPS THE ID IS DECIDED BY MERGE ORDER, NOT BY MERIT. The pull request landed FIRST keeps the id it wrote; every later one re-allocates from decisions/NEXT-RULING-ID as it then stands, and the re-allocation is written into the renumbered entry naming the id it was drafted under and the branch it was drafted on. Do not weigh which text deserves the number.
THE TWO LIVE COLLISIONS, SO THEY ARE NOT REDISCOVERED: R-090 and R-091 mean different things on #157 and on #172. R-098 means different things on #181 and on #184.
R-103 GOVERNS WHAT #184 CARRIES. Its R-099 and R-100 rest on a premise this run falsified: nothing was reverted from main, and b25dc75 is the tip of #181, never main. R-099 keeps its generalisation and loses its instance, R-100 is moot, RESTORE-01 is not a restore and its work is this card, and GUARD-02 survives on its own merits with its justification corrected. DO NOT EDIT R-099 OR R-100: a ruling is never edited, R-103 is the superseding entry, and the branch keeps them as written.
RESOLVE LOCALLY, NEVER IN THE WEB EDITOR, per R-052. Against the full tree, validator before every commit.
NO FORCE PUSH, on any of the four branches, --force-with-lease included, per CLAUDE.md section 3. A branch whose history needs rewriting gets a new branch, and landing four branches through one new branch is permitted and is probably the shape this takes.
ORDER, WHEN NOTHING ELSE DECIDES: #181 first, because it carries the false-journal fix and that is the only item here with a live external cost.
DROPPING A CARD IS ALLOWED AND MUST BE NAMED. Some of the eleven may be obsolete by the time this runs. Dropping one is a line in the pull request naming the card and the ruling that makes it obsolete, never a silent omission.
THIS CARD MERGES NOTHING IT HAS NOT RESOLVED. A green check on a conflicting pull request is stale, per CLAUDE.md section 3, and `npm run checks:state <pr>` prints the merge state beside the check result.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-107, RUN 20260904-010000, from docs/reports/2026-09-03-executor-sample-ttl-and-document-source.md section 2 defect 1 and section 6 item 1, plus the pull request census this run took at origin/main e15e928.

THE CENSUS, VERBATIM FROM `gh pr list`:
#157 triage/20260902-070904 DIRTY: R-090 to R-095, cards P3-35, P3-36, RST-04, the phase 3 gate audit.
#172 triage/20260903-070005 DIRTY: R-087 to R-091, cards RULE-03, AUT-19, P3-37, BOARD-03.

WHY ONE CARD AND NOT FOUR, WHICH DOCTRINE-TRIAGE SECTION 5 REQUIRES ARGUED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Two pairs collide on ids, so a resolution done alone has to be redone against the next one. #184 cannot be disposed of correctly without #181 open beside it, because R-103 is the finding that #184 measured #181 and called the result a revert. Four resolutions taken separately is four chances to invent a fifth meaning for R-098.

WHY IT IS NOT RST-02 AND NOT AUT-18. RST-02 is the class fix for the sweep that never selected a triage branch. AUT-18 is the class fix for the census that never named an open pull request. Both are still todo and both stay. This is the INSTANCE, and RST-03 is the precedent for an instance card being separate: RST-03 did exactly this for one stranded pull request and is itself still todo.

IT IS ON THE PHASE 2 BOARD because the loose-ends and harness cards live here, per R-041 and R-061, although the content it lands spans both boards.

THE ID IS RST-05 AND NOT RST-04 DELIBERATELY. RST-04 is authored on #157 and is not on main, so check:unique-ids would accept RST-04 here and fail the moment #157 landed.

cards.title: scripts/poc/test-chat-classify.sh is red on main and is in no required check, so the responder classifier has been unproven for as long as anyone can measure.
cards.plain: One of the safety checks on the automatic chat replies has been failing quietly, and nothing ever runs it. If the assistant started treating a stray message as an instruction, nobody would find out from a check.
cards.acceptance: BOTH, AND THE SECOND IS NOT OPTIONAL. (1) `bash scripts/poc/test-chat-classify.sh` exits 0, with the CURRENT failing output quoted in the pull request first, which is `the five outcomes, in order: expected [ignored,empty,ruling,ruling,question], got [ignored,empty,ruling,ruling,answer]`, reproduced in a clean worktree at origin/main so the pull request shows the red it is fixing. (2) `grep -c "test-chat-classify.sh" .github/workflows/quality.yml` prints 1 or more, and the step carries a name comment the way every other proof step in that file does, so the check is findable by name from a run log.
cards.defaults:
FIX WHICHEVER SIDE IS WRONG, ON THE EVIDENCE, AND SAY WHICH IN THE PULL REQUEST. If a committed ruling changed the classifier's behaviour and the test was never updated, the TEST is corrected and that ruling is cited by id. If no such ruling exists, THE CLASSIFIER is wrong and the classifier is fixed, because the narrowness of what counts as an instruction is a security property under CLAUDE.md section 13 and a classifier that has quietly widened is a command surface that has quietly widened.

WHERE THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT DECIDE IT, TAKE THE NARROWER OUTCOME: the fifth message is a QUESTION, not an ANSWER. Misreading a question as an answer acts on something nobody said; misreading an answer as a question asks again. Those two errors are not the same size.

WIRING IT INTO quality IS HALF THE CARD AND SHIPS IN THE SAME PULL REQUEST. A green test that nothing runs is the exact defect this card exists to end, so fixing the assertion without wiring the step fixes nothing that survives the week.

IT IS NOT PATH-FILTERED. CLAUDE.md section 3.1 permits exactly two filtered steps, names them, and says a third is a change to that section rather than an application of it. This step needs no container and no database, so there is nothing to argue for.

DO NOT DELETE THE TEST. A failing test removed is a check that was never run, recorded as a check that passes.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED.

evidence.ref: PR #212, branch card/aut-20. CLAUSE 1: the red reproduced at origin/main 23f34b3 before any edit, exit 1, output quoted verbatim in the pull request body and matching the string the card quotes: expected [ignored,empty,ruling,ruling,question], got [ignored,empty,ruling,ruling,answer]. After the fix, bash scripts/poc/test-chat-classify.sh exits 0 with nine PASS lines and AUT-6 ACCEPTANCE PASSED. CLAUSE 2: grep -c "test-chat-classify.sh" .github/workflows/quality.yml prints 2, and the step is named "Prove the responder classifier" with the comment tag AUT-6-AUT-20-CLASSIFY-PROOF, unfiltered, beside its four siblings. Both clauses re-run in CI by the quality check on the head sha of this pull request.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-112, run 20260904-040001, from docs/reports/2026-09-04-executor-aut-16-board-set.md section 4 finding 2.

THE FINDING WAS VERIFIED BEFORE THIS CARD WAS WRITTEN AND THE VERIFICATION IS THE POINT. The report says the test fails on main, before its own branch, and that it is not wired into quality. The second half is re-checkable from the repository and was re-checked: the quality workflow names twenty two steps and test-chat-classify.sh is in none of them, while its four siblings, test-harness-caps.sh, test-install.sh, test-ask-digest.sh and test-board-set.sh, are each wired in by name with a comment tag.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM. The classifier decides what an incoming Telegram message IS. CLAUDE.md section 13 makes the narrowness of that decision the whole of the channel's security model: identity is checked first, two exact forms are accepted, everything else is logged and never acted on. The one test that holds that shape has been red and unwatched, and the failing case is specifically one where a message that should be classified as a QUESTION is classified as an ANSWER.

AN UNWIRED TEST IS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS IN A WEEK. It is not the same as an assertion with no failing case, which npm run check:assertion-register already catches. This is a whole test file with no runner, which nothing catches, and a check that would notice the class rather than the instance is worth a card if a third one appears.

SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR, run 20260905-040005, PR #212. THE TEST WAS THE WRONG SIDE AND THE CLASSIFIER WAS RIGHT ON ALL FIVE MESSAGES.

The card defaults say to cite the ruling when a committed change moved the classifier and left the test behind. ASK-01, 2026-09-01, CLAUDE.md section 14, gave chat-classify.mjs an ask spool and a ruling spool that it both READS and WRITES, each defaulting to a real directory under the machine log root, with --asks and --rulings to point them elsewhere. This test was written for AUT-6, before either spool existed, and passed neither flag.

SO THE RED WAS A FACT ABOUT A LOG DIRECTORY. The live ask spool held exactly one outstanding question, and ASK-01 rule 3 says ordinary text with exactly one question outstanding IS the answer to it. The fifth fixture message was routed as an answer, correctly. In CI, where that directory does not exist, the same unchanged test would have gone GREEN for an equally accidental reason, so wiring it in without this fix would have bought a step that proves nothing.

THE HALF THE CARD DID NOT KNOW ABOUT IS THAT IT ALSO WROTE. Every run spooled the fixture two ruling messages into the real pending ruling spool, where inbox.mjs reads them as decisions the owner made, and spooled the fifth message into the real answer spool as an owner instruction against whichever card was outstanding. The consumed directory holds both fixture files dated 2026-09-04, so inbox.mjs had already picked up two fabricated rulings once. The three files produced during this run were moved into a quarantine directory outside the live spools rather than deleted, and both live spools were confirmed empty afterwards. The 2026-09-04 pair is recorded, not acted on.

THE FIX IS THE TEST AND NOTHING ELSE. Not one line of chat-classify.mjs is touched. Every invocation now passes both flags at temp directories through one classify() helper, the isolation is itself asserted rather than assumed, and ASK-01 rule 3 is pinned against a fixture spool holding one question. Nine assertions, up from six.

THE STEP IS UNFILTERED, per the defaults and CLAUDE.md section 3.1, which permits exactly two filtered steps and names both.

cards.title: A scheduled run reports when its own deployed copy of the harness differs from the repository, because the deployed scripts and the worktree modules do not upgrade together.
cards.plain: The nightly automation runs from copies installed on the machine, and nothing notices when those copies fall behind what was actually built. A session can silently be following last week's instructions and its report would look normal.
cards.acceptance: `bash scripts/poc/test-install.sh` exits 0 WITH NEW CASES ADDED, or a sibling test file wired into the quality job BY NAME, proving BOTH halves against a CONSTRUCTED fixture install root and never against /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin, which test-install.sh already refuses to touch and whose refusal is asserted at its line 232. BOTH halves PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current tree with the failing output quoted in the pull request. (1) DRIFT IS REPORTED: given a fixture install root whose deployed run.sh differs by one byte from the repository copy at the commit being executed, the run writes a drift line naming the file and the first twelve characters of both sha256 sums to its log AND appends an escalation to docs/poc/state.json. (2) NO DRIFT IS SILENT: given byte-identical copies, neither the log line nor the escalation appears. PLUS `bash -n scripts/poc/run.sh` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
IT REPORTS, IT NEVER RE-INSTALLS. A run that reinstalls its own harness is rewriting the script it is currently executing, and bash reads a script incrementally from disk, so the failure mode is a run that changes behaviour halfway through with nothing in the log to say so. install.sh stays a human-invoked command and CLAUDE.md section 15 stays as written.

A DRIFT IS AN ESCALATION, NOT A REFUSAL. The run continues. A stale run that says it is stale is strictly better than no run, and refusing to start would convert a reporting gap into an outage the first time somebody edits a script and forgets the reinstall, which is the exact situation this card is being written about.

THREE FILES, AND THE LIST IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED. run.sh, responder.sh and digest.sh are the deployed copies. The .mjs files beside them are read from a worktree at origin/main and cannot drift, so comparing them would produce a permanent false negative. Take the list from install.sh itself rather than writing a fourth copy of it: AUT-16 removed three copies of a path list for this reason and a new hardcoded list here re-creates the same defect in a smaller place.

COMPARE BYTES, NOT MTIMES. A file copied by install.sh has a new mtime and identical content, and a file edited and copied has both, so mtime answers a different question than the one being asked.

THE FIXTURE ROOT IS BUILT AND TORN DOWN BY THE TEST. No test writes anywhere under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin or /Users/ivan/rc-poc-logs, and no test reads /Users/ivan/rc-secrets. NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED.

AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-113, run 20260904-040001, from docs/reports/2026-09-04-executor-aut-16-board-set.md section 4 finding 3.

THE FINDING AS REPORTED WAS AN ACTION, AND AN ACTION IS NOT A CARD. The report says install.sh must be re-run because AUT-16 changed run.sh and digest.sh, and that the deployed copies are stale until somebody does it. Re-running it is one command and it will be done; a card whose acceptance is "somebody ran a command on a laptop" is not machine-checkable and DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 5 says plainly that such a thing is not a card. What IS a card is the reason nobody knew: nothing anywhere compares the deployed copy to the repository, so the staleness was found by an executor reading a rule rather than by anything running.

THE ONE-OFF RE-RUN IS NOT THIS CARD AND IS NOT BLOCKED BY IT. It is named in this run's report as an unowned action and it needs no owner decision: any terminal on this machine can run it. It is deliberately NOT an escalation, because the closed list in DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 6 is what goes to the owner and a command a terminal may run itself is not on it. This card is the class.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY test-install.sh, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY GREEN. That test installs into a fixture prefix and invokes what it installed, which proves the INSTALLER works. It says nothing about whether the installer was ever RUN on this machine after the last change, and its own comments say it deliberately never touches the real deployed directory. Those are two different properties and only the first has a check.

THE COST IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD. AUT-16 had to choose an argument shape whose OLD reading is the old behaviour, precisely because for one merge window a new shell script calls an old parser. That mitigation is correct and it is not a substitute for knowing which window you are in.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR.

TWO DEFAULTS APPLIED AND LOGGED, per CLAUDE.md 5.

  1. THE LIST IS DERIVED THROUGH A NEW FLAG ON install.sh RATHER THAN THROUGH A REGEX OVER ITS TEXT. The defaults say to take the list from install.sh itself rather than writing a fourth copy of it. Scraping the manifest rows out of the file would have worked until somebody reformatted them; a --manifest flag makes the derivation exact and prints absolute paths that are already resolved, so the caller does not re-resolve REPO_ROOT and POC_BIN_DIR and become the fourth copy that way instead. The flag exits before anything is created, checked or installed, and the test asserts that it creates nothing.
  2. THE 755 ROWS ARE SELECTED BY MODE, NOT BY NAME. The card names three files; selecting by mode gives those three today and gives a fourth script automatically.

A FINDING, REPORTED AND NOT BUILT. The three PLISTS are deployed copies too, they are in the same manifest, and they can drift in exactly the same way: an edited schedule that was never re-installed leaves the agent running at the old times with nothing to say so. They are the manifest's 644 rows and this check skips them, because the card names three files and CLAUDE.md 3 forbids the quiet extra. Extending the mode filter is a one-character change for whoever authors that card.

THE ESCALATION IS AN ESCALATION AND NOT A REFUSAL, per the defaults. The run continues on a drift. Refusing to start would turn a reporting gap into an outage the first time somebody edited a script and forgot the reinstall, which is the situation this card was written about.

AND IT APPLIES TO ITSELF. This card changes run.sh, so it is inert on the machine until scripts/poc/install.sh is re-run, which is the very condition it reports. The first scheduled run after the reinstall will compare clean; a run before it will report the drift this card just built, correctly.

cards.title: A scheduled run does not start a card it cannot finish and merge, because the required check costs between eighteen and twenty five minutes of a forty five minute cap.
cards.plain: The nightly sessions keep building work they then cannot publish, because the automatic checks eat half the time available. Each session should finish what the previous one left before starting anything new, and should not start something it has no time to publish.
cards.acceptance: `bash scripts/poc/test-harness-caps.sh` exits 0 WITH NEW CASES ADDED, or a sibling test file wired into the quality job BY NAME, proving ALL THREE halves, EACH PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current scripts/poc/run.sh with the failing output quoted in the pull request. The decision is lifted into ONE named function behind an EXTRACT fence the way the existing checkpoint fence is, and the test calls that function rather than a copy of it. (1) REFUSES: with a stub clock leaving fewer seconds than the configured estimate plus margin, the function returns NO card, exits with the documented refuse code, and writes a line naming the remaining seconds and the estimate. (2) PROCEEDS: with a stub clock leaving more, it returns the lowest-id eligible card, unchanged from today. (3) FINISHES BEFORE IT STARTS: given an open pull request on a branch this harness opened whose mergeStateStatus is BEHIND or CONFLICTING, that pull request is preferred over any new card whatever the remaining clock, and the test asserts WHICH of the two was chosen. PLUS `bash -n scripts/poc/run.sh` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE ESTIMATE IS A COMMITTED CONSTANT, NOT A LIVE QUERY. A run that has to call the GitHub API to decide whether it may start work has added a network failure mode to the decision that protects it from network failure. Seed it at 1500 seconds, the observed maximum of the last eight quality runs, with a 300 second margin, in ONE named variable beside the cap, so raising it is a one-line diff a reader can find.

THE CAP ITSELF IS NOT RAISED BY THIS CARD AND MAY NOT BE. Forty five minutes is the owner's number in CLAUDE.md section 13 and changing it is his decision, not a consequence of this one. A pull request that touches the cap is out of scope and gets split.

A RUN THAT REFUSES TO START A CARD IS NOT A SILENT RUN. CLAUDE.md section 13 says silence about an eligible card is a defect and never a normal outcome, and it names four reasons a run can ship nothing. This adds a fifth, "not enough clock left to merge it", and it is written to the log and appended as an escalation exactly like the other four. A run that quietly does nothing because the arithmetic said so is a worse outcome than the one being fixed.

BOUNDARY WITH AUT-9, RECORDED SO NEITHER IS HALF-DONE. AUT-9 makes the cap MEASURE the wall clock correctly and stops a dead lock being honoured forever. This card decides what to START given a clock that already measures correctly. AUT-9 owns the measurement, this owns the decision, and neither touches the other's code path. If AUT-9 has not shipped, this card reads the clock the way run.sh reads it today and does not fix it here.

BOUNDARY WITH AUT-18: that card makes every open pull request VISIBLE and merges nothing. Half (3) here is about PREFERRING an inherited branch, which is a selection decision, not a census. Neither is a substitute for the other and neither is blocked on the other.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED.

CLAUSE 1, REFUSES. A stubbed clock leaving 1000s against a requirement of 1800s

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-114, run 20260904-040001, from docs/reports/2026-09-04-executor-aut-16-board-set.md, whose own header records that the cap arrived with PR #186 open and its quality check still running.

THE ARITHMETIC, FROM COMMITTED RUN HISTORY AND NOT FROM AN IMPRESSION. The last measured quality runs took 24m48s, 18m09s and 19m43s, and one was cancelled at 21m. The cap is 45 minutes. So the required check costs between forty and fifty five percent of the entire budget, and two consequences follow with no judgement involved: a run can merge at most one pull request, and only if its head sha is pushed inside the first twenty minutes; and a run that builds a card from scratch cannot also merge it.

IT HAS NOW HAPPENED ON THREE CONSECUTIVE RUNS. Run 20260904-010000 built AUT-16 in full and ran out of clock with PR #186 open. Run 20260904-040001 merged it, having inherited finished work and pushed at minute two, and then could not start AUT-17 for the same reason and said so. The pattern reads in the reports as three runs each failing to finish, and it is not: it is the harness meeting an arithmetic constraint nobody wrote down.

THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR A LONGER CAP AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. Making the run longer moves the boundary; making the run KNOW where the boundary is removes the class. The executor of the 20260904-040001 run made this decision by hand and documented the reasoning, correctly. This card is that decision, written down once, so it is not re-derived at four in the morning by a session that may reason differently.

THE ONE THING IT COSTS, WHICH IS ALREADY VISIBLE: a card's report and its board edit sit unmerged for three hours, so the digest reads a board behind what has actually been built. That is a consequence of the constraint rather than a second defect, and it is why this card is high rather than medium.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR.

TWO DEFAULTS APPLIED AND LOGGED, per CLAUDE.md 5.

  1. THE ESTIMATE AND THE MARGIN ARE TWO NAMED CONSTANTS AND NOT ONE. The defaults say "in ONE named variable beside the cap, so raising it is a one-line diff a reader can find", and the antecedent is the estimate. They are kept separate because they answer different questions: the estimate is what the check costs and is MEASURED, the margin is what everything else costs and is CHOSEN. Folding them into a single 1800 would make raising one look like raising the other. Each is written once and the test asserts the count, so the one-line-diff property the default asks for holds for both.
  2. DIRTY IS ACCEPTED ALONGSIDE CONFLICTING. The card names BEHIND and CONFLICTING. The GitHub API returns DIRTY for a conflicting pull request while the documentation calls the field CONFLICTING, and this repository has hit that exact string this session: PR #214 reported mergeStateStatus DIRTY. Accepting only the documented name would have made clause 3 never fire against the real API. Both are accepted and each has its own case.

A THING THE CARD DID NOT ASK FOR AND THE TEST NEEDED. `extract` in test-harness-caps.sh is called as `$(extract ...)`, which runs it in a subshell, so its `exit 1` on a missing fence never reaches the caller: a deleted fence produced seventeen soft failures against an empty file instead of one hard one. test-pr-census.sh already carries that warning in its own words. Guarded at the new call site rather than by rewriting extract, which the three existing blocks use as it is.

THE BOUNDARY WITH AUT-9 HELD: this card reads the clock exactly the way run.sh reads it today, through date +%s and a deadline computed once, and changes no measurement. THE BOUNDARY WITH AUT-18 HELD: nothing here merges, censuses or closes anything; it selects.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-110, run 20260904-040001, from docs/reports/2026-09-04-executor-aut-16-board-set.md section 6.

WHAT THE REPORT SAYS AND WHY IT IS NOT MERELY A NOTE. "The eligible-card selector now returns phase 3 cards ahead of phase 2 ones." That is true, it was authorised in advance by AUT-16's own defaults and by R-071, and it was verified from the repository before this card was written: the phase 2 board offers AUT-17 as its first eligible card and the phase 3 board offers EXT-10, and the working set puts phase 3 first, so the next eligible card is EXT-10.

THE DEFECT IS THAT CLAUDE.md DOES NOT SAY SO. Section 2 reads "The board is the work queue", singular, and "Take the lowest-id eligible card", with a worked example of ids sorting lexically. A fresh session booting on the two lines in section 12 and reading section 2 computes AUT-17 and is wrong, and nothing anywhere is red. Section 12 states the standard this fails: a session needs exactly two lines and everything else is in this file, and a session that needs a third line is a defect in that file.

IT IS ALSO THE SHAPE THE PROJECT KEEPS PAYING FOR. R-071 found three components each holding a private copy of one board path; this is the same fact held in a fourth place, a human-readable one, which is the copy no test can see. The acceptance is written as an agreement check for exactly that reason: the document and the module must not be able to disagree silently.

IT IS ON THE PHASE 2 BOARD because the harness and doctrine cards live here, per R-041 and R-061.

cards.title: A check refuses a pull request that carries a card's code while that card's board status does not move in the same pull request.
cards.plain: The board is the only place the owner can see what is finished. Twice in one day work was merged while the board still said it had not been started, so the board undercounted what had been built and nobody could tell by looking. From now on the system itself refuses to accept the work unless the board is updated with it.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named check runs in quality on every pull request, NOT path-filtered, and REFUSES a pull request that modifies application code under a card id whose board status is identical at the merge base and at the head. PLUS: it asserts its INPUT COUNT against its MATCHED COUNT in three ledgers, so a path, a token or a card id that was silently skipped is a failure rather than a clean report. PLUS: a card id it cannot resolve to a card on any board is a FAILURE and never a pass. PLUS: it FAILS CLOSED on any pull request shape it cannot classify, including a path matching no classifier rule and code carried under no card id at all. PLUS COMMAND: a proof harness exits 0 with the failing half shown: a mutant pull request carrying code with no board flip turns the check RED, and a control on the same fixture harness proves it stays SILENT on a docs-only and on a report-only pull request. Every refusing case is paired with a control that must pass. PLUS: the check is replayed against the real merged history and the result is recorded in the report. cards.title: The scheduled harness checks open pull request depth BEFORE opening another one, and parks its output instead of opening a pull request above the threshold.
cards.plain: The system that works overnight opens its finished work for review four times a day whether or not the previous batch has been accepted yet. Work therefore piles up faster than it can be accepted, and clearing it takes hours instead of minutes. It should look at how much is already waiting and hold its work back rather than adding to the pile.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named test under scripts/poc/ exits 0 proving all four of: with open pull request count BELOW the threshold the harness opens its pull request exactly as it does today; with the count AT OR ABOVE the threshold it opens NONE and leaves the branch pushed with its work committed; the parked branch is NAMED in the run report and in the digest, with the count that caused the park; and a parked run on the NEXT scheduled tick opens the pull request when the count has fallen, without redoing the work. Each of the four must fail before the change and the results must be shown in the pull request. PLUS: the threshold is ONE NAMED CONSTANT in one file, read from one place, never duplicated per call site. PLUS: it FAILS OPEN INTO OPENING THE PULL REQUEST. If the open count cannot be obtained the harness opens as it does today, because an unopened pull request is invisible work and a queue that is one too long is merely slow. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE PRODUCER IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE CONSUMER. required_status_checks.strict is CORRECT and DOES NOT CHANGE. Under strict, a branch must be up to date with main before it merges, so a queue drains serially by construction and every pull request behind main at merge time costs a rebase and a full check run. That is the price of the property, the property is worth it, and the answer is to stop producing faster than the drain empties.

THE OBSERVED COST, WHICH IS WHY THIS CARD EXISTS: thirteen pull requests, merged one at a time, taking hours rather than minutes, with ELEVEN OF THIRTEEN behind main at merge time. Every one of those eleven needed main merged into it and a fresh check run before it could go.

PROPOSED THRESHOLD: THREE. Recommended rather than left open. Three is roughly one drain cycle at the observed check cost, so a run that finds three already open is a run whose output would land behind three rebases. The number belongs on the card so the first reader can argue with it; it is a constant and changing it is a one-line diff.

PARK, NEVER DISCARD. The work is committed and the branch is pushed. Only the pull request is withheld. A harness that threw away the work to avoid the queue would be trading a slow queue for lost work.

COUNT ONLY OPEN PULL REQUESTS, and count them from the API at the moment of the decision, never from a cached number. A closed or merged pull request costs the queue nothing.

IT IS NOT AUT-22 AND IT IS NOT AUT-18. AUT-22 stops a run STARTING a card it cannot finish and merge, which is about the cost of one card against the length of a run. AUT-18 makes a run REPORT the open pull requests it did not merge. This card is the third question: whether to add to the queue at all. All three can hold at once and none of them subsumes another.

recommended and as the owner ratified in the dispatch that ordered this build.

COMMAND: `bash scripts/poc/test-producer-gate.sh` exits 0, 29 assertions.

IT LIFTS THE REAL run.sh RATHER THAN RESTATING IT. The gate is fenced as
EXTRACT-BEGIN/EXTRACT-END producer-gate and the test extracts it verbatim, the

instead of passing on an empty extraction, which is asserted: run against the

EXTRACT block named 'producer-gate'`.

EACH CLAUSE FAILS FIRST, PROVEN BY A MUTANT OF THE POST-CHANGE FILE RATHER THAN
BY THE MISSING FENCE, because the missing fence fails all four at once and proves
only that the file changed. Five mutants, each disabling one clause, each red:
  clause 1, below the threshold opens : gate_decision forced to park always
      -> FAIL no pull request was created below the threshold (4 assertions red)
  clause 2, AT the threshold parks    : -ge changed to -gt, the off-by-one
      -> FAIL a pull request was created at the threshold (2 red)
  clause 3, named with its count      : open_count dropped from the park record
      -> FAIL the park record is missing the branch or the count
  clause 4, the next tick releases    : gate_release_parked short-circuited
      -> FAIL tick two did not open the parked branch (4 red)
  fail open                            : the unobtainable count made to park
      -> FAIL the gate did not fail open
A sixth mutant on the OTHER file, `if (parkedCount > 0)` forced false in
plain-digest.mjs, turns the digest half red: FAIL the plain digest does not
mention held work. So both files are load bearing and neither is decoration.

THE FOUR CLAUSES, EACH ASSERTED ON BOTH SIDES.
1. BELOW: exactly one create call, for the branch and title handed in, nothing
   parked. The boundary is asserted at threshold minus one in its own case.
2. AT OR ABOVE: zero create calls and one park record, asserted AT the threshold
   exactly and again well above it. `at or above` is the half a `>` would break,
   which is why the boundary has its own case rather than sharing one.
3. NAMED WITH THE COUNT: the run report line carries
   `PARKED branch=... open=5 threshold=3`; the spool record carries branch,
   count, threshold, run id and timestamp; the FULL digest renders a
   `PARKED, NOT OPENED` section from that spool; and the PLAIN digest says work
   is held with NO branch, NO number and NO path, asserted by running
   plain-digest's own assertPlain over the rendered text and requiring zero
   violations. It is also asserted to say NOTHING when nothing is parked.
4. THE NEXT TICK RELEASES: tick one parks with the queue at 4; tick two, with
   the queue at 0, opens one pull request for the branch tick one parked, names
   the release in the run report, and drops the record. WITHOUT REDOING THE WORK
   is an assertion and not a claim: `git`, `gh` and `gh_bounded` are shadowed as
   tripwires and the file recording their calls must stay EMPTY, so a release
   that committed, pushed or created a branch would go red. Two negative cases
   ride with it: with the queue still full the parked branch stays parked, and a
   parked branch that has vanished from the remote is dropped rather than
   retried forever.

ONE NAMED CONSTANT, ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY AND NOT ONLY BY READING.
`POC_PR_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` is assigned on exactly one line of the extracted block,
the test greps for that count; no comparison uses a bare literal; and the name is
read in five places. A second copy at another call site fails the test.

IT FAILS OPEN INTO OPENING, TWICE OVER. An empty answer from the counting seam
opens and says `FAILING OPEN` in the run report, and a NON-NUMERIC answer, which
is what a gh error printed to stdout looks like, reads as cannot-tell and opens
too rather than being compared as a word.

THE SPOOL IS OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN AND NOT A SHORTCUT.
A park withholds the pull request that CARRIES docs/poc/state.json, so a park
recorded in that file would ride on the branch that was parked and reach main
only once the park ended. The one fact that must survive a park is the one a
state field would seal inside it. It is /Users/ivan/rc-poc-logs/parked, the same
shape as ASK-01's spool.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY EXECUTOR FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH. NOT BUILT, AT HIS INSTRUCTION: the dispatch says author, do not build.

THE DISPATCH'S OWN WORDS ON THE PART THAT IS NOT THE DEFECT, RECORDED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT RE-OPEN IT: "required_status_checks.strict is correct and does not change." The strict setting is what makes a green check mean the branch was tested against the main it is about to join, and giving it up to drain a queue faster would trade a real guarantee for a scheduling convenience.

THE DEFECT IS THAT THE HARNESS OPENS PULL REQUESTS ON A FOUR-TIMES-DAILY SCHEDULE REGARDLESS OF QUEUE DEPTH, so the queue regrows faster than a serial drain empties it. Two independent rates with no feedback between them is the shape, and a producer gate is the smallest thing that couples them.

WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, AND IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the thirteen-pull-request figure and the eleven-of-thirteen behind-main figure are the owner's, from the drain he watched. They are recorded here as the motivating cost. Whoever builds this card should re-derive them from the merge history before quoting them anywhere the number matters, per the rule that a handed-over fact is re-derived rather than transcribed.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR, ON THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, WHICH RATIFIED THE THRESHOLD OF THREE AS SPECIFIED AND RESTATED THAT IT FAILS OPEN INTO OPENING THE PULL REQUEST.

THE MOTIVATING FIGURES WERE NOT RE-DERIVED, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The card's own note asks whoever builds it to re-derive the thirteen pull requests and the eleven-of-thirteen behind main from the merge history before quoting them anywhere the number matters. They are NOT quoted anywhere in this build: the threshold is three because the owner ratified three, not because of an arithmetic on those figures, and the gate's behaviour does not depend on them. They stay on the card as the owner's account of the drain he watched.

WHICH PULL REQUEST THE GATE ACTUALLY HOLDS, because the card says "its pull request" and the harness has only one of its own. run.sh opens exactly ONE pull request itself, the state pull request at step 5. The card pull requests and the triage pull request are opened by the EXECUTOR and TRIAGE model sessions inside the run, not by this shell, and a gate placed there would have to reach inside a model session. The gate therefore governs the state pull request, which is the one the harness produces on a four-times-daily schedule regardless of queue depth, which is the defect the card names.

A DEFAULT TAKEN AND RECORDED: WHICH DIGEST CARRIES THE BRANCH NAME. The card says the parked branch is named "in the run report and in the digest". There are two digests and CLAUDE.md 15 forbids branch names, pull request numbers and mechanics in the one the owner receives. The branch name and the count go to the run report and to the FULL digest under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-logs, which is written for POC-BUILDER and is where that vocabulary already lives. The plain digest carries the same fact in the owner's terms with none of that vocabulary in it, and the test asserts the absence by running assertPlain over the rendered text. Writing a branch name into the plain digest would have satisfied the card's sentence and broken section 15 of the file the card is written under.

A CONSEQUENCE OF THE RUN ORDER, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The digest is sent at step 4 and the park decision is taken at step 5, so a run never reports its OWN park. It reports every park still outstanding, and that repeats until the queue clears. The repetition is the property, not a defect: a held pull request that went quiet would look exactly like one that was never held. It is written into the header of readParked() so the next reader does not file it as a bug.

INSTALL.SH MUST BE RE-RUN, AND MERGING THIS DOES NOT DO IT. CLAUDE.md 15 says run.sh is a deployed copy under /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin and R-120 records that merging a change to it does not reach the scheduled runs. This card's change is inert on the machine until scripts/poc/install.sh is re-run. That is named in the pull request and in the session report.
